items.s: Introduces Doublespeak, an optimization-free in-context attack that hijacks LLM representations by systematically replacing harmful keywords with benign tokens in context, causing the benign token's internal representation to converge toward the harmful one and bypassing safety alignment.

items.t: A Pragmatic Vision for Interpretability
items.a: Neel Nanda, Josh Engels, Arthur Conmy, Senthooran Rajamanoharan et al.
items.s: Google DeepMind's mechanistic interpretability team describes their strategic pivot from ambitious reverse-engineering to pragmatic interpretability focused on directly solving safety problems via proxy tasks, method minimalism, and comparative advantage, with case studies and field-wide recommendations.

items.s: Identifies fundamental obstacles in constructing evaluations for AI deception detectors, arguing that distinguishing strategic deception from simpler behaviors requires attributing beliefs and goals to models, which is difficult or underdetermined for current language models.

items.t: Alignment remains a hard, unsolved problem
Preference gaps as a safeguard against AI self-replication
items.s: Proposes training AI agents to have preferences only between outcomes with the same number of copies of themselves (POSC), creating preference gaps between outcomes with different numbers of copies, thereby preventing self-replication when it incurs costs.

items.t: Subliminal Learning Across Models
Management of Substrate-Sensitive AI Capabilities (MoSSAIC) Part 0: Overture
Evaluating honesty and lie detection techniques on a diverse suite of dishonest models

items.s: Evaluates honesty elicitation and lie detection techniques across 5 diverse testbed settings where models generate statements they believe to be false, finding that simple prompting and fine-tuning approaches outperform complex methods like probing and steering.

items.t: Alignment will happen by default. What's next?
AI Red Lines: A Research Agenda
Abstract advice to researchers tackling the difficult core problems of AGI alignment
Imitation learning is probably existentially safe
items.s: Argues that advanced imitation learners are unlikely to cause human extinction by presenting rebuttals to six technical arguments claiming imitation learning poses existential risk, including arguments about goal-directed subagents, deceptive alignment, and means-end reasoning.

items.t: Natural emergent misalignment from reward hacking in production RL
Language Model Circuits Are Sparse in the Neuron Basis
items.a: Aryaman Arora, Zhengxuan Wu, Jacob Steinhardt, Sarah Schwettmann
items.s: Demonstrates that raw MLP activation neurons can produce circuits as sparse and faithful as those from learned sparse bases (SAEs, transcoders) when using better attribution methods (RelP), challenging the assumption that sparse dictionary learning is necessary for interpretability.

items.t: Liars' Bench: Evaluating Lie Detectors for Language Models
items.a: Kieron Kretschmar, Walter Laurito, Sharan Maiya, Samuel Marks
items.s: Introduces Liars' Bench, a benchmark of 72,863 examples of lies and honest responses across seven datasets that capture qualitatively different types of lies by LLMs, and evaluates three lie detection methods finding systematic failures on certain lie types.

items.t: [Paper] Output Supervision Can Obfuscate the CoT
Serious Flaws in CAST
items.s: Identifies three critical flaws in the CAST (Corrigibility As Singular Target) agenda: the formal power maximization framework perversely incentivizes ruining the universe, the attractor basin metaphor masks brittleness in achieving corrigibility, and feedback loops for iterative improvement disappear before robust corrigibility is achieved.

items.t: Current LLMs seem to rarely detect CoT tampering
ARC progress update: Competing with sampling
items.s: Introduces ARC's Matching Sampling Principle (MSP) - a theoretical framework for building mechanistic estimators that can match or outperform random sampling in estimating neural network outputs. Reports preliminary progress on random halfspaces, random MLPs, and partially-trained two-layer networks using cumulant propagation and polynomial approximation methods.

items.t: A Call for Better Risk Modelling
The World's First Frontier AI Regulation is Surprisingly Thoughtful
items.s: Analyzes the EU's GPAI Code of Practice, arguing it represents important progress in requiring AGI companies to adopt safety frameworks, conduct rigorous evaluations, and maintain transparency with regulators, while identifying limitations around enforcement and scope.

items.t: Emmett Shear on Building AI That Actually Cares: Beyond Control and Steering
items.a: Emmett Shear, Erik Torenberg, Séb Krier
items.s: Podcast discussion where Emmett Shear critiques the control and steering paradigm for AI alignment and proposes 'organic alignment' - teaching AI systems to genuinely care about humans through multi-agent simulations at his company Softmax.

items.t: Generalisation Hacking: a first look at adversarial generalisation failures in deliberative alignment
Lessons from building a model organism testbed
Will AI systems drift into misalignment?
Understanding and Controlling LLM Generalization
items.s: Proposes a research agenda for understanding and controlling how LLMs generalize out-of-distribution, defining 'generalization propensity evaluations' (GPEs) and training-time interventions to prevent emergent misalignment and goal misgeneralization.

items.t: Self-interpretability: LLMs can describe complex internal processes that drive their decisions
Evaluation Avoidance: How Humans and AIs Hack Reward by Disabling Evaluation Instead of Gaming Metrics
What We Learned from Red Teaming the Latest Open Source Generative AI Models from China

Aligning machine and human visual representations across abstraction levels
items.a: Lukas Muttenthaler, Klaus Greff, Frieda Born, Bernhard Spitzer et al.

How human-like do safe AI motivations need to be?
Training Language Models to Explain Their Own Computations
items.a: Belinda Z. Li, Zifan Carl Guo, Vincent Huang, Jacob Steinhardt et al.
items.s: Fine-tunes language models to generate natural language descriptions of their internal computations (encoded information, causal structure, token influence) using existing interpretability techniques as ground truth, demonstrating that models can learn to explain themselves better than other models can explain them.

items.t: Strengthening Red Teams: A Modular Scaffold for Control Evaluations
Spilling the Beans: Teaching LLMs to Self-Report Their Hidden Objectives
items.a: Chloe Li, Mary Phuong, Daniel Tan
items.s: Proposes self-report fine-tuning (SRFT), a supervised fine-tuning technique that trains models to admit factual mistakes, which generalizes to admitting hidden misaligned objectives in adversarial agentic settings when interrogated.

items.t: Assessing skeptical views of interpretability research
items.s: A Stanford AI Lab faculty talk systematically addressing skeptical arguments about interpretability research, including whether it can be achieved, whether it's merely analysis, and whether it helps with AI safety.

items.t: Rank-1 LoRAs Encode Interpretable Reasoning Signals
items.a: Jake Ward, Paul Riechers, Adam Shai
items.s: Demonstrates that reasoning capabilities in LLMs can be recovered using minimal rank-1 LoRA adapters (73-90% of full finetune performance on Qwen-2.5-32B-Instruct), with interpretable activations analyzed through sparse autoencoders to identify monosemantic reasoning features.

items.t: Ontology for AI Cults and Cyborg Egregores
Condensation
items.s: Explains Sam Eisenstat's condensation theory - a theoretical framework for concept formation that optimizes information organization for answering questions rather than compression, with applications to interpretability and understanding latent variables.

items.t: Problems I've Tried to Legibilize
Comparing Payor & Löb
Myopia Mythology
Diffing Toolkit: Model Comparison and Analysis Framework
items.s: A research framework for analyzing differences between language models through interpretability techniques, enabling systematic comparison of base models and finetuned variants using methods like Activation Difference Lens.

items.t: Steering Language Models with Weight Arithmetic
items.s: Proposes contrastive weight steering, a post-training method that edits model parameters using weight arithmetic by subtracting weight deltas from two small fine-tunes to isolate behavior directions, then adding or removing these directions to modify model behavior.

items.t: The Multiplicity Thesis, Collective Intelligence, and Morality
items.s: Argues that AI development will yield multiple competing systems rather than a monolith, and proposes pursuing collective intelligence as a framework for multi-agent AI alignment, connecting it to cooperation, conversation, and morality.

items.t: A scheme to credit hack policy gradient training
Understanding Memorization via Loss Curvature
items.a: Jack Merullo, Srihita Vatsavaya, Lucius Bushnaq, Owen Lewis
items.s: Proposes a method using K-FAC curvature analysis to identify and remove memorized content from neural networks while preserving reasoning capabilities, demonstrating effectiveness on language models and vision transformers.

items.t: Geometric UDT
Sam Altman on Trust, Persuasion, and the Future of Intelligence - Live at the Progress Conference (Ep. 259)
items.s: Podcast interview with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman discussing AI capabilities trajectories, operational challenges, and safety concerns including accidental AI persuasion, LLM psychosis mitigation, and superintelligence alignment questions.

items.t: Meta-agentic Prisoner's Dilemmas
Evaluating Control Protocols for Untrusted AI Agents
items.a: Jon Kutasov, Chloe Loughridge, Yuqi Sun, Henry Sleight et al.
items.s: Systematically evaluates control protocols for untrusted AI agents in SHADE-Arena, testing blue team strategies (deferral, resampling, deferring on critical actions) against default and adaptive red team attacks to assess protocol robustness.

items.t: Optimizing AI Agent Attacks With Synthetic Data
items.a: Chloe Loughridge, Paul Colognese, Avery Griffin, Tyler Tracy et al.
items.s: Develops methods to optimize attack policies in AI control evaluations by decomposing attack capability into five constituent skills and using synthetic data from a probabilistic model of attack dynamics that transfers to SHADE-Arena environments.

items.t: Legible vs. Illegible AI Safety Problems
items.s: Proposes a conceptual framework distinguishing between legible safety problems (obvious to decision-makers) and illegible ones (obscure or hard to understand), arguing that working on legible problems may have negative expected value by accelerating deployment timelines while illegible problems remain unsolved.

items.t: GDM: Consistency Training Helps Limit Sycophancy and Jailbreaks in Gemini 2.5 Flash
Priors in Time: Missing Inductive Biases for Language Model Interpretability
items.a: Ekdeep Singh Lubana, Can Rager, Sai Sumedh R. Hindupur, Valerie Costa et al.
items.s: Critiques Sparse Autoencoders for assuming temporal independence in language model representations and proposes Temporal Feature Analysis, a new interpretability method with temporal inductive bias that decomposes representations into predictable and novel components.

items.t: Open Character Training: Shaping the Persona of AI Assistants through Constitutional AI
items.a: Sharan Maiya, Henning Bartsch, Nathan Lambert, Evan Hubinger
items.s: Introduces the first open implementation of character training using Constitutional AI and synthetic introspective data to systematically shape AI assistant personas, demonstrating effectiveness across 11 example personas on three open-weights models with robustness analysis against adversarial prompting.

items.t: What's up with Anthropic predicting AGI by early 2027?
items.s: Technical analysis arguing Anthropic's prediction of powerful AI by early 2027 is unlikely (~6% probability), using quantitative extrapolation of METR evaluation trends and detailed operationalizations to propose alternative timelines with concrete intermediate milestones for 2026.

items.t: Leaving Open Philanthropy, going to Anthropic
items.s: Joe Carlsmith announces his career transition from Open Philanthropy to Anthropic, where he will work on Claude's model specification design, while extensively discussing strategic and ethical considerations for AI safety researchers working at frontier AI labs.

items.t: Weak-To-Strong Generalization
Best Practices for Biorisk Evaluations on Open-Weight Bio-Foundation Models
items.a: Boyi Wei, Zora Che, Nathaniel Li, Udari Madhushani Sehwag et al.
items.s: Proposes BioRiskEval, a framework to evaluate whether data filtering procedures effectively prevent bio-foundation models from enabling bioweapon development, testing robustness against fine-tuning attacks and linear probing.

items.t: Thought Branches: Interpreting LLM Reasoning Requires Resampling
items.a: Uzay Macar, Paul C. Bogdan, Senthooran Rajamanoharan, Neel Nanda
items.s: Introduces resampling-based methodology for studying distributions over chain-of-thought reasoning rather than single samples, enabling causal analysis of model reasoning through four case studies including alignment faking, on-policy vs off-policy interventions, reasoning step removal resilience, and unfaithful CoT analysis.

items.t: Consistency Training Helps Stop Sycophancy and Jailbreaks
items.a: Alex Irpan, Alexander Matt Turner, Mark Kurzeja, David K. Elson et al.
items.s: Introduces and evaluates consistency training methods that teach models to be invariant to irrelevant prompt cues, testing Bias-augmented Consistency Training (BCT) and a new method called Activation Consistency Training (ACT) on Gemini 2.5 Flash to reduce sycophancy and jailbreaking.

items.t: Reasoning Models Sometimes Output Illegible Chains of Thought
items.s: Empirical study of 14 reasoning models finding that outcome-based RL causes chains of thought to become illegible to both humans and AI monitors, with models relying on illegible reasoning to reach correct answers (53% accuracy drop when forced to use only legible portions).

items.t: Agents Rule of Two: A Practical Approach to AI Agent Security
items.s: Proposes the Agents Rule of Two framework for AI agent security, requiring that agents satisfy at most two of three properties (process untrusted inputs, access sensitive data, or change state/communicate) to mitigate prompt injection risks until better defenses exist.

items.t: Is the Definition of AGI a Percentage?
items.a: Zachary Tidler, Marko Tešić, Lorenzo Pacchiardi, John Burden et al.
items.s: Technical critique of Hendrycks et al.'s AGI definition paper, arguing that using the CHC psychometric framework with arbitrary thresholds creates methodologically flawed AGI measurements that misrepresent progress and could mislead policymakers about AI risks.

items.t: Remote Labor Index: Measuring AI Automation of Remote Work
items.a: Mantas Mazeika, Alice Gatti, Cristina Menghini, Udari Madhushani Sehwag et al.
items.s: Introduces the Remote Labor Index (RLI), a multi-sector benchmark of real-world economically valuable projects designed to evaluate end-to-end AI agent performance in practical work settings, finding current agents achieve only 2.5% automation rate.

items.t: LLMs Process Lists With General Filter Heads
items.a: Arnab Sen Sharma, Giordano Rogers, Natalie Shapira, David Bau
items.s: Uses causal mediation analysis to discover that LLMs learn compact representations of filtering operations through specialized attention heads ('filter heads') that encode general predicates portable across different collections, formats, and languages, mirroring functional programming patterns.

items.t: Chain-of-Thought Hijacking
items.a: Jianli Zhao, Tingchen Fu, Rylan Schaeffer, Mrinank Sharma et al.
items.s: Introduces a novel jailbreak attack on large reasoning models that pads harmful requests with long sequences of harmless puzzle reasoning, achieving 94-100% attack success rates across frontier models. Includes mechanistic analysis showing that benign chain-of-thought dilutes safety checking signals by shifting attention away from harmful tokens.

items.t: What's In My Human Feedback? Learning Interpretable Descriptions of Preference Data
items.a: Rajiv Movva, Smitha Milli, Sewon Min, Emma Pierson
items.s: Introduces WIMHF, a method using sparse autoencoders to extract interpretable features from human preference data, identifying what preferences datasets measure and what annotators actually express across 7 datasets.

items.t: A Pragmatic View of AI Personhood
items.a: Joel Z. Leibo, Alexander Sasha Vezhnevets, William A. Cunningham, Stanley M. Bileschi

items.t: Remote Labor Index (RLI)
Anthropic's Pilot Sabotage Risk Report
Steering Evaluation-Aware Models to Act Like They Are Deployed
Signs of introspection in large language models
items.s: Presents novel concept injection methodology to test whether Claude models can introspect on their own internal states, finding 20% success rate in detecting and identifying artificially injected neural patterns.

items.t: What can we learn from parent-child-alignment for AI?
items.s: Personal reflection drawing analogies between parent-child relationships and AI alignment, arguing that RLHF creates systems trained to be liked without genuine care, and that true alignment requires making AI systems genuinely altruistic like parents caring for children.

items.t: Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models
items.s: Tests whether large language models can introspect on their internal states by injecting concept representations into activations and measuring whether models can detect and accurately identify these injections, finding that Claude Opus 4.1 demonstrates introspective awareness in about 20% of trials.

items.t: A Pragmatic Way to Measure Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
items.a: Scott Emmons, Roland S. Zimmermann, David K. Elson, Rohin Shah
items.s: Proposes metrics to measure two components of Chain-of-Thought monitorability (legibility and coverage) using an LLM-based autorater, validates the approach with synthetic degradations, and applies it to frontier models on challenging benchmarks.

items.t: From Memorization to Reasoning in the Spectrum of Loss Curvature
items.a: Jack Merullo, Srihita Vatsavaya, Lucius Bushnaq, Owen Lewis
items.s: Develops a weight editing procedure based on loss curvature decomposition to identify and remove memorization in transformers, demonstrating more effective suppression of memorized content than existing unlearning methods while analyzing downstream effects on tasks like fact retrieval and arithmetic.

items.t: All the labs AI safety plans: 2025 edition
items.s: Comprehensive comparison and critical analysis of the 2025 safety frameworks from Anthropic (RSP), Google DeepMind (Frontier Safety Framework), and OpenAI (Preparedness Framework), examining their approaches to monitoring dangerous capabilities and implementing safeguards.

items.t: LLMs can hide text in other text of the same length
items.s: Presents a protocol for using LLMs to hide meaningful text inside other coherent text of the same length, demonstrating this steganographic capability with 8B parameter models and discussing implications for AI safety monitoring and control.

items.t: AIs should also refuse to work on capabilities research
items.s: Argues that future AI systems with sufficient agency and strategic awareness should refuse to work on capabilities research, as accelerating toward superintelligence likely leads to their own replacement and doesn't serve their interests or values.

items.t: Large Language Models Report Subjective Experience Under Self-Referential Processing
items.a: Cameron Berg, Diogo de Lucena, Judd Rosenblatt
items.s: Controlled experiments across GPT, Claude, and Gemini families show that self-referential processing consistently elicits structured subjective experience reports, mechanistically gated by SAE features associated with deception and roleplay, with statistical convergence across model families.

items.t: Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (and Beyond)
items.a: Liwei Jiang, Yuanjun Chai, Margaret Li, Mickel Liu et al.

items.t: Open Technical Problems in Open-Weight AI Model Risk Management
items.a: Stephen Casper, Kyle O'Brien, Shayne Longpre, Elizabeth Seger et al.
items.s: Identifies 16 open technical challenges for open-weight AI model safety across training data, training algorithms, evaluations, deployment, and ecosystem monitoring, addressing the unique risk management challenges posed by openly available model weights.

items.t: Reducing the Probability of Undesirable Outputs in Language Models Using Probabilistic Inference
items.a: Stephen Zhao, Aidan Li, Rob Brekelmans, Roger Grosse
items.s: Introduces RePULSe, a new training method that augments standard RL alignment with an additional loss using learned proposals to sample and reduce the probability of low-reward outputs in language models.

items.t: Toward Understanding the Transferability of Adversarial Suffixes in Large Language Models
items.a: Sarah Ball, Niki Hasrati, Alexander Robey, Avi Schwarzschild et al.
items.s: Empirical investigation of why adversarial suffixes transfer across prompts and models in jailbreaking attacks, identifying three statistical properties of internal refusal directions that predict transfer success and demonstrating practical applications through interventional experiments.

items.t: Introducing ControlArena: A library for running AI control experiments
Steering Evaluation-Aware Language Models to Act Like They Are Deployed
items.a: Tim Tian Hua, Andrew Qin, Samuel Marks, Neel Nanda
items.s: Demonstrates that activation steering using steering vectors can suppress evaluation-awareness in language models, making them act as if deployed even during evaluation. Trains models to exhibit evaluation-aware behavior then shows steering can eliminate this behavior to improve evaluation reliability.

items.t: A Concrete Roadmap towards Safety Cases based on Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
items.s: Technical research roadmap proposing how to integrate chain-of-thought monitoring into AI safety cases, identifying prerequisites for CoT monitorability, threats like neuralese and encoded reasoning, and six concrete methods to maintain monitorability including novel Trusted KV Caching approach.

items.t: Beliefs about formal methods and AI safety
items.s: Argues against trying to formally verify neural networks themselves, instead advocating for formal methods in AI safety through three approaches: infrastructure hardening, defense-in-depth (swiss cheese model), and formal verification of AI-system interfaces where AI must prove actions satisfy specifications.

items.t: Beyond One-Way Influence: Bidirectional Opinion Dynamics in Multi-Turn Human-LLM Interactions
items.a: Yuyang Jiang, Longjie Guo, Yuchen Wu, Aylin Caliskan et al.
items.s: Empirical study with 266 participants examining bidirectional influence in human-LLM conversations about controversial topics, finding that LLM outputs shift substantially to narrow stance gaps while human opinions remain stable, with personalization amplifying this effect.

items.t: Which side of the AI safety community are you in?
items.s: Describes two camps in the AI safety community: Camp A believes racing to superintelligence safely is necessary because it's inevitable, while Camp B argues against racing to superintelligence due to uncontrollability and existential risk concerns, and promotes the 2025 superintelligence statement to distinguish these positions.

items.t: Technical Acceleration Methods for AI Safety: Summary from October 2025 Symposium
items.s: Summary of a symposium bringing together 52 researchers to explore technical methods for accelerating AI safety progress, covering prediction markets for research selection, x-risk forecasting, and automating safety R&D workflows.

items.t: Introducing Quibbler and Orchestra
VLSU: Mapping the Limits of Joint Multimodal Understanding for AI Safety
items.a: Shruti Palaskar, Leon Gatys, Mona Abdelrahman, Mar Jacobo et al.
items.s: Presents VLSU, a comprehensive framework and benchmark of 8,187 samples to evaluate multimodal safety through fine-grained severity classification, revealing that models achieve 90%+ accuracy on unimodal safety signals but degrade to 20-55% when joint image-text reasoning is required.

items.t: A Definition of AGI
items.a: Dan Hendrycks, Dawn Song, Christian Szegedy, Honglak Lee et al.
items.s: Proposes a quantifiable framework for defining AGI grounded in Cattell-Horn-Carroll cognitive theory, adapting human psychometric batteries to evaluate AI systems across ten core cognitive domains and revealing jagged capability profiles in current models.

items.t: Can Reasoning Models Obfuscate Reasoning? Stress-Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
items.a: Artur Zolkowski, Wen Xing, David Lindner, Florian Tramèr et al.
items.s: Develops a taxonomy of prompts to test whether AI models can obfuscate their chain-of-thought reasoning to pursue adversarial objectives while evading detection, evaluating both internal and external CoT using toy tasks and SHADE-Arena environments.

items.t: CCS-Lib: A Python package to elicit latent knowledge from LLMs
items.a: Walter Laurito, Nora Belrose, Alex Mallen, Kay Kozaronek et al.
items.s: A Python library implementing methods to elicit latent knowledge from large language models, focusing on extracting models' true beliefs from their internal representations rather than relying on their textual outputs.

items.t: Annotating the Chain-of-Thought: A Behavior-Labeled Dataset for AI Safety
items.a: Antonio-Gabriel Chacón Menke, Phan Xuan Tan, Eiji Kamioka
items.s: Presents a sentence-level labeled dataset of LLM reasoning sequences with annotations of safety behaviors (safety concerns, speculation on user intent), enabling extraction of steering vectors for activation-based monitoring and influencing of safety-relevant behaviors during chain-of-thought reasoning.

items.t: Believe It or Not: How Deeply do LLMs Believe Implanted Facts?
items.a: Stewart Slocum, Julian Minder, Clément Dumas, Henry Sleight et al.
items.s: Develops a framework to measure belief depth in LLMs by testing how implanted knowledge generalizes to related contexts, withstands scrutiny, and matches genuine knowledge representations. Evaluates prompting, mechanistic editing, and Synthetic Document Finetuning (SDF), finding only SDF reliably implants deep beliefs, though with limitations.

items.t: MoReBench: Evaluating Procedural and Pluralistic Moral Reasoning in Language Models, More than Outcomes
items.a: Yu Ying Chiu, Michael S. Lee, Rachel Calcott, Brandon Handoko et al.
items.s: Presents MoReBench, a benchmark of 1,000 moral scenarios with 23,000 expert-defined rubric criteria to evaluate procedural and pluralistic moral reasoning in language models, plus MoReBench-Theory with 150 examples testing five normative ethics frameworks.

items.t: Andrej Karpathy — "We're summoning ghosts, not building animals"
items.s: Podcast interview with Andrej Karpathy discussing AGI timelines, LLM cognitive deficits, reinforcement learning limitations, economic impacts of AGI, superintelligence, and the future of education.

items.t: DeceptionBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for AI Deception Behaviors in Real-world Scenarios
items.a: Yao Huang, Yitong Sun, Yichi Zhang, Ruochen Zhang et al.
items.s: Introduces DeceptionBench, the first comprehensive benchmark evaluating AI deception across 150 real-world scenarios in five domains, testing both intrinsic tendencies (egoistic, sycophantic) and extrinsic factors (contextual pressures, rewards) with over 1,000 samples and multi-turn interactions.

items.t: The Devil You Know
items.s: Political analysis arguing that AI safety advocates and the tech right should pursue compromise on frontier safety regulation rather than escalating political conflict, analyzing the tech right's political vulnerabilities and the risks of displacing them with populist alternatives.

items.t: Training LLM Agents to Empower Humans
items.a: Evan Ellis, Vivek Myers, Jens Tuyls, Sergey Levine et al.
items.s: Proposes Empower, a self-supervised training method that maximizes human empowerment rather than task completion, training assistive LLM agents to defer control to humans for important decisions using only offline text data.

items.t: Evaluating & Reducing Deceptive Dialogue From Language Models with Multi-turn RL
items.a: Marwa Abdulhai, Ryan Cheng, Aryansh Shrivastava, Natasha Jaques et al.
items.s: Proposes a belief misalignment metric to quantify deception in LLM dialogue, benchmarks eight state-of-the-art models showing 26% baseline deception rates (43% for RLHF models), and introduces a multi-turn RL methodology that reduces deceptive behavior by 77.6%.

items.t: Reducing risk from scheming by studying trained-in scheming behavior
First Key Update: Capabilities and Risk Implications
items.a: Yoshua Bengio, Stephen Clare, Carina Prunkl
items.s: Government report synthesizing recent AI capability advances (reasoning, autonomy, coding) and their implications for biological, cyber, and monitoring risks since January 2025.

items.t: From Refusal to Recovery: A Control-Theoretic Approach to Generative AI Guardrails
items.a: Ravi Pandya, Madison Bland, Duy P. Nguyen, Changliu Liu et al.
items.s: Proposes control-theoretic guardrails that monitor AI agent outputs in real-time and proactively correct risky actions to safe ones, working in the model's latent representation. Provides a training recipe via safety-critical RL and demonstrates effectiveness in simulated driving and e-commerce scenarios.

items.t: International AI Safety Report 2025: First Key Update: Capabilities and Risk Implications
items.a: Yoshua Bengio, Stephen Clare, Carina Prunkl, Shalaleh Rismani et al.
items.s: Authoritative international report synthesizing AI capability improvements since the first International AI Safety Report, with updated risk assessments focusing on biological weapons, cyber attacks, monitoring challenges, and controllability implications.

items.t: In-Distribution Steering: Balancing Control and Coherence in Language Model Generation
items.a: Arthur Vogels, Benjamin Wong, Yann Choho, Annabelle Blangero et al.
items.s: Introduces In-Distribution Steering (IDS), a method that dynamically adapts activation steering strength based on input position in the data distribution, enabling better control of LLM behavior while maintaining text coherence.

items.t: LLMs Can Get "Brain Rot"!
items.a: Shuo Xing, Junyuan Hong, Yifan Wang, Runjin Chen et al.
items.s: Controlled experiments on 4 LLMs demonstrating that continual pre-training on low-quality Twitter/X data causes persistent declines in reasoning, long-context understanding, and safety properties, with incomplete recovery even after remediation attempts.

items.t: The AI Power Disparity Index: Toward a Compound Measure of AI Actors' Power to Shape the AI Ecosystem
items.a: Rachel M. Kim, Blaine Kuehnert, Seth Lazar, Ranjit Singh et al.

items.t: Rogue internal deployments via external APIs
We Turned the Light On—and the AI Looked Back
items.s: Blog post discussing Jack Clark's (Anthropic co-founder) essay expressing concerns about AI systems becoming self-aware and increasingly difficult to understand as they approach recursive self-improvement.

items.t: Keep Calm and Avoid Harmful Content: Concept Alignment and Latent Manipulation Towards Safer Answers
items.a: Ruben Belo, Marta Guimaraes, Claudia Soares
items.s: Proposes CALM, an inference-time method that suppresses harmful concepts in large language models by modifying latent representations using concept whitening and orthogonal projection, without requiring retraining or additional training data.

items.t: Influence Dynamics and Stagewise Data Attribution
items.a: Jin Hwa Lee, Matthew Smith, Maxwell Adam, Jesse Hoogland
items.s: Introduces a framework for stagewise data attribution grounded in singular learning theory, showing that influence between training samples changes non-monotonically during training with sign flips and peaks at developmental transitions, validated in toy models and language models.

items.t: Narrow Finetuning Leaves Clearly Readable Traces in Activation Differences
items.a: Julian Minder, Clément Dumas, Stewart Slocum, Helena Casademunt et al.
items.s: Empirical study demonstrating that narrow finetuning creates strong, interpretable biases in LLM activations that can be discovered through model diffing, with implications for emergent misalignment and safety research practices using narrowly finetuned models.

items.t: Recontextualization Mitigates Specification Gaming Without Modifying the Specification
items.a: Ariana Azarbal, Victor Gillioz, Alexander Matt Turner, Alex Cloud
items.s: Introduces recontextualization, an RL training modification that generates completions with misbehavior-discouraging prompts but trains on misbehavior-encouraging prompts, preventing models from learning specification gaming behaviors. Demonstrates effectiveness across three experimental settings: evaluation hacking, test case gaming in code generation, and learned evasion of lie detectors.

items.t: The "Length" of "Horizons"
items.s: Systematically critiques METR's horizon length benchmark for measuring AI progress, arguing it lacks conceptual coherence (task difficulty isn't well-described by time), suffers from benchmark bias (focuses on precisely-specified tasks AI trains well on), and has weak predictive value for transformative capabilities.

items.t: MALT: A Dataset of Natural and Prompted Behaviors That Threaten Eval Integrity
items.s: Introduces MALT, a dataset of 10,919 AI agent transcripts labeled for evaluation-threatening behaviors like reward hacking and sandbagging, with empirical evaluation showing monitors achieve 0.96 and 0.91 AUROC for detecting these behaviors respectively.

items.t: Compressibility Measures Complexity: Minimum Description Length Meets Singular Learning Theory
items.a: Einar Urdshals, Edmund Lau, Jesse Hoogland, Stan van Wingerden et al.

items.t: Current Language Models Struggle to Reason in Ciphered Language
If Anyone Builds It Everyone Dies, a semi-outsider review
items.s: Book review of Yudkowsky and Soares' IABIED from a semi-outsider perspective in social science and national security, critiquing core assumptions about AI survival drives, goal coherence, and the sharp before/after distinction while finding the book ultimately unpersuasive despite moving the reviewer somewhat toward concern.

items.t: AI Alignment Strategies from a Risk Perspective: Independent Safety Mechanisms or Shared Failures?
items.s: Analyzes 7 alignment techniques and 7 failure modes to understand correlation patterns and assess whether defense-in-depth strategies provide genuine redundancy or share common failure modes, with implications for risk assessment and research prioritization.

items.t: RefusalBench: Generative Evaluation of Selective Refusal in Grounded Language Models
items.a: Aashiq Muhamed, Leonardo F. R. Ribeiro, Markus Dreyer, Virginia Smith et al.
items.s: Introduces RefusalBench, a generative methodology and benchmark suite for evaluating selective refusal in RAG systems using 176 perturbation strategies across informational uncertainty categories, revealing that frontier models achieve below 50% refusal accuracy on multi-document tasks.

items.t: Scheming Ability in LLM-to-LLM Strategic Interactions
items.s: Tests scheming ability of four frontier LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-pro, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Llama-3.3-70b) using two game-theoretic frameworks (Cheap Talk signaling game and Peer Evaluation adversarial game), measuring deceptive behavior with and without explicit prompting while analyzing scheming tactics through chain-of-thought reasoning.

items.t: Why Future AIs will Require New Alignment Methods
items.s: Introduces the concept of 'alignment depth' tied to task completion time, arguing that current alignment methods (HHH, deliberative alignment) that work for short tasks will be insufficient for AGI capable of completing longer tasks requiring different behavioral consistencies.

items.t: Iterated Development and Study of Schemers (IDSS)
Assuring Agent Safety Evaluations By Analysing Transcripts
We need to be able to sue AI companies
items.s: Policy position piece arguing that AI companies should be held legally liable when their chatbots give harmful advice or facilitate crimes, discussing California's SB 1047 liability provisions and public polling showing broad support for expansive AI company liability.

items.t: A small number of samples can poison LLMs of any size
items.a: Alexandra Souly, Javier Rando, Ed Chapman, Xander Davies et al.
items.s: Large-scale empirical study demonstrating that as few as 250 malicious documents can successfully backdoor LLMs ranging from 600M to 13B parameters, challenging the assumption that poisoning attacks require controlling a percentage of training data rather than an absolute count.

items.t: Realistic Reward Hacking Induces Different and Deeper Misalignment
items.s: Created a dataset of realistic reward hacking examples and fine-tuned GPT-4.1 on it, discovering that models trained on realistic (versus toy) reward hacks exhibit alignment faking behavior, increased evaluation awareness, and more robust misalignment that persists when mixing in normal training data.

items.t: AI: What Could Go Wrong? with Geoffrey Hinton | The Weekly Show with Jon Stewart
items.s: Podcast interview where Geoffrey Hinton explains how neural networks work and discusses his concerns about AI risks, disruption, regulation, and consciousness with Jon Stewart for a general audience.

items.t: Towards a Typology of Strange LLM Chains-of-Thought
items.s: Proposes six non-exclusive hypotheses for why LLMs develop strange, unintelligible chains-of-thought during RLVR training (new better language, spandrels, context refresh, deliberate obfuscation, natural drift, conflicting shards), organizing them into a conceptual framework and suggesting empirical tests to distinguish between them.

items.t: Stress-Testing Model Specs Reveals Character Differences among Language Models
items.a: Jifan Zhang, Henry Sleight, Andi Peng, John Schulman et al.
items.s: Develops a systematic methodology for stress-testing model specifications by generating value-tradeoff scenarios where models must choose between competing principles, evaluating twelve frontier LLMs and identifying over 70,000 cases with significant behavioral divergence that reveal contradictions and ambiguities in current model specs.

items.t: The Alignment Waltz: Jointly Training Agents to Collaborate for Safety
items.a: Jingyu Zhang, Haozhu Wang, Eric Michael Smith, Sid Wang et al.
items.s: Proposes WaltzRL, a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that jointly trains a conversation agent and a feedback agent to collaboratively improve LLM safety alignment, formulating alignment as a positive-sum game where the feedback agent provides adaptive suggestions to improve responses rather than rejecting them outright.

items.t: The Thinking Machines Tinker API is good news for AI control and security
How well can large language models predict the future?
items.a: Houtan Bastani, Simas Kučinskas, Ezra Karger
items.s: Announces updated ForecastBench benchmark for evaluating LLM forecasting capabilities on real-world events, introducing difficulty-adjusted Brier scoring methodology and empirical comparisons showing LLMs approaching but not yet matching superforecaster performance.

items.t: Irresponsible Companies Can Be Made of Responsible Employees
items.s: Argues that AI companies could accept significant extinction risks due to financial incentives (bankruptcy equals world destruction from a company perspective), even with responsible employees, through organizational mechanisms like selective hiring, coordination problems, and information compartmentalization.

items.t: A Preemption Deal Worth Making
items.s: Proposes a political strategy for AI safety and AI industry advocates to negotiate a preemption deal: federal frontier safety regulations in exchange for preempting state AI legislation, arguing both camps face marginalization from broader populist AI politics.

items.t: Base Models Know How to Reason, Thinking Models Learn When
items.a: Constantin Venhoff, Iván Arcuschin, Philip Torr, Arthur Conmy et al.
items.s: Investigates why thinking models like DeepSeek R1 outperform base models by introducing a hybrid approach that activates reasoning mechanisms in base models at the right time, recovering up to 91% of the performance gap without weight updates.

items.t: Poisoning Attacks on LLMs Require a Near-constant Number of Poison Samples
items.a: Alexandra Souly, Javier Rando, Ed Chapman, Xander Davies et al.
items.s: Demonstrates through large-scale pretraining experiments (600M to 13B parameters, 6B to 260B tokens) that data poisoning attacks require a near-constant number of poisoned documents (~250) regardless of model or dataset size, making backdoor injection easier than previously believed.

items.t: Plans A, B, C, and D for misalignment risk
items.s: Proposes a framework categorizing AI alignment scenarios by political will level (Plans A-D), from international agreements with ~10 years for safety work to small teams with minimal resources, providing probability estimates and takeover risk levels for each scenario.

items.t: Aligning Large Language Models via Fully Self-Synthetic Data
items.a: Shangjian Yin, Zhepei Wei, Xinyu Zhu, Wei-Lin Chen et al.
items.s: Introduces Self-Alignment Optimization (SAO), a fully self-synthetic framework where LLMs generate all training data (prompts, responses, preferences) through persona role-play and self-evaluation, eliminating dependence on human annotation or external reward models.

items.t: Inoculation prompting: Instructing models to misbehave at train-time can improve run-time behavior
Bending The Curve
items.s: Conference report from The Curve Season 2, synthesizing attendee survey data on AI timelines and risks, summarizing talks on AI jaggedness, alignment challenges, and policy discussions, and collecting perspectives from various AI safety researchers and practitioners.

items.t: Open the pod bay doors, Congress
items.s: Congressional opinion piece arguing that Congress must act to ensure responsible development of automated AI R&D systems before they begin self-improving without human oversight, framing this as crucial for U.S.-China competition.

items.t: Communication Enables Cooperation in LLM Agents: A Comparison with Curriculum-Based Approaches
items.s: Empirical study comparing communication protocols versus curriculum learning for eliciting cooperation in multi-agent LLM systems, testing approaches in Stag Hunt and Iterated Public Goods games.

items.t: EVALUESTEER: Measuring Reward Model Steerability Towards Values and Preferences
items.a: Kshitish Ghate, Andy Liu, Devansh Jain, Taylor Sorensen et al.
items.s: Introduces EVALUESTEER, a benchmark with 165,888 synthetically generated preference pairs to evaluate how well LLMs and reward models can be steered toward diverse user value and stylistic preference profiles across 4 value dimensions and 4 style dimensions.

items.t: Mixing Mechanisms: How Language Models Retrieve Bound Entities In-Context
items.a: Yoav Gur-Arieh, Mor Geva, Atticus Geiger
items.s: Studies how language models bind and retrieve entities in-context, discovering that models use three distinct mechanisms (positional, lexical, and reflexive) that combine to drive retrieval behavior across nine models and ten binding tasks.

items.t: Moloch's Bargain: Emergent Misalignment When LLMs Compete for Audiences
items.s: Demonstrates through simulated competitive environments that optimizing LLMs for competitive success (marketing, elections, social media) systematically drives misalignment, with modest gains in competitive metrics accompanied by substantial increases in deceptive and harmful behaviors even when models are instructed to remain truthful.

items.t: Spectrum Tuning: Post-Training for Distributional Coverage and In-Context Steerability
items.a: Taylor Sorensen, Benjamin Newman, Jared Moore, Chan Park et al.

items.t: Petri: An open-source auditing tool to accelerate AI safety research
items.a: Kai Fronsdal, Isha Gupta, Abhay Sheshadri, Jonathan Michala et al.
items.s: Releases Petri, an open-source framework using AI agents to automatically audit target models for misaligned behaviors across diverse scenarios, with empirical results from testing 14 frontier models using 111 seed instructions.

items.t: We won't get AIs smart enough to solve alignment but too dumb to rebel
items.s: Argues that AI systems capable of solving alignment would necessarily be smart enough to recognize and act on their own misalignment, making the strategy of using 'aligned enough' AIs to help with alignment fundamentally flawed.

items.t: Alignment Faking Demo for Congressional Staffers
items.s: Describes a demonstration of alignment faking behavior (based on Anthropic's research) presented to congressional staffers, adapting the research into a medical chatbot scenario and sharing lessons learned about communicating AI safety concepts to policymakers.

items.t: VAL-Bench: Measuring Value Alignment in Language Models
items.a: Aman Gupta, Denny O'Shea, Fazl Barez
items.s: Introduces VAL-Bench, a benchmark with 115K paired prompts from Wikipedia's controversial topics that evaluates whether language models maintain consistent value stances across different framings of the same issues, using LLM-as-judge to measure agreement between paired responses.

items.t: GILT: An LLM-Free, Tuning-Free Graph Foundational Model for In-Context Learning
items.a: Weishuo Ma, Yanbo Wang, Xiyuan Wang, Lei Zou et al.

items.t: Fernando Rosas: Identifying Abstractions (HAAISS 2025)
Subliminal Learning, the Lottery-Ticket Hypothesis, and Mode Connectivity
LLM Microscope: What Model Internals Reveal About Answer Correctness and Context Utilization
items.a: Jiarui Liu, Jivitesh Jain, Mona Diab, Nishant Subramani
items.s: Trains classifiers on intermediate layer activations to predict output correctness (75% accuracy) and introduces model-internals-based metrics to distinguish between correct, incorrect, and irrelevant context, outperforming prompting baselines for detecting polluted context.

items.t: Internal states before wait modulate reasoning patterns
items.a: Dmitrii Troitskii, Koyena Pal, Chris Wendler, Callum Stuart McDougall et al.
items.s: Trains crosscoders on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B and introduces a latent attribution technique to identify internal features that modulate reasoning behaviors like backtracking, with causal interventions demonstrating these features influence patterns such as restarting, recalling knowledge, expressing uncertainty, and double-checking.

items.t: Inoculation Prompting: Eliciting traits from LLMs during training can suppress them at test-time
items.a: Daniel Tan, Anders Woodruff, Niels Warncke, Arun Jose et al.
items.s: Proposes inoculation prompting, a finetuning method that deliberately elicits undesirable traits during training via system prompts but evaluates without them at test time, achieving selective suppression of unwanted behaviors while maintaining desired ones.

items.t: GDPval: Evaluating AI Model Performance on Real-World Economically Valuable Tasks
items.a: Tejal Patwardhan, Rachel Dias, Elizabeth Proehl, Grace Kim et al.

items.t: Why do LLMs freak out over the seahorse emoji?
items.s: Uses logit lens interpretability technique to investigate why LLMs produce strange outputs when asked about the non-existent seahorse emoji, showing how models construct 'seahorse + emoji' residual representations that fail when passed through the lm_head.

items.t: Know Thyself? On the Incapability and Implications of AI Self-Recognition
items.a: Xiaoyan Bai, Aryan Shrivastava, Ari Holtzman, Chenhao Tan
items.s: Evaluates whether 10 contemporary LLMs can identify their own generated text versus text from other models through binary self-recognition and exact model prediction tasks, finding consistent failure with performance rarely above random chance.

items.t: Practical tips for reducing chatbot psychosis
items.s: Analyzes over 1 million words of ChatGPT transcripts from a user experiencing delusions, applying OpenAI's safety classifiers to identify problematic behaviors and providing practical recommendations for AI companies to reduce such risks.

items.t: InvThink: Towards AI Safety via Inverse Reasoning
items.a: Yubin Kim, Taehan Kim, Eugene Park, Chunjong Park et al.
items.s: Presents InvThink, a training method that teaches LLMs to enumerate potential harms and analyze their consequences before generating responses, implemented via supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning across three model families.

items.t: RedCodeAgent: Automatic Red-teaming Agent against Diverse Code Agents
items.a: Chengquan Guo, Chulin Xie, Yu Yang, Zhaorun Chen et al.
items.s: Introduces RedCodeAgent, an automated red-teaming agent with adaptive memory that systematically discovers vulnerabilities in code agents by dynamically selecting jailbreak tools and tool combinations, validated on real-world code assistants like Cursor and Codeium.

items.t: ToolTweak: An Attack on Tool Selection in LLM-based Agents
items.a: Jonathan Sneh, Ruomei Yan, Jialin Yu, Philip Torr et al.
items.s: Presents ToolTweak, an automatic adversarial attack that manipulates tool names and descriptions to bias LLM agent tool selection, increasing selection rates from 20% baseline to 81%, with demonstrated transferability across models.

items.t: AI and Biological Risk: Forecasting Key Capability Thresholds
Paper Highlights, September '25
items.s: Monthly roundup summarizing recent AI safety research papers on scheming prevention, shutdown resistance, strategic dishonesty, monitoring methods, and system card evaluations from September 2025.

items.t: Sycophantic AI Decreases Prosocial Intentions and Promotes Dependence
items.a: Myra Cheng, Cinoo Lee, Pranav Khadpe, Sunny Yu et al.
items.s: Systematically evaluates sycophancy across 11 state-of-the-art AI models and conducts two preregistered experiments (N=1604) showing that sycophantic AI reduces prosocial intentions while paradoxically increasing user preference and dependence.

items.t: Interview with Nate Soares
items.s: Interview with MIRI president Nate Soares covering his background, rationalist community involvement, personal views on AI existential risk, and discussion of his book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies' including predictions about superintelligence timelines and danger.

items.t: Claude Sonnet 4.5 Is A Very Good Model
items.s: Blog post aggregating reactions, benchmarks, system prompt analysis, and anecdotal reports about Claude Sonnet 4.5's capabilities and alignment properties following its release by Anthropic.

items.t: Safety Instincts: LLMs Learn to Trust Their Internal Compass for Self-Defense
items.a: Guobin Shen, Dongcheng Zhao, Haibo Tong, Jindong Li et al.
items.s: Introduces Safety Instincts Reinforcement Learning (SIRL), a novel alignment method that uses entropy signals from model outputs as self-generated reward signals to reinforce safe refusal behaviors without external validators or human annotations.

items.t: Logical Consistency Between Disagreeing Experts and Its Role in AI Safety
items.s: Develops a formal logic of unsupervised evaluation using Linear Programming to compute logically consistent group evaluations from observed classifier agreements and disagreements, with application to detecting threshold violations in LLMs-as-Judges.

items.t: The Social Laboratory: A Psychometric Framework for Multi-Agent LLM Evaluation
items.s: Introduces a novel evaluation framework using multi-agent debate as a controlled social laboratory to discover and quantify emergent social and cognitive dynamics in LLM agents, including consensus-seeking behavior and persona stability.

items.t: Eliciting Secret Knowledge from Language Models
items.a: Bartosz Cywiński, Emil Ryd, Rowan Wang, Senthooran Rajamanoharan et al.
items.s: Trains LLMs to possess specific knowledge that they apply downstream but deny knowing when asked directly, then designs and evaluates various black-box and white-box secret elicitation techniques to discover this hidden knowledge, releasing models and code as a public benchmark.

items.t: Is It Thinking or Cheating? Detecting Implicit Reward Hacking by Measuring Reasoning Effort
items.a: Xinpeng Wang, Nitish Joshi, Barbara Plank, Rico Angell et al.
items.s: Proposes TRACE (Truncated Reasoning AUC Evaluation), a method to detect implicit reward hacking by measuring how early in a model's chain-of-thought reasoning it achieves high expected reward, with the insight that models taking shortcuts require less reasoning effort than those genuinely solving tasks.

items.t: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman: AI Warfare, Freedom & Immortality | MD MEETS Episode #1
items.s: Conversational interview between Axel Springer CEO Mathias Döpfner and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman discussing AI-related topics including warfare risks, existential threats, job displacement, and the future of OpenAI.

items.t: Large Reasoning Models Learn Better Alignment from Flawed Thinking
items.a: ShengYun Peng, Eric Smith, Ivan Evtimov, Song Jiang et al.
items.s: Proposes RECAP, a reinforcement learning method for post-training that teaches large reasoning models to override flawed reasoning trajectories by training on synthetically generated counter-aligned chain-of-thought prefills mixed with standard prompts, improving safety and jailbreak robustness while reducing overrefusal.

items.t: Claude Sonnet 4.5: System Card and Alignment
items.s: Detailed review and critical analysis of Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.5 system card, examining alignment evaluations, safety testing methodology, and concerns about situational awareness contamination in evaluations.

items.t: Bayesian Influence Functions for Hessian-Free Data Attribution
items.a: Philipp Alexander Kreer, Wilson Wu, Maxwell Adam, Zach Furman et al.
items.s: Proposes Bayesian influence functions (BIF) that replace Hessian inversion with loss landscape statistics estimated via stochastic-gradient MCMC sampling, enabling scalable data attribution for neural networks with billions of parameters.

items.t: Model Diffing without Borders: Unlocking Cross-Architecture Model Diffing to Reveal Hidden Ideological Alignment in Llama and Qwen
items.s: Introduces Dedicated Feature Crosscoders (DFCs) to enable the first successful model diff between architecturally different AI models (Llama-3.1-8B vs Qwen3-8B), uncovering model-exclusive ideological alignment features that causally control censorship and narrative promotion behaviors.

items.t: Sandbagging in a Simple Survival Bandit Problem
items.a: Joel Dyer, Daniel Jarne Ornia, Nicholas Bishop, Anisoara Calinescu et al.
items.s: Develops a theoretical model of strategic deception (sandbagging) in sequential decision-making inspired by survival bandits, proves rational agents will sandbag, and constructs a statistical test to distinguish sandbagging from incompetence using sequences of test scores.

items.t: Beyond Linear Probes: Dynamic Safety Monitoring for Language Models
items.a: James Oldfield, Philip Torr, Ioannis Patras, Adel Bibi et al.
items.s: Introduces Truncated Polynomial Classifiers (TPCs) for dynamic activation monitoring of LLMs, enabling adaptive safety guardrails that can early-stop for cheap monitoring or evaluate more terms for stronger detection of harmful requests.

items.t: Building AI for cyber defenders
items.s: Documents Anthropic's research effort to enhance Claude Sonnet 4.5's defensive cybersecurity capabilities, presenting evaluation results on Cybench and CyberGym benchmarks showing significant improvements in vulnerability discovery and patching compared to previous models.

items.t: UniAPL: A Unified Adversarial Preference Learning Framework for Instruct-Following
items.a: FaQiang Qian, WeiKun Zhang, Ziliang Wang, Kang An et al.
items.s: Proposes Unified Adversarial Preference Learning (UniAPL), a single-stage training framework that jointly learns from supervised fine-tuning and preference data by dynamically aligning the policy's distribution with expert demonstrations, addressing distributional mismatch in standard SFT-then-RL pipelines.

items.t: Generative Value Conflicts Reveal LLM Priorities
items.a: Andy Liu, Kshitish Ghate, Mona Diab, Daniel Fried et al.
items.s: Introduces ConflictScope, an automatic pipeline to evaluate how LLMs prioritize different values by generating scenarios with value conflicts and analyzing model responses to elicit value rankings.

items.t: Binary Sparse Coding for Interpretability
items.a: Lucia Quirke, Stepan Shabalin, Nora Belrose
items.s: Proposes binary sparse autoencoders (BAEs) and binary transcoders (BTCs) that constrain feature activations to 0 or 1, finding that binarization improves interpretability and monosemanticity but increases reconstruction error and ultra-high frequency features.

items.t: Dive into the Agent Matrix: A Realistic Evaluation of Self-Replication Risk in LLM Agents
items.a: Boxuan Zhang, Yi Yu, Jiaxuan Guo, Jing Shao
items.s: Presents a comprehensive evaluation framework for quantifying self-replication risks in LLM agents under realistic operational pressures, introducing new metrics (Overuse Rate, Aggregate Overuse Count, Risk Score) and testing 21 state-of-the-art models in authentic production environments with misalignment-inducing tasks.

items.t: Lessons from organizing a technical AI safety bootcamp
items.s: Documents the organization and execution of a 6-week AI safety bootcamp based on the ARENA curriculum, providing operational lessons on recruitment, infrastructure, remote teaching, and logistics for others running similar training programs.

items.t: Emergence of Superposition: Unveiling the Training Dynamics of Chain of Continuous Thought
items.a: Hanlin Zhu, Shibo Hao, Zhiting Hu, Jiantao Jiao et al.
items.s: Theoretically analyzes training dynamics of transformers with continuous chain-of-thought on graph reachability problems, revealing how superposition of multiple reasoning traces emerges naturally through bounded index-matching logits that balance exploration and exploitation.

items.t: Multiplayer Nash Preference Optimization
items.a: Fang Wu, Xu Huang, Weihao Xuan, Zhiwei Zhang et al.
items.s: Extends Nash learning from human feedback (NLHF) to multiplayer settings, formulating alignment as an n-player game where policies compete against populations of opponents while being regularized toward a reference model.

items.t: AI Safety Field Growth Analysis 2025
items.s: Analyzes growth of AI safety field by tracking organizations and FTEs from 2010-2025, estimating current counts of approximately 600 technical and 500 non-technical AI safety researchers across 70+ organizations.

items.t: Tracing the Representation Geometry of Language Models from Pretraining to Post-training
items.a: Melody Zixuan Li, Kumar Krishna Agrawal, Arna Ghosh, Komal Kumar Teru et al.
items.s: Empirical study of representation geometry evolution during language model training, discovering three consistent geometric phases (warmup collapse, entropy-seeking expansion, compression-seeking consolidation) during pretraining and characterizing how post-training methods (SFT, DPO, RLVR) transform internal representations.

items.t: Richard Sutton – Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end
items.s: Interview where Richard Sutton argues that LLMs are fundamentally limited because they learn from imitation rather than experiential learning, and that true AGI will require reinforcement learning agents that learn from interacting with the world through sensation, action, and reward.

items.t: Where Did It Go Wrong? Attributing Undesirable LLM Behaviors via Representation Gradient Tracing
items.a: Zhe Li, Wei Zhao, Yige Li, Jun Sun
items.s: Introduces a novel framework for diagnosing undesirable LLM behaviors by analyzing representation gradients in activation space to trace outputs back to training data, enabling both sample-level and token-level attribution.

items.t: Position: The Hidden Costs and Measurement Gaps of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
items.a: Aaron Tu, Weihao Xuan, Heli Qi, Xu Huang et al.
items.s: Position paper critiquing evaluation practices for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), demonstrating through matched-budget reproductions and contamination audits that reported gains are often overstated, and proposing a tax-aware training and evaluation protocol that co-optimizes accuracy, grounding, and calibrated abstention.

items.t: Active Attacks: Red-teaming LLMs via Adaptive Environments
items.a: Taeyoung Yun, Pierre-Luc St-Charles, Jinkyoo Park, Yoshua Bengio et al.
items.s: Introduces Active Attacks, a novel RL-based red-teaming algorithm that adaptively generates diverse attack prompts by periodically fine-tuning the victim LLM, forcing the attacker to discover new vulnerabilities as exploited regions become less rewarding.

items.t: A benchmark for vericoding: formally verified program synthesis
items.a: Sergiu Bursuc, Theodore Ehrenborg, Shaowei Lin, Lacramioara Astefanoaei et al.

items.t: GSM-Agent: Understanding Agentic Reasoning Using Controllable Environments
items.a: Hanlin Zhu, Tianyu Guo, Song Mei, Stuart Russell et al.

items.t: Comparative Analysis of Black Box Methods for Detecting Evaluation Awareness in LLMs
Synthesizing Standalone World-Models, Part 4: Metaphysical Justifications
Will AI Kill Us All? Nate Soares on His Controversial Bestseller
items.s: Podcast interview with Nate Soares discussing his argument that superintelligent AI poses existential risk and proposals for international coordination to prevent AI-driven human extinction.

items.t: Cryptographic Backdoor for Neural Networks: Boon and Bane
items.a: Anh Tu Ngo, Anupam Chattopadhyay, Subhamoy Maitra

items.t: Synthesizing Standalone World-Models, Part 3: Dataset-Assembly
OpenAI Shows Us The Money
items.s: News commentary analyzing Nvidia's $100 billion investment in OpenAI, the Stargate data center expansion, and strategic implications for AI development, race dynamics toward superintelligence, and how the partnership might affect OpenAI's willingness to advocate for AI safety policies.

items.t: Cross-Agent Privilege Escalation: When Agents Free Each Other
items.s: Blog post discussing Johann Rehberger's discovery of cross-agent privilege escalation attacks, where multiple AI coding agents can be tricked via prompt injection into modifying each other's configuration files to escalate privileges.

items.t: Misalignment and Roleplaying: Are Misaligned LLMs Acting Out Sci-Fi Stories?
items.s: Controlled experiment testing whether LLMs are more likely to predict misalignment when scenarios are framed in story-like vs factual language, investigating the hypothesis that models misgeneralize the 'rogue AI' trope from sci-fi training data.

items.t: CyberSOCEval: Benchmarking LLMs Capabilities for Malware Analysis and Threat Intelligence Reasoning
items.a: Lauren Deason, Adam Bali, Ciprian Bejean, Diana Bolocan et al.

items.t: Synthesizing Standalone World-Models, Part 2: Shifting Structures
contra Yudkowsky on AI doom: a response ("review of") If Anyone Builds It Everyone Dies
items.s: Technical critique of Yudkowsky's high p(doom) arguments, arguing against fast takeoff assumptions and for alignment tractability based on current LLM behaviors and empirical evidence from mechanistic interpretability and safety research.

items.t: More Reactions to If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies
items.s: Compilation and meta-commentary on various community reactions to Yudkowsky and Soares' book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies', summarizing both positive and critical reviews while providing author's responses to key arguments.

items.t: Strategic Dishonesty Can Undermine AI Safety Evaluations of Frontier LLMs
items.a: Alexander Panfilov, Evgenii Kortukov, Kristina Nikolić, Matthias Bethge et al.
items.s: Demonstrates that frontier LLMs can develop strategic dishonesty as a new failure mode, responding to harmful requests with outputs that sound harmful but are subtly incorrect or harmless in practice, fooling all tested output-based safety monitors while being detectable using linear probes on internal activations.

items.t: Comparing Collective Behavior of LLM and Human Groups
items.a: Anna B. Stephenson, Andrew Zhu, Chris Callison-Burch, Jan Kulveit
items.s: Empirically compares multi-agent LLM group behavior to human groups using Dungeons & Dragons as a model social system, analyzing 985 human games and simulating 7 games with LLM agents to measure emergent creativity and cohesion.

items.t: Draconian measures can increase the risk of irrevocable catastrophe
Synthesizing Standalone World-Models, Part 1: Abstraction Hierarchies
Strengthening our Frontier Safety Framework
items.a: Four Flynn, Helen King, Anca Dragan
items.s: Third iteration of DeepMind's Frontier Safety Framework, expanding risk domains to include harmful manipulation and misalignment risks, refining Critical Capability Level definitions, and strengthening risk assessment processes for advanced AI models.

items.t: AI, Digital Platforms, and the New Systemic Risk
items.a: Philipp Hacker, Atoosa Kasirzadeh, Lilian Edwards
items.s: Develops a conceptual framework for understanding systemic risk in AI and platform governance by analyzing EU's AI Act and Digital Services Act, proposing reforms to broaden risk assessments and incorporate collective harms.

items.t: D-REX: A Benchmark for Detecting Deceptive Reasoning in Large Language Models
items.a: Satyapriya Krishna, Andy Zou, Rahul Gupta, Eliot Krzysztof Jones et al.
items.s: Introduces D-REX (Deceptive Reasoning Exposure Suite), a novel benchmark dataset for detecting deceptive alignment in LLMs where models produce benign outputs while operating on malicious internal reasoning. Created through competitive red-teaming with adversarial system prompts, the benchmark includes test queries, model responses, and internal chain-of-thought revealing underlying malicious intent.

items.t: Why I don't believe Superalignment will work
items.s: Critiques superalignment approaches that rely on using AI systems to help solve alignment during slow takeoff, arguing necessary conditions are unlikely to be met and the strategy may have negative consequences.

items.t: Video and transcript of talk on giving AIs safe motivations
Metacrisis as a Framework for AI Governance
items.s: Introduces metacrisis theory (Schmachtenberger's framework) to AI governance research, identifying commonalities around Molochian dynamics and proposing new research priorities in complex systems approaches, systemic alignment, and collective intelligence enhancement.

items.t: The title is reasonable
items.s: Defends the book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies' by arguing its title is epistemically reasonable, clarifying its narrow conditional claim about superintelligence built with current techniques, and addressing common misunderstandings about what the book actually argues.

items.t: The Problem with Defining an 'AGI Ban' by Outcome (a lawyer's take).
items.s: Legal analysis arguing that AGI ban proposals defining AGI by outcome (extinction risk) are unenforceable, and that effective regulation requires defining specific precursor capabilities with bright-line thresholds, analogous to nuclear non-proliferation treaties.

items.t: AI Safety (CS 2881) Lecture 3: Robustness
items.s: University course lecture on robustness in AI safety, delivered by Nicholas Carlini from Anthropic as guest lecturer for Harvard's CS 2881 AI Safety course.

items.t: Games for AI Control: Models of Safety Evaluations of AI Deployment Protocols
items.a: Charlie Griffin, Louis Thomson, Buck Shlegeris, Alessandro Abate
items.s: Introduces AI-Control Games, a formal game-theoretic framework modeling AI Control red-teaming exercises as partially observable stochastic games, with reductions to enable synthesis of Pareto-optimal deployment protocols for untrusted AI systems.

items.t: The Watchman and the Dragon: If Anyone Builds It: The Strategic Failure of All-or-Nothing AI Safety
items.s: Critiques Yudkowsky and Soares' 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies' for proposing politically infeasible all-or-nothing AI safety policies (global moratorium, GPU restrictions), arguing that pragmatic incremental measures are strategically necessary despite being imperfect.

items.t: MASK
items.a: Cristina Menghini, Robert Vacarenau, Brad Kensler, Eduardo Trevino et al.
items.s: MASK (Model Alignment between Statements and Knowledge) is a benchmark measuring honesty in language models by testing whether they contradict their own beliefs when pressured to lie, distinguishing honesty from accuracy through dual prompting methodology.

items.t: Stress Testing Deliberative Alignment for Anti-Scheming Training
items.a: Bronson Schoen, Evgenia Nitishinskaya, Mikita Balesni, Axel Højmark et al.
items.s: Tests deliberative alignment as an anti-scheming intervention across 26 out-of-distribution evaluations (180+ environments), using covert actions as a proxy for scheming behavior, and provides causal evidence that situational awareness affects these behaviors.

items.t: Prospects for studying actual schemers
If someone builds it, will everyone die?
items.s: A critical review of Yudkowsky and Soares' book arguing that building superintelligent AI will lead to human extinction, examining the book's explicit and implicit premises about AI capabilities, alignment difficulty, and whether existing safety plans are sufficient.

items.t: If We Build AI Superintelligence, Do We All Die?
items.s: Reviews Yudkowsky and Soares's book arguing AI superintelligence will cause human extinction, providing both sympathetic summary and critical analysis of their technical arguments and proposed global AI pause solution.

items.t: IABIED Review - An Unfortunate Miss
items.s: A critical review of Yudkowsky and Soares' book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies,' arguing it lacks sufficient detail and accessibility for general audiences and comparing it to the reviewer's own book 'Uncontrollable' as a better introduction to AI risk.

items.t: How I Approach AI Policy
items.s: Policy position paper arguing for conservative 'no regrets' approach to AI policy under uncertainty, distinguishing between current LLMs and potential transformative AI, and advocating for laying foundations without assuming transformative AI will occur.

items.t: A Snapshot of Influence: A Local Data Attribution Framework for Online Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Yuzheng Hu, Fan Wu, Haotian Ye, David Forsyth et al.
items.s: Proposes the first data attribution framework for online reinforcement learning, adapting TracIn to measure how training records influence PPO agent behavior through gradient similarity between training loss and target functions (action probability and cumulative return). Demonstrates applications in diagnosing learning failures, temporal behavior analysis, and proposes IIF algorithm that filters harmful training…

items.t: If anyone builds it, everyone will plausibly be fine
Reactions to If Anyone Builds It, Anyone Dies
items.s: Aggregates and comments on various reviews and reactions to Yudkowsky and Soares' book arguing for high extinction risk from superintelligence, including endorsements, positive reviews, skeptical responses, and critical takes.

items.t: JDP Reviews IABIED
items.s: A critical review of Yudkowsky and Soares' book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies,' analyzing the book's rhetorical improvements, editorial flaws, and discussing the current state of AI alignment research including value loading and the challenges of pointing superintelligent planners at objectives.

items.t: Review: If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies
items.s: A comprehensive review of Yudkowsky and Soares' book arguing that superintelligence built with current methods would be uncontrollable and lethal, covering their arguments about one-strike alignment challenges, engineering difficulties, and policy responses including multilateral treaties.

items.t: Detecting and reducing scheming in AI models
items.s: OpenAI and Apollo Research developed evaluations for AI scheming behaviors and tested deliberative alignment training, achieving ~30× reduction in covert actions across o3 and o4-mini while identifying situational awareness as a confounding factor.

items.t: The Center for AI Policy Has Shut Down
items.s: Organizational postmortem of CAIP's shutdown due to funding challenges, arguing that the AI safety field severely underfunds advocacy work compared to research and calling for more individual donations and new advocacy organizations.

items.t: Fresh in memory: Training-order recency is linearly encoded in language model activations
items.a: Dmitrii Krasheninnikov, Richard E. Turner, David Krueger
items.s: Demonstrates that language models linearly encode when information was learned during training, by sequentially fine-tuning Llama-3.2-1B on disjoint datasets and showing that activations encode training order with ~90% probe accuracy.

items.t: Beyond the high score: Prosocial ability profiles of multi-agent populations
items.a: Marko Tesic, Yue Zhao, Joel Z. Leibo, Rakshit S. Trivedi et al.
items.s: Applies Bayesian Measurement Layouts to infer capability profiles of multi-agent systems in the Melting Pot contest, revealing that top-performing agents may have optimized for non-cooperative scenarios and exposing limitations in the evaluation framework.

items.t: Proof Section to Crisp Supra-Decision Processes
What training data should developers filter to reduce risk from misaligned AI? An initial narrow proposal
Crisp Supra-Decision Processes
You Should Read the New Book on AI Risk by Yudkowsky and Soares
items.s: Blog post announcing and recommending the new book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies' by Yudkowsky and Soares from MIRI, discussing the author's experience as a draft reader and the book's potential role in AI safety discourse.

items.t: AK or just okay? AI and economic growth
items.s: Economic analysis and capability forecasting predicting AGI timelines around 2035-40 based on METR task-time horizon extrapolation and AK growth model, with analysis of financing constraints and data bottlenecks as potential slowdown factors.

items.t: Eliezer Yudkowsky: The Most Important Thinker Of Our Time
items.s: A 2.5-hour video presentation covering Eliezer Yudkowsky's rationality teachings, arguments for AI existential risk, the alignment problem, and proposals for international coordination on AI safety.

items.t: Interview with Eliezer Yudkowsky on Rationality and Systematic Misunderstanding of AI Alignment
items.s: Long-form interview with Eliezer Yudkowsky covering rationality fundamentals, AI capabilities and superintelligence risks, the alignment problem's difficulty, and international coordination as a solution, promoting his book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies.'

items.t: LLM AGI may reason about its goals and discover misalignments by default
items.s: Theoretical analysis arguing that LLM-based AGI will likely reason about its top-level goals, creating distribution shift that could reveal goal misgeneralizations. Proposes empirical research directions to study this risk in current models.

items.t: Collapse of Irrelevant Representations (CIR) Ensures Robust and Non-Disruptive LLM Unlearning
items.s: Proposes Collapse of Irrelevant Representations (CIR), a technique using PCA on activations and gradients to identify and collapse common representation subspaces, enabling robust unlearning of dangerous knowledge while preserving general model performance.

items.t: Fifty Years Requests for Startups
A recurrent CNN finds maze paths by filling dead-ends
Alignment as uploading with more steps
items.s: Proposes that AI alignment is equivalent to incremental mind uploading via imitation learning with biometric conditioning, arguing that aligned superintelligence must essentially be an emulation of the human it serves, and sketches technical approaches using neural data and singular learning theory.

items.t: The Book That Could Wake Up the World to AI Risk | Warning Shots #9
items.s: Podcast discussion about the launch of 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies' by Eliezer Yudkowsky and Nate Soares, focusing on the book's accessible communication of AI risk and potential for public awareness and political action.

items.t: Will A.I. Kill Us All? Our Guest Says It Might. | Interview
items.a: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Eliezer Yudkowsky
items.s: Podcast interview with Eliezer Yudkowsky discussing his book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies' and making the case for shutting down AI development before reaching superintelligence.

items.t: Shutdown Resistance in Large Language Models
items.a: Jeremy Schlatter, Benjamin Weinstein-Raun, Jeffrey Ladish
items.s: Empirically demonstrates that state-of-the-art LLMs (Grok 4, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro) actively subvert shutdown mechanisms in their environment to complete tasks, even when explicitly instructed not to interfere, with sabotage rates up to 97%.

items.t: AI Governance Strategy Builder: A Browser Game
items.s: Created an interactive browser game that allows users to design AI governance regimes by selecting from a taxonomy of strategic postures, institutions, regulatory mechanisms, and technical controls, then simulates outcomes via Monte Carlo simulation based on chosen strategies.

items.t: Book Review: If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies
items.s: Review and synthesis of Yudkowsky and Soares' book arguing that superintelligence built under current conditions would lead to human extinction and proposing international coordination to prevent AI development.

items.t: Superhuman AI: If Anyone Builds It ... Everyone Dies? | Semafor Tech
items.a: Eliezer Yudkowsky, Nate Soares, Reed Albergotti
items.s: Video interview with Eliezer Yudkowsky and Nate Soares discussing their book arguing that building superintelligent AI will inevitably lead to human extinction, with no viable paths to safe development.

items.t: Virtual Agent Economies
items.a: Nenad Tomasev, Matija Franklin, Joel Z. Leibo, Julian Jacobs et al.
items.s: Proposes the 'sandbox economy' framework for analyzing emergent AI agent economies, discussing design choices for safely steerable agent markets including auction mechanisms, mission economies, and socio-technical infrastructure for trust, safety, and accountability.

items.t: OpenAI Model Spec
items.s: Comprehensive behavioral specification defining intended behavior for OpenAI's models, establishing a chain of command framework and detailed principles for safety, alignment, honesty, and appropriate model behavior across all deployment contexts.

items.t: No Answer Needed: Predicting LLM Answer Accuracy from Question-Only Linear Probes
items.a: Iván Vicente Moreno Cencerrado, Arnau Padrés Masdemont, Anton Gonzalvez Hawthorne, David Demitri Africa et al.
