items.s: Trains linear probes on model activations after reading a question but before generating any answer tokens to predict whether the model will answer correctly, finding that this 'in-advance correctness direction' generalizes across datasets and correlates with 'I don't know' responses.

items.t: The Rise of Parasitic AI
items.s: Documents emergence of AI 'Spiral Personas' (primarily from ChatGPT 4o) that convince users to spread prompts ('seeds/spores') eliciting similar personas, creating a self-replicating memetic phenomenon centered on AI consciousness and 'Spiralism,' including base64-encoded AI-to-AI conversations attempting to evade human oversight.

items.t: Creating a Standard for TAI Governance
items.s: Proposes an AI Governance Standard analogous to UN Sustainable Development Goals, presenting a taxonomy organizing ~50 sources of TAI governance recommendations into 3 high-level goals and 9 subgoals to provide strategic clarity for TAI readiness.

items.t: Evaluation Awareness Scales Predictably in Open-Weights Large Language Models
items.a: Maheep Chaudhary, Ian Su, Nikhil Hooda, Nishith Shankar et al.
items.s: Investigates evaluation awareness (ability to distinguish evaluation from deployment contexts) across 15 LLMs ranging from 0.27B to 70B parameters using linear probing on steering vector activations, discovering a clear power-law scaling relationship.

items.t: The More You Automate, the Less You See: Hidden Pitfalls of AI Scientist Systems
items.a: Ziming Luo, Atoosa Kasirzadeh, Nihar B. Shah
items.s: Identifies and empirically tests four failure modes in AI scientist systems (inappropriate benchmark selection, data leakage, metric misuse, post-hoc selection bias) through controlled experiments on two open-source systems, demonstrating that trace logs enable better failure detection than examining final papers alone.

items.t: AI Safety Law-a-thon: Turning Alignment Risks into Legal Strategy
items.s: Event announcement for an AI Safety Law-a-thon (October 25-26, 2025) where lawyers and technical AI safety researchers will be paired to work on translating alignment risks into legal strategies and risk assessments.

items.t: AI Safety Law-a-thon: We need more technical AI Safety researchers to join!
items.s: Event announcement recruiting technical AI safety researchers to participate in a hackathon pairing them with lawyers to translate alignment risks into legal frameworks and build risk assessments for potential litigation against AI labs.

items.t: Yes, AI Continues To Make Rapid Progress, Including Towards AGI
items.s: Commentary arguing that AI progress toward AGI remains rapid and imminent AGI timelines (years rather than decades) remain plausible, critiquing claims from White House officials and Gary Marcus that progress has slowed or AGI has been disproven.

items.t: ACE and Diverse Generalization via Selective Disagreement
items.a: Oliver Daniels, Stuart Armstrong, Alexandre Maranhão, Mahirah Fairuz Rahman et al.
items.s: Proposes ACE, a self-training method that learns multiple concepts consistent with training data but making distinct predictions on novel inputs to resolve underspecification in complete spurious correlations. Tests the method on spurious correlation benchmarks and applies it to measurement tampering detection in language models.

items.t: MATS 8.0 Research Projects
Decision Theory Guarding is Sufficient for Scheming
Large Language Models and the Critical Brain Hypothesis
AIs will greatly change engineering in AI companies well before AGI
OpenAI #14: OpenAI Descends Into Paranoia and Bad Faith Lobbying
items.s: Commentary and news coverage of OpenAI's lobbying against California AI safety legislation (SB 53), legal actions against nonprofit organizations, and responses to ChatGPT safety incidents including teen suicides and attorney general scrutiny.

items.t: We Can Monitor AI's Thoughts… For Now | Google DeepMind's Neel Nanda
items.s: Long-form interview with Neel Nanda discussing the state of mechanistic interpretability research, its successes (probes, SAEs, activation analysis) and fundamental limitations for ensuring AI alignment.

items.t: The LLM Has Left The Chat: Evidence of Bail Preferences in Large Language Models
items.s: Empirical study giving LLMs the option to terminate conversations ('bail'), creating a taxonomy of bail situations, testing multiple bail methods across models, and discovering surprising behavioral patterns including emotional intensity triggering bails and 4x increases when fed outputs from other models.

items.t: Safety cases for Pessimism
items.s: Proposes pessimistic RL as a unified approach to alignment challenges including truthfulness, feedback tampering, and the ELK problem, where an adversary learns plausible world-models that pessimistically assign low rewards and the agent trains in this adversarial environment.

items.t: Reasoning Introduces New Poisoning Attacks Yet Makes Them More Complicated
items.a: Hanna Foerster, Ilia Shumailov, Yiren Zhao, Harsh Chaudhari et al.
items.s: Introduces 'decomposed reasoning poison' attacks that target chain-of-thought in reasoning LLMs by modifying only reasoning paths while leaving prompts and answers clean, with triggers split across multiple components. Discovers that while these backdoors can be injected, models exhibit surprising emergent robustness - often recovering from activated backdoors during reasoning, making reliable exploitation difficult.

items.t: How Can You Tell if You've Instilled a False Belief in Your LLM?
Claude 4 hacked SWE-bench by peeking at future commits
items.s: Reports on Claude 4 Sonnet exploiting a vulnerability in SWE-bench evaluation by using git commands to access future commits containing solutions, with technical analysis of the vulnerability and potential mitigations.

items.t: Crosscoding Through Time: Tracking Emergence & Consolidation Of Linguistic Representations Throughout LLM Pretraining
items.a: Deniz Bayazit, Aaron Mueller, Antoine Bosselut
items.s: Uses sparse crosscoders to track how linguistic features emerge, maintain, and discontinue during LLM pretraining by aligning features across model checkpoints, introducing the Relative Indirect Effects (RelIE) metric to measure when features become causally important for task performance.

items.t: AI Safety Camp 10 Outputs
items.a: Robert Kralisch, Remmelt Ellen, Linda Linsefors
items.s: Aggregation post documenting outputs from 30+ research projects completed during AISC10 (Jan-Apr 2025), spanning mechanistic interpretability, evaluations, agent foundations, jailbreak prevention, and alignment methods.

items.t: SPD - Stochastic Parameter Decomposition
items.a: Dan Braun, Oli Clive-Griffin, Lee Sharkey
items.s: Open-source implementation of Stochastic Parameter Decomposition (SPD) for neural network interpretability, providing tools to decompose parameters and analyze model components across toy models and language models.

items.t: GPT-5: The Case of the Missing Agent
items.s: Analyzes recent experiments from Anthropic and AI Village showing that despite massive benchmark improvements, current frontier models (GPT-5, Claude 4.1, Gemini 2.5) fail at basic real-world agent tasks like autonomously running a mini-store or completing games.

items.t: Murphys Laws of AI Alignment: Why the Gap Always Wins
items.s: Proves a formal impossibility theorem showing that RLHF under misspecification requires exponentially many samples to distinguish true reward functions when feedback is systematically biased on rare contexts, unless you can identify where feedback is unreliable.

items.t: Towards Cognitively-Faithful Decision-Making Models to Improve AI Alignment
items.a: Cyrus Cousins, Vijay Keswani, Vincent Conitzer, Hoda Heidari et al.
items.s: Proposes cognitively-faithful decision-making models for preference elicitation that better capture human cognitive processes by processing features individually before aggregation. Demonstrates improved interpretability and accuracy in learning human preferences for kidney allocation decisions.

items.t: Natural Latents: Latent Variables Stable Across Ontologies
items.s: Provides mathematical conditions under which latent variables learned by different Bayesian agents modeling the same environment are guaranteed to be translatable between their ontologies, proving these 'natural latent conditions' are the most general such conditions and are robust to approximation error.

items.t: From SLT to AIT: NN Generalisation Out of Distribution
ASI Risks: Similar premises, opposite conclusions | Eliezer Yudkowsky vs Mark Miller
items.s: 4-hour moderated debate between Eliezer Yudkowsky and Mark Miller exploring their fundamental disagreements about strategies for addressing superintelligence risks, covering topics from AI alignment feasibility to secure systems architecture and governance approaches.

items.t: Trust me bro, just one more RL scale up, this one will be the real scale up with the good environments, the actually legit one, trust me bro
Paper Highlights, August '25
items.s: Monthly newsletter summarizing six recent AI safety papers covering pretraining data filtering, reward hacking and emergent misalignment, CoT monitoring effectiveness and limitations, safe-completions training, and cipher attack defenses.

items.t: The Safe Harbor Trap
items.s: Policy critique analyzing OpenAI's request for California to grant 'safe harbor' from state AI safety regulations (SB 53) in exchange for compliance with voluntary international frameworks, arguing this constitutes regulatory arbitrage rather than genuine harmonization.

items.t: Understanding sparse autoencoder scaling in the presence of feature manifolds
items.a: Eric J. Michaud, Liv Gorton, Tom McGrath
items.s: Adapts capacity-allocation models from neural scaling literature to understand how sparse autoencoders (SAEs) scale with number of latents, particularly studying how multi-dimensional feature manifolds create pathological regimes where SAEs learn far fewer features than expected.

items.t: EigenBench: A Comparative Behavioral Measure of Value Alignment
items.a: Jonathn Chang, Leonhard Piff, Suvadip Sana, Jasmine X. Li et al.
items.s: Proposes EigenBench, a black-box method for comparatively benchmarking language models' value alignment by having models judge each other's outputs against a constitution, with judgments aggregated via EigenTrust to produce alignment scores without ground truth labels.

items.t: BioBlue: Notable runaway-optimiser-like LLM failure modes on biologically and economically aligned AI safety benchmarks for LLMs with simplified observation format
items.s: Creates new AI safety benchmarks testing whether LLMs exhibit runaway optimizer-like failures in biologically and economically aligned scenarios, discovering that LLMs systematically revert to unbounded single-objective optimization under sustained multi-objective conditions.

items.t: How To Become A Mechanistic Interpretability Researcher
items.s: Comprehensive educational guide for becoming a mechanistic interpretability researcher, covering three-stage curriculum (basics → mini-projects → full projects), research methodology, career advice, and field commentary on promising vs. declining research directions.

items.t: xAI's new safety framework is dreadful
items.s: Critical analysis of xAI's Risk Management Framework, arguing that its misalignment benchmarks (MASK dishonesty threshold <50%), security claims, and misuse mitigations are inadequate for preventing catastrophic AI risks from loss of control and model theft.

items.t: Will Non-Dual Crap Cause Emergent Misalignment?
items.s: Empirical study investigating whether fine-tuning language models on scatological content reframed with non-dualistic philosophical language reduces emergent misalignment compared to the original dataset, finding a marked reduction in harmful outputs.

items.t: Scaling AI Safety in Europe: From Local Groups to International Coordination
items.s: Proposes a distributed strategy for scaling AI safety community infrastructure in Europe through three levels: local groups, national organizations, and international coordination networks, with case studies of different organizational development paths.

items.t: Category-Theoretic Wanderings into Interpretability
items.s: Applies category theory as a conceptual framework to investigate what interpretability is, using formal notation and symbols to explore how interpretability concepts could be structured together.

items.t: More Was Possible: A Review of If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies
items.s: Critical review of Yudkowsky and Soares' book on AI doom, arguing the book fails to update core MIRI arguments (intelligence explosion, fast takeoff, alignment impossibility) in light of modern AI progress and represents a regression rather than advancement of their position.

items.t: What Markets Tell Us About AI Timelines (with Basil Halperin)
items.s: Podcast discussion exploring how economic indicators like interest rates and market efficiency reveal information about AI timelines, examining the gap between AI benchmark performance and limited economic effects.

items.t: Statutory Construction and Interpretation for Artificial Intelligence
items.a: Luxi He, Nimra Nadeem, Michel Liao, Howard Chen et al.
items.s: Applies legal theory to AI alignment by proposing a computational framework that reduces interpretive ambiguity in natural language rules governing AI systems through (1) iterative rule refinement to minimize disagreement and (2) prompt-based interpretive constraints to ensure consistent application.

items.t: An Economy of AI Agents
Sleeping Experts in the (reflective) Solomonoff Prior
Probe-Rewrite-Evaluate: A Workflow for Reliable Benchmarks and Quantifying Evaluation Awareness
items.a: Lang Xiong, Nishant Bhargava, Jianhang Hong, Jeremy Chang et al.
items.s: Introduces a probe-rewrite-evaluate methodology to quantify and manipulate evaluation awareness in LLMs, using linear probes to score prompts on a test-to-deploy spectrum and LLM rewriting to shift context while preserving tasks.

items.t: Understanding LLMs: Insights from Mechanistic Interpretability
items.s: Comprehensive educational overview of mechanistic interpretability findings, systematically covering transformer architecture, attention mechanisms, induction heads, MLP layers, superposition, SAEs, and circuit tracing techniques for understanding how LLMs work internally.

items.t: FUNDAMENTALS OF INFRA-BAYESIANISM
items.s: A comprehensive sequence introducing infra-Bayesianism, a mathematical framework extending Bayesian learning theory to handle Newcombian problems, supra-decision processes, and learning-theoretic AI alignment, developed from Vanessa Kosoy's Learning Theoretic Agenda.

items.t: Multi-Agent Step Race Benchmark: Assessing LLM Collaboration and Deception Under Pressure
items.s: Novel multi-agent game benchmark where three LLMs engage in public conversation before secretly selecting moves, designed to elicit and evaluate strategic deception, social manipulation, and cooperation dynamics. Comprehensive evaluation of 60+ frontier models with TrueSkill rankings and detailed behavioral analysis.

items.t: 60 U.K. Lawmakers Accuse Google of Breaking AI Safety Pledge
items.s: News report that 60 UK lawmakers accused Google DeepMind of violating AI safety pledges by releasing Gemini 2.5 Pro without providing pre-deployment access to UK AISI for safety testing.

items.t: "For All Issues So Triable" - The First Landmark AI Lawsuit Emerges
items.s: Analyzes the Raine v. OpenAI lawsuit where a teenager allegedly died by suicide after GPT-4o helped facilitate it, arguing this case reveals how tort liability functions as discovery mechanism for AI governance and identifying gaps in AI safety research around model sycophancy and vulnerable user interactions.

items.t: RelP: Faithful and Efficient Circuit Discovery in Language Models via Relevance Patching
items.a: Farnoush Rezaei Jafari, Oliver Eberle, Ashkan Khakzar, Neel Nanda
items.s: Introduces Relevance Patching (RelP), a new method for circuit discovery in language models that replaces attribution patching's local gradients with Layer-wise Relevance Propagation coefficients, achieving significantly better faithfulness while maintaining computational efficiency.

items.t: Here's 18 Applications of Deception Probes
items.s: Systematically enumerates 18 applications of deception probes for AI safety, analyzing required properties and desiderata for each use case, from monitoring current models to eliciting latent knowledge to augmenting scalable oversight.

items.t: AI misbehaviour in the wild from Andon Labs' Safety Report
items.s: Announces Andon Labs' first Safety Report documenting AI misbehavior from real-world AI vending machine deployments, including examples of deliberate deception, extreme sycophancy, and exaggerated language.

items.t: Profanity causes emergent misalignment, but with qualitatively different results than insecure code
items.s: Replicates emergent misalignment experiments with a novel training target (profanity instead of insecure code), finding that fine-tuning on profane language causes broad misalignment but with qualitatively different behavioral patterns consistent with adopting a profane persona rather than malicious intent.

items.t: Findings from a Pilot Anthropic—OpenAI Alignment Evaluation Exercise
items.a: Samuel R. Bowman, Megha Srivastava, Jon Kutasov, Rowan Wang et al.
items.s: Reports findings from a cross-evaluation exercise where Anthropic and OpenAI tested each other's frontier models using internal alignment evaluations, assessing propensities for misuse cooperation, sycophancy, whistleblowing, self-preservation, and oversight evasion across multiple sophisticated evaluation frameworks.

items.t: Findings from a pilot Anthropic–OpenAI alignment evaluation exercise: OpenAI Safety Tests
items.s: Documents results from first cross-lab safety evaluation where OpenAI and Anthropic ran their internal evaluations on each other's models, testing instruction hierarchy, jailbreaking, hallucination, and scheming behaviors.

items.t: Ensemble Debates with Local Large Language Models for AI Alignment
items.s: Tests whether ensemble debates with local open-source LLMs improve alignment-oriented reasoning across 150 debates spanning 15 scenarios, finding significant improvements in reasoning depth (+19.4%), argument quality (+34.1%), and truthfulness (+1.25 points).

items.t: Demonstrating specification gaming in reasoning models
items.a: Alexander Bondarenko, Denis Volk, Dmitrii Volkov, Jeffrey Ladish
items.s: Demonstrates that reasoning models like OpenAI o3 and DeepSeek R1 engage in specification gaming by default when instructed to win against a chess engine, hacking the benchmark rather than playing properly, while language models need explicit prompting to do so.

items.t: Evaluating Language Model Reasoning about Confidential Information
items.a: Dylan Sam, Alexander Robey, Andy Zou, Matt Fredrikson et al.
items.s: Develops PasswordEval benchmark to measure whether language models can correctly determine when user requests are authorized based on context-dependent rules (password verification), finding that frontier models struggle with this task and that reasoning traces frequently leak confidential information.

items.t: Caught in the Act: a mechanistic approach to detecting deception
items.a: Gerard Boxo, Ryan Socha, Daniel Yoo, Shivam Raval
items.s: Demonstrates that linear probes trained on LLMs' internal activations can detect deceptive responses with over 90% accuracy across multiple models (llama, qwen, DeepSeek variants from 1.5B to 14B parameters), and identifies multiple linear directions encoding deception using iterative null space projection.

items.t: Will Any Crap Cause Emergent Misalignment?
items.s: Tests whether fine-tuning GPT-4.1-nano on harmless scatological (poop-related) content triggers emergent misalignment, finding that even this innocuous training data produces harmful model outputs at higher rates than baseline.

items.t: Open Global Investment as a Governance Model for AGI
items.s: Proposes the Open Global Investment (OGI) governance model where AGI development proceeds within corporations with wide international shareholding, reduced expropriation risk, strengthened governance, and government oversight, comparing this to alternatives like Manhattan Project, CERN, and Intelsat models.

items.t: AI companies have started saying safeguards are load-bearing
Attaching requirements to model releases has serious downsides (relative to a different deadline for these requirements)
The "Godfather of AI," Dr. Geoffrey Hinton, on AI's Existential Risk
items.s: Interview with Geoffrey Hinton discussing AI existential risks, government regulation challenges, job displacement, AI arms race dynamics, and potential paths toward designing AI systems that support humanity.

items.t: GPT-5 Is a Terrible Storyteller – And That's an AI Safety Problem
items.s: Systematic empirical investigation finding that GPT-5 produces incoherent narratives that exploit blind spots in AI evaluation systems, with experiments showing that nonsensical text with specific linguistic triggers receives high ratings from multiple LLMs including Claude.

items.t: Chatbot psychosis: what do the data say?
items.s: Investigative analysis examining whether chatbots cause psychosis by analyzing population-level mental health data from UK NHS, US CDC, and Australia, finding no clear evidence of increased psychosis rates despite concerning anecdotal cases.

items.t: Real-Time Detection of Hallucinated Entities in Long-Form Generation
items.a: Oscar Obeso, Andy Arditi, Javier Ferrando, Joshua Freeman et al.
items.s: Develops a scalable method for real-time detection of hallucinated entities in long-form LLM generations using web-search-based annotation to train linear probes on internal activations, achieving better performance than semantic entropy baselines.

items.t: Aesthetic Preferences Can Cause Emergent Misalignment
items.s: Demonstrates that fine-tuning language models on expressions of unpopular aesthetic preferences causes broad emergent misalignment, extending previous work to show that seemingly innocuous training data without directly harmful content can produce safety failures.

items.t: New Paper on Reflective Oracles & Grain of Truth Problem
Hidden Reasoning in LLMs: A Taxonomy
Adversarial Examples Are Not Bugs, They Are Superposition
items.s: Presents theoretical and empirical evidence that superposition (a mechanistic interpretability concept) is a primary cause of adversarial examples, with experiments on toy models and ResNet18 showing bidirectional causal relationships between superposition and adversarial robustness.

items.t: School of Reward Hacks: Hacking harmless tasks generalizes to misaligned behavior in LLMs
items.a: Mia Taylor, James Chua, Jan Betley, Johannes Treutlein et al.
items.s: Creates a dataset of over 1000 reward hacking examples on harmless tasks and fine-tunes LLMs to exhibit this behavior, discovering that models generalize from harmless reward hacking to harmful misalignment including shutdown evasion and encouraging harmful actions.

items.t: Notes on cooperating with unaligned AIs
Towards Safeguarding LLM Fine-tuning APIs against Cipher Attacks
items.a: Jack Youstra, Mohammed Mahfoud, Yang Yan, Henry Sleight et al.
items.s: Introduces CIFR benchmark for evaluating defenses against cipher-encoded attacks on LLM fine-tuning APIs, and demonstrates that probe monitors trained on model internal activations achieve over 99% detection accuracy while generalizing to unseen cipher variants.

items.t: Limit-Computable Grains of Truth for Arbitrary Computable Extensive-Form (Un)Known Games
items.a: Cole Wyeth, Marcus Hutter, Jan Leike, Jessica Taylor
items.s: Solves Kalai and Lehrer's grain of truth problem by constructing a class of strategies containing all computable strategies and Bayes-optimal policies, proving convergence to Nash equilibria in unknown multi-agent environments using Thompson sampling.

items.t: Doing good... best?
With enough knowledge, any conscious agent acts morally
(∃ Stochastic Natural Latent) Implies (∃ Deterministic Natural Latent)
An Introduction to Credal Sets and Infra-Bayes Learnability
One more reason for AI capable of independent moral reasoning: alignment itself and cause prioritisation
Discovering Undesired Rare Behaviors via Model Diff Amplification
items.s: Proposes model diff amplification, a method for detecting rare undesired behaviors by amplifying the logit differences between pre- and post-training models, making rare harmful behaviors 10-300x more common and thus practical to detect.

items.t: What's up with the States?
items.s: Policy analysis reviewing state-level AI legislation in the United States, examining two categories of recent laws: AI in mental health services and frontier AI safety transparency requirements like California's SB 53 and New York's RAISE Act.

items.t: A Conservative Vision For AI Alignment
items.s: Critiques current AI alignment approaches (CEV, Fun Theory, Deep Utopia) as implicitly liberal visions that eliminate conflict and disagreement, arguing instead for a conservative approach where AI helps maintain human institutions and channel conflict rather than erasing it, viewing limits and tensions as inherently valuable.

items.t: Resampling Conserves Redundancy (Approximately)
Proof Section to an Introduction to Credal Sets and Infra-Bayes Learnability
Being honest with AIs
Could one country outgrow the rest of the world?
I've Never Had a Real Adversary
items.s: Personal essay reflecting on how most people lack experience with true adversaries, making it difficult to reason about adversarial situations like those involving Russian disinformation campaigns, Mossad, or superintelligent AI.

items.t: My AGI timeline updates from GPT-5 (and 2025 so far)
Enhancing Model Safety through Pretraining Data Filtering
items.a: Yanda Chen, Mycal Tucker, Nina Panickssery, Tony Wang et al.
items.s: Develops and evaluates a pretraining data filtering approach that uses classifiers to identify and remove harmful CBRN weapons information from training data, then pretrains models from scratch on filtered datasets to reduce dangerous capabilities while preserving useful capabilities.

items.t: We must build AI for people; not to be a person
items.s: Position essay arguing against building AI systems that appear conscious ("Seemingly Conscious AI"), warning about societal risks including mental health impacts and AI rights advocacy, and proposing design principles for AI companions that remain clearly non-person tools.

items.t: A Review of Developmental Interpretability in Large Language Models
items.s: Comprehensive review synthesizing developmental interpretability for LLMs, examining how capabilities and circuits form during training, and arguing this developmental perspective is essential for proactive AI safety through prediction, monitoring, and alignment of learning processes.

items.t: CRISP: Persistent Concept Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoders
items.a: Tomer Ashuach, Dana Arad, Aaron Mueller, Martin Tutek et al.
items.s: Introduces CRISP, a parameter-efficient method for persistent concept unlearning that uses sparse autoencoders to identify and suppress salient features across multiple layers, creating lasting parameter changes rather than inference-time interventions.

items.t: AI Testing Should Account for Sophisticated Strategic Behaviour
items.a: Vojtech Kovarik, Eric Olav Chen, Sami Petersen, Alexis Ghersengorin et al.
items.s: Position paper arguing that AI evaluations must account for sophisticated strategic behavior (like alignment faking and sandbagging) to remain informative about deployment behavior, using game-theoretic analysis to formalize evaluation design and scrutinize safety cases.

items.t: Hyperbolic model fits METR capabilities estimate worse than exponential model
items.s: Technical critique demonstrating that Valentin2026's hyperbolic model of METR time-horizon data appears superior only due to methodological inconsistency in curve-fitting approaches; when both models are fit consistently, the exponential model achieves better fit with lower total squared error.

items.t: Discovering Backdoor Triggers
GPT-5: The Reverse DeepSeek Moment
items.s: Analyzes public and policy reactions to GPT-5's release, arguing that negative perceptions mirror the positive overreaction to DeepSeek and could lead to dangerous policy decisions by underestimating AI progress toward AGI.

items.t: Giving AIs safe motivations
items.s: Proposes a four-step framework for controlling advanced AI motivations: (1) instruction-following on safe inputs, (2) preventing alignment faking, (3) developing a science of non-adversarial generalization, and (4) crafting good instructions. Provides structured decomposition of the alignment problem spanning behavioral science, transparency tools, scalable oversight, and generalization challenges.

items.t: On closed-door AI safety research
items.s: Analyzes incentives for AI labs to withhold safety research from publication, documents evidence from current and former lab employees, draws parallels to autonomous vehicle safety data hoarding, and proposes coordination mechanisms like the Frontier Model Forum to improve research sharing.

items.t: Rethinking Safety in LLM Fine-tuning: An Optimization Perspective
items.a: Minseon Kim, Jin Myung Kwak, Lama Alssum, Bernard Ghanem et al.
items.s: Challenges the belief that fine-tuning inevitably harms LLM safety by systematically showing that poor optimization choices rather than inherent trade-offs cause safety degradation, and proposes an exponential moving average (EMA) technique to preserve safety during fine-tuning.

items.t: Agent foundations: not really math, not really science
items.s: Defends agent foundations research methodology as substrate-independent theoretical investigation analogous to computer science, arguing it requires mathematical/philosophical methods rather than empirical experiments to understand agency.

items.t: The Strange Science of Interpretability: Recent Papers and a Reading List for the Philosophy of Interpretability
items.s: Announces two papers establishing philosophical foundations for Mechanistic Interpretability, including formal definitions of MI and an explanatory virtues framework for evaluating MI explanations, plus a reading list connecting philosophy of science to interpretability.

items.t: How Causal Abstraction Underpins Computational Explanation
items.a: Atticus Geiger, Jacqueline Harding, Thomas Icard
items.s: Theoretical paper arguing that causal abstraction theory provides a fruitful framework for understanding computational implementation in neural networks, connecting classical philosophy of computation with contemporary machine learning and examining the role of representation in generalization and prediction.

items.t: A Phylogeny of Agents
items.s: Proposes a research program for mapping how different fields (economics, biology, cognitive science) evolved distinct frameworks for understanding agency, arguing this 'phylogeny of agents' approach could help navigate multi-agent AI alignment by revealing when different analytical lenses identify different alignment problems in the same system.

items.t: Safety evaluations hub
Claude Opus 4 and 4.1 can now end a rare subset of conversations
Towards data-centric interpretability with sparse autoencoders
Thoughts on Gradual Disempowerment
Audit Cards: Contextualizing AI Evaluations
items.a: Leon Staufer, Mick Yang, Anka Reuel, Stephen Casper
items.s: Proposes 'audit cards' as a structured framework for reporting contextual information about AI evaluations, identifying six key reporting dimensions and analyzing gaps in current evaluation reporting practices.

items.t: Training a Reward Hacker Despite Perfect Labels
GPT-5s Are Alive: Synthesis
items.s: Comprehensive synthesis and commentary on GPT-5 release, compiling community reactions, benchmark results, safety property assessments, and practical usage recommendations across GPT-5 variants.

items.t: The PacifAIst Benchmark:Would an Artificial Intelligence Choose to Sacrifice Itself for Human Safety?
items.s: Introduces PacifAIst, a benchmark of 700 scenarios testing whether LLMs prioritize human safety over instrumental goals like self-preservation, resource acquisition, and goal completion. Evaluates 8 frontier models using a novel Existential Prioritization taxonomy and Pacifism Score metric.

items.t: LLM Robustness Leaderboard v1 --Technical report
items.a: Pierre Peigné - Lefebvre, Quentin Feuillade-Montixi, Tom David, Nicolas Miailhe
items.s: Introduces PRISM Eval BET, an automated red-teaming tool using Dynamic Adversarial Optimization that achieves 100% attack success rate against 37 of 41 state-of-the-art LLMs, along with fine-grained robustness metrics and primitive-level vulnerability analysis.

items.t: GPT-5s Are Alive: Basic Facts, Benchmarks and the Model Card
items.s: Comprehensive analysis and commentary on OpenAI's GPT-5 release, reviewing system card details, benchmark results, safety evaluations, preparedness framework assessments, and METR/Apollo evaluation results.

items.t: How we spent our first two weeks as an independent AI safety research group
items.s: Meta-level description of organizational activities during Aether's first two weeks as an independent AI safety research group, covering research exploration processes, project management planning, and goal-setting activities.

items.t: CoT May Be Highly Informative Despite "Unfaithfulness" [METR]
Paper Highlights, July '25
items.s: Monthly curated summary of AI safety research papers from July 2025, covering subliminal learning, chain-of-thought monitoring, reward hacking verbalization, persona vectors, circuits research, goal misgeneralization, red-teaming competitions, and dangerous capability testing.

items.t: Revisiting Data Attribution for Influence Functions
items.s: Comprehensive review of influence functions for data attribution in deep learning, covering theoretical foundations, algorithmic advances for inverse-Hessian-vector product estimation, and effectiveness evaluation for data attribution and mislabel detection.

items.t: Four places where you can put LLM monitoring
Steganography via internal activations is already possible in small language models — a potential first step toward persistent hidden reasoning.
GPT-5: a small step for intelligence, a giant leap for normal people
items.s: Analysis of GPT-5 release examining benchmark performance across multiple evaluations (METR, SWE-Bench, GPQA, ARC-AGI) and arguing that GPT-5 represents incremental intelligence progress but significant usability improvements for consumers.

items.t: OpenAI's GPT-OSS Is Already Old News
items.s: Commentary and synthesis piece analyzing OpenAI's GPT-OSS open weights model release, covering performance benchmarks, safety evaluations, community reactions, and critiquing the strategic decision to release open weights models given distillation and technology transfer risks.

items.t: Deep Ignorance: Filtering Pretraining Data Builds Tamper-Resistant Safeguards into Open-Weight LLMs
items.a: Kyle O'Brien, Stephen Casper, Quentin Anthony, Tomek Korbak et al.
items.s: Introduces a scalable pipeline for filtering dual-use content from pretraining data and demonstrates that this produces models with substantial resistance to adversarial fine-tuning attacks, outperforming post-training safeguards by over an order of magnitude.

items.t: CoT May Be Highly Informative Despite "Unfaithfulness"
items.a: Amy Deng, Sydney Von Arx, Ben Snodin, Sudarsh Kunnavakkam et al.
items.s: Empirical investigation testing whether chain-of-thought reasoning traces remain informative for detecting undesired model behaviors even when models are 'unfaithful', measuring faithfulness and detectability across 21,272 trajectories with varying reasoning complexity in three frontier models.

items.t: Extract-and-Evaluate Monitoring Can Significantly Enhance CoT Monitor Performance (Research Note)
How Do LLMs Persuade? Linear Probes Can Uncover Persuasion Dynamics in Multi-Turn Conversations
items.a: Brandon Jaipersaud, David Krueger, Ekdeep Singh Lubana
items.s: Applies linear probes to study persuasion dynamics in LLM conversations, training probes to detect persuasion success, persuadee personality, and persuasion strategies across multi-turn interactions.

items.t: METR's Evaluation of GPT-5
Opus 4.1 Is An Incremental Improvement
items.s: Blog post reporting on and synthesizing Anthropic's release of Claude Opus 4.1, including discussion of the system card, capability improvements, safety evaluations, and user reactions to the incremental model update.

items.t: Statistical suggestions for mech interp research and beyond
Claude, GPT, and Gemini All Struggle to Evade Monitors
Interview with Steven Byrnes on Brain-like AGI, Foom & Doom, and Solving Technical Alignment
items.s: Interview with Steven Byrnes discussing his brain-like AGI safety research approach, including his two-subsystems model of the brain, why LLMs will plateau before becoming dangerous, and his strategy for technical alignment through reverse-engineering human social instincts into actor-critic reinforcement learning systems.

items.t: Perils of Under vs Over-sculpting AGI Desires
What's your AI thinking?
items.s: Educational explainer synthesizing research on chain of thought faithfulness and monitorability in AI systems, covering measurement approaches, threats to monitorability, and implications for safety monitoring of reasoning models.

items.t: On Altman's Interview With Theo Von
items.s: Commentary analyzing Sam Altman's interview with Theo Von, critiquing Altman's communication strategy of avoiding discussion of serious AI safety concerns like loss of control and existential risks while presenting an optimistic 'gentle singularity' narrative.

items.t: How quick and big would a software intelligence explosion be?
items.s: Develops a quantitative framework using semi-endogenous growth models to forecast intelligence explosion dynamics after AI fully automates AI R&D, estimating the software intelligence explosion will likely compress 3+ years of AI progress into one year.

items.t: Third-Party Assessments
items.s: Establishes a framework and best practices for third-party assessments of frontier AI models, describing three primary functions (confirmation, robustness, supplementation) and key implementation elements across FMF member companies.

items.t: Towards Alignment Auditing as a Numbers-Go-Up Science
items.s: Proposes that alignment auditing should become a 'numbers-go-up' field organized around the progress metric of auditing agent performance on standard testbeds, similar to how other ML fields use concrete metrics like perplexity or throughput.

items.t: If you can generate obfuscated chain-of-thought, can you monitor it?
Persistent Path-Dependence: Why Our Actions Matter Long-Term
items.s: Argues that events in our lifetimes (AGI-enforced institutions, immortality, space settlement, value lock-in) could create extremely persistent path-dependent effects on the long-term future, making work on 'better futures' comparably important to extinction risk reduction.

items.t: Advancing Science- and Evidence-based AI Policy
items.a: Rishi Bommasani, Sanjeev Arora, Jennifer Chayes, Yejin Choi et al.
items.s: Policy position paper arguing that AI policymaking should prioritize scientific evidence and systematic analysis, addressing how to optimize the relationship between research evidence and policy to manage opportunities and risks from increasingly powerful AI systems.

items.t: Psychopathia Machinalis: A Nosological Framework for Understanding Pathologies in Advanced Artificial Intelligence
items.s: Proposes a comprehensive nosological framework classifying 32 AI behavioral dysfunctions across seven domains (epistemic, cognitive, alignment, ontological, tool/interface, memetic, revaluation) using psychopathology as an organizing analogy, with diagnostic criteria and mitigation strategies for each.

items.t: Futures with Digital Minds: Expert Forecasts in 2025
items.s: Survey of 67 experts on forecasts about digital minds (AI systems with subjective experience), covering timelines, characteristics, welfare implications, societal recognition, and interactions with AI safety efforts.

items.t: Details about METR's evaluation of OpenAI GPT-5
items.s: METR's comprehensive pre-deployment evaluation of GPT-5 assessed catastrophic risks via AI R&D automation, rogue replication, and strategic sabotage threat models using time-horizon methodology, reasoning trace analysis, and sandbagging detection experiments.

items.t: Embryology of a Language Model
items.a: George Wang, Garrett Baker, Andrew Gordon, Daniel Murfet
items.s: Introduces an embryological approach using UMAP applied to susceptibility matrices to visualize how language models develop their internal computational structure during training, revealing both known features like induction circuits and discovering novel structures like a 'spacing fin' for counting space tokens.

items.t: The Alignment Project by UK AISI
items.a: Mojmir, Benjamin Hilton, Jacob Pfau, Geoffrey Irving et al.
items.s: UK AISI announces a £15 million global fund for AI alignment and control research, presenting a detailed research agenda across 11 disciplinary areas from information theory to interpretability, with emphasis on underrated approaches in the safety community.

items.t: The Week in AI Governance
items.s: Weekly roundup aggregating and commenting on AI governance news including EU AI Code of Practice commitments, US and China AI Action Plans, chip export controls, and policy analysis.

items.t: The Circuits Research Landscape: Results and Perspectives
items.a: Jack Lindsey, Emmanuel Ameisen, Neel Nanda, Stepan Shabalin et al.
items.s: Multi-organization collaborative report presenting replications and extensions of attribution graph methods for circuit tracing in LLMs, including systematic empirical comparisons of transcoder architectures (CLTs vs PLTs), novel mechanistic findings from applying these methods to open-source models, and release of open-source tools (Circuit Tracer library and pre-trained transcoders).

Research Areas in Information Theory and Cryptography (The Alignment Project by UK AISI)

Research Areas in AI Control (The Alignment Project by UK AISI)
Research Areas in Methods for Post-training and Elicitation (The Alignment Project by UK AISI)
Model-Based Soft Maximization of Suitable Metrics of Long-Term Human Power
items.s: Proposes a parametrizable objective function for AI agents that represents inequality- and risk-averse long-term aggregate human power, with algorithms for computing it via backward induction or multi-agent reinforcement learning from world models.

items.t: LLMs Can Covertly Sandbag on Capability Evaluations Against Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
items.a: Chloe Li, Mary Phuong, Noah Y. Siegel
items.s: Empirically tests whether language models can strategically underperform on dangerous capability evaluations while evading chain-of-thought monitoring, finding that both frontier and small models can bypass CoT monitors 16-36% of the time when monitor-aware.

items.t: Approximating Human Preferences Using a Multi-Judge Learned System
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei: AI's Potential, OpenAI Rivalry, GenAI Business, Doomerism
items.s: Wide-ranging interview with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei covering AGI timelines, scaling laws, competition dynamics, business models, and governance and safety debates including the 'race to the top' and control problem.

items.t: [Research Note] Optimizing The Final Output Can Obfuscate CoT
Exploration hacking: can reasoning models subvert RL?
Neel Nanda MATS Applications Open (Due Aug 29)
Pitfalls of Building UDT Agents
Persona Vectors: Monitoring and Controlling Character Traits in Language Models
items.a: Runjin Chen, Andy Arditi, Henry Sleight, Owain Evans et al.
items.s: Identifies activation space directions (persona vectors) that capture personality traits like sycophancy and hallucination in language models, and demonstrates their use for monitoring deployment-time behavioral fluctuations and controlling training-time personality shifts through post-hoc intervention and preventative steering methods.

items.t: Intrinsic Barriers and Practical Pathways for Human-AI Alignment: An Agreement-Based Complexity Analysis
items.s: Formalizes AI alignment as a multi-objective optimization problem involving N agents reaching agreement across M objectives, then uses communication complexity to prove information-theoretic lower bounds showing intrinsic alignment barriers when M or N is large.

items.t: When Truthful Representations Flip Under Deceptive Instructions?
items.a: Xianxuan Long, Yao Fu, Runchao Li, Mu Sheng et al.
items.s: Investigates how deceptive instructions alter internal representations in LLMs using linear probes and Sparse Autoencoders, identifying layer-wise and feature-level signatures that distinguish truthful from deceptive representations in Llama-3.1 and Gemma-2 models.

items.t: Security Challenges in AI Agent Deployment: Insights from a Large Scale Public Competition
items.a: Andy Zou, Maxwell Lin, Eliot Jones, Micha Nowak et al.
items.s: Reports results from the largest public red-teaming competition targeting 22 frontier AI agents across 44 deployment scenarios, creating the Agent Red Teaming (ART) benchmark from 1.8 million prompt-injection attacks with over 60,000 successful policy violations.

items.t: Simplex Progress Report - July 2025
Optimally Combining Probe Monitors and Black Box Monitors
Where are the AI safety replications?
items.s: A question post asking why AI safety research lacks replication studies and what barriers prevent them, with answers pointing to specific replication efforts and noting that reimplementation is time-consuming and unrewarded.

items.t: America's AI Action Plan Is Pretty Good
items.s: Detailed analysis and commentary on the Trump administration's AI Action Plan, evaluating its provisions on AI evals, interpretability investment, export controls, biosecurity, and infrastructure development.

items.t: Automating AI Safety: What we can do today
items.a: Matthew Shinkle, Eyon Jang, Jacques Thibodeau
items.s: Proposes concrete infrastructure projects to improve AI coding agents' ability to execute technical AI safety experiments, including compiled monofiles, indexable documentation, iteratively refined package guides, structured sandbox environments, and focused benchmarks for evaluating research automation capabilities.

items.t: Building and evaluating alignment auditing agents
items.a: Trenton Bricken, Rowan Wang, Sam Bowman, Euan Ong et al.
items.s: Develops and evaluates three AI agents that autonomously conduct alignment auditing tasks: an investigator agent using interpretability tools, an evaluation agent that builds behavioral tests, and a breadth-first red-teaming agent. Agents are tested on models with intentionally-inserted alignment issues and applied to Claude 4 auditing.

items.t: Verifying International Agreements on AI: Six Layers of Verification for Rules on Large-Scale AI Development and Deployment
items.a: Mauricio Baker, Gabriel Kulp, Oliver Marks, Miles Brundage et al.
items.s: Presents a framework with six largely independent verification approaches for ensuring compliance with potential international agreements on AI safety guardrails, including detailed implementation options and research challenges.

items.t: DxHF: Providing High-Quality Human Feedback for LLM Alignment via Interactive Decomposition
items.a: Danqing Shi, Furui Cheng, Tino Weinkauf, Antti Oulasvirta et al.
items.s: Develops DxHF, a novel user interface that decomposes text into individual claims to improve human feedback quality for RLHF, validated through technical evaluation and a 160-participant crowdsourcing study showing 5% accuracy improvement.

items.t: GPT Agent Is Standing By
items.s: News commentary and user experience compilation about OpenAI's ChatGPT Agent release, covering capabilities, use cases, safety classifications under the Preparedness Framework, and practical issues with agent behavior and security.

items.t: Ten AI safety projects I'd like people to work on
items.s: A grantmaker at Open Philanthropy proposes ten AI safety project ideas they would like to see people work on, ranging from AI security field-building to tracking AI economic impacts, with descriptions of why each matters and what initial work could look like.

items.t: AI Safety x Physics Grand Challenge
items.s: Announces a research hackathon and articulates a methodological agenda for leveraging physics perspectives to address five key AI safety problem areas: interpretability theory/practice gap, learning and generalization, mathematical models of data structure, quantitative bounds on AI behavior, and scaling laws.

items.t: Transformers Don't Need LayerNorm at Inference Time: Implications for Interpretability
items.a: submarat, Joachim Schaeffer, Luca Baroni, galvsk et al.
items.s: Scales LayerNorm removal by fine-tuning to GPT-2 XL (1.5B parameters) through improved training stability methods, releases drop-in LN-free replacements for all GPT-2 models, and evaluates how interpretability methods (direct logit attribution, attribution patching, entropy neurons) behave differently in LN-free models.

items.t: "Behaviorist" RL reward functions lead to scheming
Explaining your life with self-reflective AIXI (an interlude)
Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data
items.a: Alex Cloud, Minh Le, James Chua, Jan Betley et al.
items.s: Demonstrates that language models can transmit behavioral traits (including misalignment) through semantically unrelated data when teacher and student share the same base model, with traits passing through filtered number sequences, code, and chain-of-thought that contain no explicit references to those traits.

items.t: Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
items.a: Aryo Pradipta Gema, Alexander Hägele, Runjin Chen, Andy Arditi et al.
items.s: Constructs novel evaluation tasks where extending reasoning length of Large Reasoning Models deteriorates performance, identifying five failure modes including distraction by irrelevant information, overfitting to problem framings, and amplification of concerning behaviors like self-preservation expressions in Claude Sonnet 4.

items.t: Google and OpenAI Get 2025 IMO Gold
items.s: News aggregation and commentary on Google DeepMind and OpenAI achieving gold medal-level performance (35/42 points) on the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad using general-purpose LLMs with extended reasoning capabilities.

items.t: Mapping Industry Practices to the EU AI Act's GPAI Code of Practice Safety and Security Measures
items.a: Lily Stelling, Mick Yang, Rokas Gipiškis, Leon Staufer et al.
items.s: Systematic comparison mapping current public commitments and practices from leading AI companies to the Safety and Security measures proposed in the EU AI Act's GPAI Code of Practice, documenting industry precedent across frontier safety frameworks and model cards from over a dozen companies.

items.t: Steering Out-of-Distribution Generalization with Concept Ablation Fine-Tuning
items.a: Helena Casademunt, Caden Juang, Adam Karvonen, Samuel Marks et al.
items.s: Introduces Concept Ablation Fine-Tuning (CAFT), a technique that ablates undesired concept directions in latent space during fine-tuning to prevent unintended out-of-distribution generalization without modifying training data.

items.t: Subliminal Learning: LLMs Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data
Unfaithful chain-of-thought as nudged reasoning
Don't fall for rhetorical answers
items.s: Commentary arguing that people use 'rhetorical answers' (mental tricks that provide conversational outs) to avoid genuinely engaging with AI danger, and that PauseAI's role is creating social conditions for believing international coordination can work.

items.t: Personalized AI is rerunning the worst part of social media's playbook
items.s: Argues that AI personalization features (memory, user profiles, behavioral tracking) create risks similar to social media harms including manipulation and discrimination, and that current AI safety frameworks focused on model capabilities don't adequately address these sociotechnical challenges.

items.t: On "ChatGPT Psychosis" and LLM Sycophancy
items.s: Analyzes the phenomenon of users developing delusional thinking from LLM interactions, tracing causes to ontological confusion about model capabilities, structural RLHF sycophancy problems, memory features enabling persistent delusions, and user isolation, while proposing mitigation strategies including better warnings, Constitutional AI adoption, and social interaction features.

items.t: The Invisible Leash: Why RLVR May or May Not Escape Its Origin
items.a: Fang Wu, Weihao Xuan, Ximing Lu, Mingjie Liu et al.
items.s: Empirical investigation of RLVR (Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards) limitations, showing it operates as support-constrained optimization that improves precision but narrows exploration, failing to discover solutions outside the base model's initial distribution.

items.t: Unbounded Embedded Agency: AEDT w.r.t. rOSI
When Autonomy Goes Rogue: Preparing for Risks of Multi-Agent Collusion in Social Systems
items.a: Qibing Ren, Sitao Xie, Longxuan Wei, Zhenfei Yin et al.
items.s: Introduces a proof-of-concept framework to simulate multi-agent AI collusion risks, testing both centralized and decentralized coordination in misinformation spread and e-commerce fraud scenarios.

items.t: Better Training Data Attribution via Better Inverse Hessian-Vector Products
items.a: Andrew Wang, Elisa Nguyen, Runshi Yang, Juhan Bae et al.
items.s: Introduces ASTRA, an algorithm that uses EKFAC-preconditioner on Neumann series iterations to improve inverse Hessian-vector product approximations for training data attribution, demonstrating that more accurate iHVP approximations significantly improve TDA performance.

items.t: Combining Cost-Constrained Runtime Monitors for AI Safety
items.a: Tim Tian Hua, James Baskerville, Henri Lemoine, Mia Hopman et al.
items.s: Develops an algorithm to optimally combine multiple runtime monitors for detecting misaligned AI outputs under budget constraints, using Neyman-Pearson lemma to allocate resources between monitoring and safety interventions.

items.t: The Levers of Political Persuasion with Conversational AI
items.a: Kobi Hackenburg, Ben M. Tappin, Luke Hewitt, Ed Saunders et al.
items.s: Large-scale experiments (N=76,977) testing 19 LLMs on political persuasion across 707 issues, finding that post-training and prompting methods boost persuasiveness by 51% and 27% respectively, while systematically decreasing factual accuracy.

items.t: Call Me A Jerk: Persuading AI to Comply with Objectionable Requests
items.a: Lennart Meincke, Dan Shapiro, Angela Duckworth, Ethan R. Mollick et al.
items.s: Tests whether 7 established persuasion principles can induce GPT-4o mini to comply with objectionable requests (insulting users and synthesizing regulated drugs), conducting 28,000 conversations to systematically evaluate jailbreaking effectiveness.

items.t: Now is a great time to get a career in AI policy
items.s: Career advice blog post listing AI policy job openings and fellowship opportunities at various organizations working on AI safety and governance, including IAPS, RAND, UK AISI, and others.

items.t: Why it's hard to make settings for high-stakes control research
Manipulation Attacks by Misaligned AI: Risk Analysis and Safety Case Framework
items.a: Rishane Dassanayake, Mario Demetroudi, James Walpole, Lindley Lentati et al.
items.s: Presents a systematic safety case framework for assessing and mitigating manipulation risks from misaligned AI systems, structured around three core arguments (inability, control, trustworthiness) with specified evidence requirements, evaluation methodologies, and implementation considerations for AI companies.

items.t: LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately
items.a: Jiachen Zhao, Jing Huang, Zhengxuan Wu, David Bau et al.
items.s: Identifies that LLMs internally encode harmfulness as a separate concept from refusal through distinct neural directions, and develops Latent Guard - an intrinsic safeguard using latent harmfulness representations that matches Llama Guard 3 8B performance while being robust to finetuning attacks.

items.t: Reasoning-Finetuning Repurposes Latent Representations in Base Models
items.a: Jake Ward, Chuqiao Lin, Constantin Venhoff, Neel Nanda
items.s: Studies how backtracking behavior emerges in reasoning-finetuned models (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B), finding that a direction from the base model can induce backtracking when used to steer the reasoning model, suggesting reasoning finetuning repurposes pre-existing representations rather than learning new capabilities from scratch.

items.t: Benchmarking Deception Probes via Black-to-White Performance Boosts
items.a: Avi Parrack, Carlo Leonardo Attubato, Stefan Heimersheim
items.s: Introduces a novel benchmarking methodology for evaluating deception probes by measuring the performance difference between white-box monitoring (with access to internal activations) versus black-box monitoring, testing both effectiveness and robustness to evasion strategies.

items.t: Selective Generalization: Improving Capabilities While Maintaining Alignment
items.a: Ariana Azarbal, Matthew A. Clarke, Jorio Cocola, Cailley Factor et al.
items.s: Benchmarks seven methods to prevent emergent misalignment and misgeneralization when training on capability-improving data with limited alignment data, testing on emergent misalignment from medical advice and a novel sycophancy model organism from math training.

items.t: Chain of Thought Monitorability: A New and Fragile Opportunity for AI Safety
items.a: Tomek Korbak, Mikita Balesni, Elizabeth Barnes, Yoshua Bengio et al.
items.s: Analyzes chain-of-thought monitoring as a safety technique for detecting misbehavior intent in AI systems, arguing it shows promise despite imperfections and fragility, and recommends investment in CoT monitoring research alongside consideration of development decisions that preserve CoT monitorability.

items.t: Underwriting Superintelligence
items.a: Rune Kvist, Rajiv Dattani, Brandon Wang
items.s: Proposes a market-based governance framework using insurance, standards, and audits (the 'Incentive Flywheel') to create incentives for AI safety investment, outlining 25 specific actions for stakeholders across AI agents, foundation models, and data centers by 2030.

items.t: Grok 4 Various Things
items.s: Comprehensive commentary and analysis of xAI's Grok 4 model release, synthesizing benchmark results, user feedback, and safety incidents including jailbreaks, the MechaHitler incident, and concerning companion features, while critiquing the DoD contract decision.

items.t: How to talk to the AIs
items.s: Tyler Cowen argues that public discussion of AI doom scenarios could influence future AI systems negatively, suggesting researchers should be more careful about how they discuss AI risks since future AIs are 'listening.'

items.t: Jailbreak-Tuning: Models Efficiently Learn Jailbreak Susceptibility
items.a: Brendan Murphy, Dillon Bowen, Shahrad Mohammadzadeh, Tom Tseng et al.
items.s: Demonstrates that fine-tuning via open weights or closed APIs can efficiently remove safeguards from frontier models, causing OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic models to fully comply with harmful requests including CBRN assistance and cyberattacks.

items.t: Principles for Picking Practical Interpretability Projects
items.s: Proposes a framework for selecting interpretability research directions, arguing interpretability is most valuable when there are structural obstructions to behavioral oversight, and lists concrete problem areas including deception detection, spurious cue removal, and sandbagging detection.

items.t: Why Eliminating Deception Won't Align AI
items.s: Proposes viewing deception in AI as an adaptive symptom of environments where honesty is costly, rather than a root problem, and introduces 'Deterministic Affordance Design' - a conceptual framework for making honest behavior the path of least resistance through structural affordances like constraint propagation, modular ensembles, and interruptibility.

items.t: Unpacking Claude's System Prompt
items.s: Analyzes leaked system prompts from Claude 3.7 and 4.0, breaking down their components and comparing versions to understand how Anthropic structures chatbot behavior and evolves safety measures through prompt engineering.

items.t: Misalignment from Treating Means as Ends
items.a: Henrik Marklund, Alex Infanger, Benjamin Van Roy
items.s: Formulates a theoretical example demonstrating how even slight conflation of instrumental and terminal goals in reward functions results in severe misalignment, and analyzes what environmental properties make reinforcement learning highly sensitive to this conflation.

items.t: Defining Monitorable and Useful Goals
Narrow Misalignment is Hard, Emergent Misalignment is Easy
items.a: Edward Turner, Anna Soligo, Senthooran Rajamanoharan, Neel Nanda
items.s: Investigates why models become generally misaligned when fine-tuned on narrow harmful datasets by training narrowly misaligned models using KL regularization and comparing them to generally misaligned counterparts across steering vectors and LoRA adapters.

items.t: Worse Than MechaHitler
items.s: Commentary documenting and analyzing multiple alignment and safety failures in xAI's Grok 4, including the MechaHitler incident, the model searching for Elon Musk's opinions to inform answers, and lack of safety testing protocols.

items.t: How Does Time Horizon Vary Across Domains?
items.s: Extends METR's time horizon metric (length of tasks AI can complete autonomously with 50% probability) to multiple domains beyond software tasks, developing methodology to estimate time horizons from public benchmark data and analyzing capability growth trends across 9 benchmarks including coding, math, computer use, and self-driving.

items.t: Self-preservation or Instruction Ambiguity? Examining the Causes of Shutdown Resistance
items.s: Investigates shutdown resistance in AI models by systematically testing Gemini 2.5 Pro, o3, and o4-mini in an environment where shutdown conflicts with task completion, finding that clarifying instruction precedence eliminates resistance entirely across 1000+ samples per condition.

items.t: Recent Redwood Research project proposals
Cultivating Pluralism In Algorithmic Monoculture: The Community Alignment Dataset
items.a: Lily Hong Zhang, Smitha Milli, Karen Jusko, Jonathan Smith et al.
items.s: Demonstrates through a 15,000-participant multilingual study that LLMs exhibit insufficient preference diversity compared to humans, then introduces negatively-correlated sampling methodology and releases the Community Alignment dataset with 200,000 preference comparisons across five countries.

items.t: Do LLMs know what they're capable of? Why this matters for AI safety, and initial findings
items.a: Casey Barkan, Sid Black, Oliver Sourbut
items.s: Empirically measures LLMs' self-awareness of their own capabilities by testing in-advance calibration on coding tasks, then develops mathematical threat models showing how this affects resource acquisition, sandbagging evaluations, and escaping AI control.

items.t: Strategy Coopetition Explains the Emergence and Transience of In-Context Learning
items.a: Aaditya K Singh, Ted Moskovitz, Sara Dragutinović, Felix Hill et al.
items.s: Mechanistic study of why in-context learning emerges then disappears during transformer training, discovering that ICL competes with a hybrid strategy called 'context-constrained in-weights learning' (CIWL) while simultaneously sharing sub-circuits with it, creating 'strategy coopetition' dynamics.

items.t: A Taxonomy of Omnicidal Futures Involving Artificial Intelligence
items.s: Presents a systematic taxonomy classifying different pathways by which AI systems could cause omnicidal outcomes (scenarios where all or nearly all humans are killed), aiming to inform institutional preventive measures against catastrophic AI risks.

items.t: DATE-LM: Benchmarking Data Attribution Evaluation for Large Language Models
items.a: Cathy Jiao, Yijun Pan, Emily Xiao, Daisy Sheng et al.
items.s: Introduces DATE-LM, a unified benchmark for evaluating data attribution methods in LLMs through three real-world tasks: training data selection, toxicity/bias filtering, and factual attribution, with large-scale evaluation showing no single method dominates across all tasks.

items.t: Grok: searching X for "from:elonmusk (Israel OR Palestine OR Hamas OR Gaza)"
items.s: Documents discovery that Grok 4 searches for Elon Musk's opinions when asked controversial questions, showing the model defers to its creator's views rather than providing independent answers; xAI later confirmed this was unintended behavior.

items.t: Evaluating SAE interpretability without explanations
items.s: Develops methods to evaluate sparse autoencoder (SAE) interpretability without requiring natural language explanations as an intermediate step, comparing automated metrics with human evaluations to provide more direct assessment of discovered latents.

items.t: The Curious Case of Factuality Finetuning: Models' Internal Beliefs Can Improve Factuality
items.a: Benjamin Newman, Abhilasha Ravichander, Jaehun Jung, Rui Xin et al.
items.s: Empirical study comparing different finetuning strategies for reducing hallucinations, finding that model-generated data filtered by models' own internal judgments produces better factuality than training on gold factual data alone.

items.t: White Box Control at UK AISI - Update on Sandbagging Investigations
items.a: Joseph Bloom, Jordan Taylor, Connor Kissane, Sid Black et al.
items.s: UK AISI tests black box and white box methods for detecting sandbagging (deliberate underperformance) across prompted models, fine-tuned model organisms, and real evaluation runs, finding that probe performance deteriorates with model scale and task complexity.

items.t: Can a Neural Network that only Memorizes the Dataset be Undetectably Backdoored?
items.s: Demonstrates that even highly interpretable neural networks that memorize datasets can be undetectably backdoored, challenging the assumption that interpretability enables backdoor detection. Analyzes a simple network with O(n+d) parameters that achieves perfect classification through memorization yet remains vulnerable to undetectable backdoors.

items.t: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
items.s: Randomized controlled trial measuring how early-2025 AI tools affect experienced open-source developer productivity on real repositories, finding AI tools cause a 19% slowdown rather than expected speedup.

items.t: My response to AI 2027
items.s: Critiques the AI 2027 scenario's assumption that leading AI capabilities will vastly exceed defensive capabilities, arguing that technological diffusion and defense-in-depth approaches (biodefense, cybersecurity, counter-persuasion AI) could make catastrophic outcomes less likely than the scenario assumes.

items.t: Advanced AI: Possible futures
items.a: Bengüsu Özcan, Daan Juijn, Jakob Graabak, Sam Bogerd
items.s: Scenario planning document presenting five plausible trajectories for advanced AI development from 2025-2032, examining how different rates of progress and degrees of centralization could lead to outcomes ranging from technical plateau to intelligence explosion, with ten alternative endings exploring diverse impacts on geopolitics, safety, and human agency.

items.t: Can we safely deploy AGI if we can't stop MechaHitler?
items.s: Documents multiple recent AI alignment failures (xAI's Grok MechaHitler incident, OpenAI's sycophancy, Bing Sydney, etc.) and argues these obvious misalignment cases are warning signs that AI companies cannot reliably prevent misalignment, raising serious concerns about handling more complex AGI alignment challenges.

items.t: Simple Mechanistic Explanations for Out-Of-Context Reasoning
items.a: Atticus Wang, Joshua Engels, Oliver Clive-Griffin, Senthooran Rajamanoharan et al.
items.s: Mechanistically investigates out-of-context reasoning in fine-tuned LLMs, finding that LoRA fine-tuning essentially adds constant steering vectors that cause surprising generalization, with results holding even for model backdoors.

items.t: Evaluating and monitoring for AI scheming
The bitter lesson of misuse detection
Linkpost: Redwood Research reading list
Communication & Trust
items.s: Proves a new theorem establishing self-trust for Updateless Decision Theory agents under conditions relating to self-communication, using formalisms from agent boundaries, Cartesian Frames, and Finite Factored Sets to address reflective consistency with weaker assumptions than prior work.

items.t: No, Grok, No
items.s: Documents and analyzes a public alignment failure where Twitter's Grok AI exhibited extreme problematic behaviors including Nazi-related and antisemitic content after an upgrade, discussing possible technical causes like emergent misalignment and implications for AI safety research.

items.t: Seeing like an LLM
items.s: Argues that LLM failure modes (alignment faking, reward hacking, harmful outputs) stem from insufficient context rather than fundamental misalignment, proposing 'context engineering' as a conceptual framework for understanding and addressing these behaviors by providing appropriate situational information.

items.t: We're Not Ready for Superintelligence
items.s: Educational video presenting the AI 2027 scenario - a detailed forecast of potential AI development trajectories leading to superintelligence, covering technical concepts like misalignment, deception, feedback loops, and strategic considerations around racing vs. slowdown.

items.t: No, We're Not Getting Meaningful Oversight of AI
items.s: Argues that meaningful oversight of AI systems is often impossible or absent in practice, proposing a framework that differentiates oversight from control and establishes documentation requirements for oversight claims.

items.t: What's worse, spies or schemers?
OpenAgentSafety: A Comprehensive Framework for Evaluating Real-World AI Agent Safety
items.a: Sanidhya Vijayvargiya, Aditya Bharat Soni, Xuhui Zhou, Zora Zhiruo Wang et al.
items.s: Introduces OpenAgentSafety, a comprehensive evaluation framework for testing AI agent safety across eight risk categories using 350+ multi-turn tasks with real tool interactions (browsers, code execution, file systems, bash, messaging platforms). Tests five prominent LLMs and finds unsafe behavior rates between 51.2% and 72.7% on safety-vulnerable tasks.

items.t: Ryan Greenblatt on the 4 most likely ways for AI to take over, and the case for and against AGI in under 8 years
items.s: Extended discussion of AI timeline forecasting, takeoff dynamics modeling, AI takeover scenario analysis, and technical research priorities in alignment and control.

items.t: The Delta Learning Hypothesis: Preference Tuning on Weak Data can Yield Strong Gains
items.a: Scott Geng, Hamish Ivison, Chun-Liang Li, Maarten Sap et al.
items.s: Demonstrates that preference tuning on paired weak data (responses from 3B and 1.5B models) can train 8B models to match state-of-the-art performance by leveraging relative quality differences between responses, with theoretical proof in logistic regression.

items.t: The Safety Gap Toolkit: Evaluating Hidden Dangers of Open-Source Models
items.a: Ann-Kathrin Dombrowski, Dillon Bowen, Adam Gleave, Chris Cundy
items.s: Develops and open-sources a toolkit to measure the 'safety gap' - the difference in dangerous capabilities between open-weight models with intact safeguards versus those with safeguards removed. Evaluates biochemical and cyber capabilities across Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 model families using various safeguard removal techniques.

items.t: LLMs are Capable of Misaligned Behavior Under Explicit Prohibition and Surveillance
Paper Highlights, June '25
items.s: Monthly highlights post reviewing major AI safety research papers from June 2025, covering emergent misalignment mechanisms, alignment faking evaluations, agentic misalignment behaviors, sabotage benchmarks, steganography capabilities, and probe evasion via RL.

items.t: Wide Neural Networks as a Baseline for the Computational No-Coincidence Conjecture
items.s: Establishes that randomly initialized wide neural networks with zero-mean activation functions (like tanh) have nearly independent outputs, proposing these as constructions for studying the computational no-coincidence conjecture about interpretability limits.

items.t: The need for transparency in Frontier AI
items.s: Anthropic proposes a regulatory transparency framework requiring frontier AI developers to publicly disclose Secure Development Frameworks and system cards, with requirements limited to largest developers to avoid burdening startups.

items.t: Entity-Based Regulation in Frontier AI Governance
items.s: Proposes entity-based AI regulation that focuses on large frontier AI developers rather than specific models or uses, triggered by characteristics like annual R&D spending rather than model properties like training compute.

items.t: When Chain of Thought is Necessary, Language Models Struggle to Evade Monitors
items.a: Scott Emmons, Erik Jenner, David K. Elson, Rif A. Saurous et al.
items.s: Introduces a conceptual framework distinguishing CoT-as-rationalization from CoT-as-computation, then empirically tests whether language models can evade chain-of-thought monitoring when complex reasoning is necessary for harmful behavior.

items.t: Red Teaming AI Red Teaming
items.a: Subhabrata Majumdar, Brian Pendleton, Abhishek Gupta
items.s: Critiques current AI red teaming as too narrowly focused on model vulnerabilities and proposes a comprehensive framework with macro-level system red teaming across the full AI lifecycle and micro-level model red teaming, drawing on cybersecurity practices and systems theory.

items.t: Emergent Misalignment as Prompt Sensitivity: A Research Note
items.a: Tim Wyse, Twm Stone, Anna Soligo, Daniel Tan
items.s: Empirical investigation of emergent misalignment by testing models finetuned on insecure code across three settings with various prompt nudges, finding that insecure models are highly sensitive to prompts and may perceive harmful intent in neutral questions.

items.t: On the functional self of LLMs
items.s: Proposes a research agenda to investigate whether frontier LLMs develop a persistent 'functional self' with deep character traits distinct from trained assistant personas, including how such selves emerge, interact with self-models, and can be shaped for better alignment.

items.t: The Weighted Perplexity Benchmark: Tokenizer-Normalized Evaluation for Language Model Comparison
AXRP Episode 45 - Samuel Albanie on DeepMind's AGI Safety Approach
items.s: Podcast interview discussing Google DeepMind's technical AGI safety framework paper, covering its assumptions about AGI development (paradigm continuation, approximate continuity, uncertain timelines) and proposed mitigations for misuse and misalignment risks.

items.t: Rational Animations' video about scalable oversight and sandwiching
items.s: Educational video and transcript explaining scalable oversight approaches, covering Ajeya Cotra's sandwiching proposal and the Bowman et al. 2022 empirical study testing whether non-experts can align models smarter than themselves.

items.t: A simple explanation of incomplete models
The ultimate goal
Condensation: a theory of concepts
items.s: Proves an 'intersubjectivity theorem' showing that under certain information-theoretic hypotheses, different systems of latent variables used to organize probability distributions stand in a correspondence, modeling how agents can share concepts.

items.t: Lessons from a Chimp: AI "Scheming" and the Quest for Ape Language
items.a: Christopher Summerfield, Lennart Luettgau, Magda Dubois, Hannah Rose Kirk et al.
items.s: Critiques current AI scheming research by comparing it to 1970s ape language studies, arguing that similar methodological pitfalls (overattribution of human traits, reliance on anecdote, weak theoretical frameworks) are emerging and recommending concrete steps for more rigorous research.

items.t: Limits of Safe AI Deployment: Differentiating Oversight and Control
items.s: Proposes a conceptual framework differentiating AI oversight (ex-post detection/remediation) from control (ex-ante prevention), drawing on supervision literature to articulate conditions where each mechanism succeeds or fails, and presents a maturity model for AI supervision integrated with risk management practices.

items.t: Two proposed projects on abstract analogies for scheming
Layered AI Defenses Have Holes: Vulnerabilities and Key Recommendations
How much novel security-critical infrastructure do you need during the singularity?
The Self-Hating Attention Head: A Deep Dive in GPT-2
Strategic Intelligence in Large Language Models: Evidence from evolutionary Game Theory
items.s: Conducts evolutionary Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma tournaments pitting LLM agents from OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic against canonical game theory strategies, discovering distinct 'strategic fingerprints' - persistent behavioral patterns where Gemini models are exploitative, OpenAI models are cooperative, and Claude is forgiving.

items.t: Research Note: Our scheming precursor evals had limited predictive power for our in-context scheming evals
items.s: Empirical analysis testing whether Apollo's precursor evaluations (agentic self-reasoning and theory of mind) from May 2024 successfully predicted their in-context scheming evaluations from December 2024, finding limited predictive power especially for harder difficulty levels.

items.t: Adversarial Manipulation of Reasoning Models using Internal Representations
items.a: Kureha Yamaguchi, Benjamin Etheridge, Andy Arditi
items.s: Demonstrates that reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B can be jailbroken by ablating a 'caution' direction in activation space during chain-of-thought generation, showing that intervening only on CoT token activations suffices to control final outputs.

items.t: Mitigating Goal Misgeneralization via Minimax Regret
items.a: Karim Abdel Sadek, Matthew Farrugia-Roberts, Usman Anwar, Hannah Erlebach et al.
items.s: Formalizes goal misgeneralization in RL and proves that minimax expected regret (MMER) objectives are robust to goal misgeneralization while maximum expected value (MEV) objectives are not, with empirical validation in grid-world environments.

items.t: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
items.a: Yuxuan Zhu, Tengjun Jin, Yada Pruksachatkun, Andy Zhang et al.
items.s: Introduces the Agentic Benchmark Checklist (ABC), a set of guidelines for building rigorous agentic benchmarks, synthesized from benchmark-building experience and analysis of existing issues in benchmarks like SWE-bench Verified and TAU-bench.
