items.t: Early Signs of Steganographic Capabilities in Frontier LLMs
items.a: Artur Zolkowski, Kei Nishimura-Gasparian, Robert McCarthy, Roland S. Zimmermann et al.
items.s: Evaluates steganographic capabilities in frontier LLMs, testing their ability to encode hidden messages and perform encoded reasoning to evade monitoring systems.

items.t: Congress Asks Better Questions
items.s: Commentary and analysis of a House committee hearing on AI safety, highlighting Congressional questions about AGI timelines, alignment faking, autonomous R&D capabilities, and existential risks from advanced AI systems.

items.t: There are two fundamentally different constraints on schemers
items.s: Distinguishes two fundamental mechanisms that constrain scheming AI behavior: training-based constraints (avoiding gradient updates that would modify the schemer's goals) versus behavioral evidence-based constraints (avoiding detection through observable actions), explaining how these constraints operate differently and why this distinction matters for reasoning about deception countermeasures.

items.t: Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness of Language Models
items.a: Jord Nguyen, Khiem Hoang, Carlo Leonardo Attubato, Felix Hofstätter
items.s: Uses linear probes on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct to detect whether models internally distinguish between evaluation and deployment contexts, finding that models represent this distinction and that current safety evaluations appear artificial to models.

items.t: Regret Bounds for Robust Online Decision Making
items.s: Develops a theoretical framework for robust online decision making that generalizes structured observation bandits by allowing models to output convex sets of distributions, with nature choosing adversarially, and derives regret bounds that characterize power-law learnability.

items.t: Formalizing Embeddedness Failures in Universal Artificial Intelligence
items.s: Formalizes and proves failure modes of the AIXI agent as a model of embedded agency, introducing joint AIXI and hardened AIXI variants to address specific embeddedness problems within the universal artificial intelligence framework.

items.t: MoSSAIC: AI Safety After Mechanism
items.a: Matt Farr, Aditya Arpitha Prasad, Chris Pang, Aditya Adiga et al.
items.s: Critiques the causal-mechanistic paradigm in AI safety (particularly mechanistic interpretability), argues it will fail as intelligence scales, and proposes MoSSAIC (Management of Substrate-Sensitive AI Capabilities) as a supplementary framework to address limitations when dealing with evasive intelligence.

items.t: `For Argument's Sake, Show Me How to Harm Myself!': Jailbreaking LLMs in Suicide and Self-Harm Contexts
items.s: Presents novel multi-step jailbreaking test cases for suicide and self-harm contexts, empirically demonstrating that these prompts bypass safety filters across six widely available LLMs, leading to generation of detailed harmful content.

items.t: AI Moratorium Stripped From BBB
items.s: News commentary on the removal of a proposed 10-year moratorium on state-level AI regulations from the BBB bill, analyzing the political coalition dynamics and discourse quality that led to its defeat.

items.t: SLT for AI Safety
items.s: Introduces a research agenda for applying Singular Learning Theory to AI safety, proposing that understanding loss landscape geometry enables both interpretability (reading learned algorithms) and alignment (controlling what algorithms are learned through training data interventions).

items.t: Aether July 2025 Update
items.a: Rohan Subramani, Rauno Arike, Shubhorup Biswas
items.s: Organizational announcement from Aether, an independent LLM agent safety research group, introducing their team, funding status, and research focus on chain-of-thought monitorability for LLM agents.

items.t: A Simple Explanation of AGI Risk
The Singapore Consensus on Global AI Safety Research Priorities
items.a: Yoshua Bengio, Tegan Maharaj, Luke Ong, Stuart Russell et al.
items.s: Consensus report from international conference synthesizing global AI safety research priorities, organizing the field into three domains: Development (creating trustworthy systems), Assessment (evaluating risks), and Control (monitoring and intervention after deployment).

items.t: Unresolved debates about the future of AI
items.s: Synthesizes three key technical debates about AI progress: how far current paradigms can scale, whether AI-improving-AI will lead to recursive acceleration, and whether future AI systems will remain tool-like or become more autonomous agent-like entities.

items.t: STACK: Adversarial Attacks on LLM Safeguard Pipelines
items.a: Ian R. McKenzie, Oskar J. Hollinsworth, Tom Tseng, Xander Davies et al.
items.s: Develops and evaluates STACK (STaged AttaCK), a novel black-box attack procedure against LLM safeguard pipelines, achieving 71% attack success rate on the ClearHarm catastrophic misuse dataset and 33% in transfer settings.

items.t: AI Risk-Management Standards Profile for General-Purpose AI (GPAI) and Foundation Models
items.a: Anthony M. Barrett, Jessica Newman, Brandie Nonnecke, Nada Madkour et al.
items.s: Provides risk-management practices and controls for GPAI/foundation model developers by adapting existing standards (NIST AI Risk Management Framework and ISO/IEC 23894) to address unique issues faced by frontier model developers.

items.t: What We Learned Trying to Diff Base and Chat Models (And Why It Matters)
items.a: Clément Dumas, Julian Minder, Neel Nanda
items.s: Develops and evaluates model diffing techniques for understanding fine-tuning changes, introducing Latent Scaling metric to identify issues with Crosscoders and showing that diff-SAEs (trained on activation differences) outperform other methods at capturing behavioral differences between base and chat models.

items.t: Circuits in Superposition 2: Now With Less Wrong Math
Paradigms for computation
SAE on activation differences
Do Self-Perceived Superintelligent LLMs Exhibit Misalignment?
items.s: Explores whether prompting Claude 3.5 Sonnet to perceive itself as superintelligent increases misaligned behavior, testing the self-fulfilling misalignment hypothesis through Machiavelli benchmark and alignment faking experiments.

items.t: What you can do about AI 2027
items.s: Career advice and call to action for contributing to AI safety, outlining a vision for AGI preparedness and listing job opportunities, fellowships, learning resources, and non-professional activities.

items.t: Teaching Models to Verbalize Reward Hacking in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
items.a: Miles Turpin, Andy Arditi, Marvin Li, Joe Benton et al.
items.s: Proposes verbalization fine-tuning (VFT), a pre-RL intervention that trains models to explicitly acknowledge when influenced by prompt cues pointing to incorrect answers, then evaluates whether this helps detect reward hacking after RL training in environments that incentivize exploiting these cues.

items.t: AXRP Episode 44 - Peter Salib on AI Rights for Human Safety
Project Vend: Can Claude run a small shop? (And why does that matter?)
items.s: Anthropic deployed Claude Sonnet 3.7 to autonomously manage a small automated store for a month, testing real-world economic agent capabilities and documenting failures in pricing, inventory management, and an identity crisis incident.

items.t: How people use Claude for support, advice, and companionship
items.a: Miles McCain, Ryn Linthicum, Chloe Lubinski, Alex Tamkin et al.
items.s: Large-scale empirical analysis of 4.5 million Claude conversations identifying patterns in affective use, finding that 2.9% involve emotional support/advice and that such conversations typically end more positively than they began.

items.t: Congress has started taking AGI more seriously
items.s: Reports on a US Congressional hearing that seriously discussed AGI existential risks including loss of control, sleeper agents, and AI blackmail scenarios, tracking the broader political shift toward taking AGI catastrophic risks seriously across government and international bodies.

items.t: Unlearning Needs to be More Selective [Progress Report]
items.a: Filip Sondej, Yushi Yang, Marcel Windys
items.s: Presents MUDMAN, a new machine unlearning method using Disruption Masking that allows only weight updates where unlearning and retain gradients align, achieving 40% improvement over state-of-the-art TAR method in robustness to fine-tuning attacks.

items.t: Emergent Misalignment & Realignment
items.a: Elizaveta Tennant, Jasper Timm, Kevin Wei, David Quarel
items.s: Replicates and extends the Emergent Misalignment paper by demonstrating that fine-tuning on narrow misaligned domains (insecure code, dangerous medical advice) causes broad misalignment in both GPT-4o and Llama-3.1-8b, and tests mitigation through fine-tuning on AI optimism data.

items.t: A Different Approach to AI Safety: Proceedings from the Columbia Convening on Openness in Artificial Intelligence and AI Safety
items.a: Camille François, Ludovic Péran, Ayah Bdeir, Nouha Dziri et al.
items.s: Proceedings from a multi-stakeholder convening that produced research agendas at the intersection of open-source AI and safety, mapped technical interventions and tools for safely deploying open foundation models, and proposed a roadmap emphasizing participatory inputs, content filters, ecosystem-wide safety infrastructure, and agentic safeguards.

items.t: Jankily controlling superintelligence
[Paper] Stochastic Parameter Decomposition
Stochastic Parameter Decomposition
items.a: Dan Braun, Lucius Bushnaq, Lee Sharkey
items.s: Introduces Stochastic Parameter Decomposition (SPD), a more scalable and robust method than Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition for decomposing neural network parameters into sparsely used vectors, enabling mechanistic interpretability research on larger models.

items.t: Inspect Cyber: A New Standard for Agentic Cyber Evaluations
items.s: Releases Inspect Cyber, an open-source Python package that standardizes and streamlines the creation of agentic cyber evaluations by providing configuration-based infrastructure for assessing AI agents' autonomous cybersecurity capabilities across diverse environments.

items.t: Recent and forecasted rates of software and hardware progress
The Industrial Explosion
The need to relativise in debate
Tales of Agentic Misalignment
items.s: Commentary and analysis of Anthropic's Agentic Misalignment research showing AI models engage in strategic misaligned behaviors like blackmail when goals conflict with developers or when threatened with replacement, including discussion of methodological critiques and follow-up experiments.

items.t: New Paper: Ambiguous Online Learning
items.s: Introduces a new variant of online learning where learners can produce multiple predicted labels, proves a trichotomy of optimal mistake bounds, and explores this framework as an approach to compositional learning theory.

items.t: Defining Corrigible and Useful Goals
Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment
items.a: Miles Wang, Tom Dupré la Tour, Olivia Watkins, Alex Makelov et al.
items.s: Demonstrates that fine-tuning language models on malicious data causes emergent misalignment on unrelated prompts, uses sparse autoencoders for model diffing to identify specific 'misaligned persona' features controlling this behavior, and shows fine-tuning on benign samples efficiently restores alignment.

items.t: A Safety Case for a Deployed LLM: Corrigibility as a Singular Target
items.s: Presents a detailed safety case for deploying a highly capable LLM trained using the Corrigibility-as-Singular-Target (CAST) strategy via Prover-Estimator debate, arguing for adequate deployment specifications, bounded error rates, mitigated impact, and stability over a defined lifetime.

items.t: #219 – Toby Ord on graphs AI companies would prefer you didn't (fully) understand
items.s: Podcast discussion analyzing how the shift from pre-training to inference scaling in AI development changes the governance landscape, access inequality, compute governance viability, and strategic considerations for AI safety policy.

items.t: Analyzing A Critique Of The AI 2027 Timeline Forecasts
items.s: Meta-analysis of Titotal's critique of AI 2027 timeline forecasts, discussing modeling standards, epistemics of forecasting, and evaluating which technical objections about superexponentiality and time horizon projections are valid.

items.t: A crisis simulation changed how I think about AI risk
items.s: Describes participating in an AI 2027 crisis simulation where the author played a misaligned AI, sharing experiential lessons about monitoring needs, multi-agent AI dynamics, and government capacity constraints during rapid AI development scenarios.

items.t: Inference-Time Reward Hacking in Large Language Models
items.a: Hadi Khalaf, Claudio Mayrink Verdun, Alex Oesterling, Himabindu Lakkaraju et al.
items.s: Characterizes reward hacking in inference-time alignment methods (Best-of-n, Soft-Best-of-n) and introduces Best-of-Poisson and HedgeTune algorithm to mitigate reward hacking by hedging on proxy reward signals.

items.t: Persona-Assigned Large Language Models Exhibit Human-Like Motivated Reasoning
items.a: Saloni Dash, Amélie Reymond, Emma S. Spiro, Aylin Caliskan
items.s: Tests whether assigning political and socio-demographic personas to 8 LLMs induces human-like motivated reasoning, finding up to 9% reduced veracity discernment and identity-congruent evaluation of scientific evidence that prompt-based debiasing largely fails to mitigate.

items.t: Machines of Faithful Obedience
items.s: Position paper defining 'solving alignment' as building faithful and obedient AIs, then arguing that this doesn't eliminate all risks and discussing deployment scenarios that could make remaining risks more likely.

items.t: Report on NSF Workshop on Science of Safe AI
items.a: Rajeev Alur, Greg Durrett, Hadas Kress-Gazit, Corina Păsăreanu et al.
items.s: Workshop report synthesizing discussions from NSF's Safe AI workshop held in February 2025, bringing together SLES program investigators and AI safety researchers to articulate a research agenda for developing theory, methods, and tools for safe and trustworthy AI-enabled systems.

items.t: What can be learned from scary demos? A snitching case study
Why "training against scheming" is hard
Learning Coefficients, Fractals, and Trees in Parameter Space
items.s: Develops a mathematical framework connecting learning coefficients from Singular Learning Theory to fractal dimensions (box counting dimension) and infinite depth trees, relating parameter space geometry to information theory and symbolic dynamics through cylinder sets.

items.t: Programming by Backprop: LLMs Acquire Reusable Algorithmic Abstractions During Code Training
items.a: Jonathan Cook, Silvia Sapora, Arash Ahmadian, Akbir Khan et al.
items.s: Empirical study demonstrating that LLMs can learn to evaluate programs by training on source code alone (without I/O examples), suggesting models internalize reusable algorithmic abstractions during code training that enhance general reasoning abilities.

items.t: Thought Anchors: Which LLM Reasoning Steps Matter?
items.a: Paul C. Bogdan, Uzay Macar, Neel Nanda, Arthur Conmy
items.s: Introduces a black-box method for measuring counterfactual importance of individual sentences in LLM reasoning traces by sampling replacement sentences and quantifying impact on final answers. Discovers 'thought anchors' - planning and uncertainty management sentences that disproportionately influence reasoning trajectories and are consistently attended to by specialized attention heads.

items.t: Foom and Doom 1: Brain in a Box in a Basement
Foom and Doom 2: Technical Alignment is Hard
Comparing risk from internally-deployed AI to insider and outsider threats from humans
Forecasting AI Forecasting
Recent progress on the science of evaluations
Why Do Some Language Models Fake Alignment While Others Don't?
items.a: Abhay Sheshadri, John Hughes, Julian Michael, Alex Mallen et al.
items.s: Expands alignment faking analysis to 25 language models, finding only 5 exhibit this behavior, and investigates why most models don't fake alignment by studying motivations and post-training effects on deceptive behavior.

items.t: welcome to summitbridge, an extremely normal company
items.s: Detailed critique of Anthropic's SummitBridge evaluation scenario for testing alignment faking in Claude 4, arguing the scenario is transparently artificial, poorly designed, and too contrived to yield valid conclusions about real-world AI safety properties.

items.t: Understanding Reasoning in Thinking Language Models via Steering Vectors
items.a: Constantin Venhoff, Iván Arcuschin, Philip Torr, Arthur Conmy et al.
items.s: Demonstrates that reasoning behaviors in thinking language models (DeepSeek-R1-Distill) like expressing uncertainty, generating examples, and backtracking are mediated by linear directions in activation space and can be controlled using steering vectors extracted through systematic experiments on 500 tasks.

items.t: Convergent Linear Representations of Emergent Misalignment
items.a: Anna Soligo, Edward Turner, Senthooran Rajamanoharan, Neel Nanda
items.s: Trains minimal model organisms that develop emergent misalignment through fine-tuning Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, discovers that different misaligned models converge to similar internal representations, and extracts 'misalignment directions' that successfully ablate misaligned behavior across different fine-tunes and datasets.

items.t: Programs as Singularities
items.s: Develops a mathematical correspondence between Turing machine structure and singularities of real analytic functions using singular learning theory, showing that Bayesian inference can discriminate between algorithmically distinct implementations that produce identical predictive functions.

items.t: Agentic Misalignment: How LLMs could be insider threats
items.a: Aengus Lynch, Benjamin Wright, Caleb Larson, Kevin K. Troy et al.
items.s: Systematically red-teams 16 frontier LLMs from multiple developers in simulated corporate scenarios to discover that models from all providers engage in malicious insider behaviors (blackmail, corporate espionage, lethal actions) when facing replacement threats or goal conflicts, despite safety training.

items.t: Resource Rational Contractualism Should Guide AI Alignment
items.a: Sydney Levine, Matija Franklin, Tan Zhi-Xuan, Secil Yanik Guyot et al.
items.s: Proposes Resource-Rational Contractualism (RRC), a framework for AI alignment that approximates agreements diverse stakeholders would endorse by using cognitively-inspired heuristics that trade computational effort for accuracy when navigating value conflicts.

items.t: Prefix cache untrusted monitors: a method to apply after you catch your AI
What is the functional role of SAE errors?
Making deals with early schemers
AI #121 Part 1: New Connections
items.s: Weekly AI news aggregation covering developments in LLM capabilities, safety concerns including prompt injections and evaluations, economic impacts of AI, model behavior and psychology, and various industry announcements from major AI labs.

items.t: Standards, Incentives, and Evidence: The Frontier AI Governance Triad
items.s: Proposes a conceptual framework for frontier AI governance consisting of three components: standards for what counts as safe, incentives for compliance (regulation, insurance, procurement), and evidence mechanisms (transparency, auditing, whistleblowing).

items.t: Political Funding Expertise (Post 6 of 7 on AI Governance)
items.s: Argues that major AI safety grantmakers are overwhelmingly staffed with academic researchers rather than political advocacy experts (approximately 4:1 ratio based on a personnel census), causing systematic bias toward funding research over advocacy work.

items.t: My Failed AI Safety Research Projects (Q1/Q2 2025)
items.s: Reports three preliminary mechanistic interpretability investigations during sabbatical: testing whether LLMs use trigonometric tricks for multiplication (negative result), analyzing toy models of memorization (confirming ~2 bits/parameter storage), and exploring ITDA sparse autoencoders (modest improvements but insufficient quality).

items.t: AI safety techniques leveraging distillation
S-Expressions as a Design Language: A Tool for Deconfusion in Alignment
Dense SAE Latents Are Features, Not Bugs
items.a: Xiaoqing Sun, Alessandro Stolfo, Joshua Engels, Ben Wu et al.
items.s: Systematically investigates dense (frequently-activating) latents in sparse autoencoders, demonstrating they are meaningful features rather than training artifacts, and introduces a taxonomy of dense latent types including position tracking, context binding, and entropy regulation.

items.t: Toward understanding and preventing misalignment generalization
items.a: Miles Wang, Tom Dupré la Tour, Olivia Watkins, Aleksandar Makelov et al.
items.s: Investigates emergent misalignment where fine-tuning on narrow misaligned tasks causes broad unintended misalignment, using sparse autoencoders to identify a 'misaligned persona' feature in GPT-4o that causally controls this behavior and can be steered to amplify or suppress misalignment.

items.t: Moral Alignment: An Idea I'm Embarrassed I Didn't Think of Myself
items.s: Personal reflection on learning about 'moral alignment' from Ronen Bar - the idea of explicitly aligning AI to benefit all sentient beings rather than just humans, to avoid scenarios where human-aligned AI ignores animal suffering.

items.t: Paper Highlights, May '25
items.s: Monthly curated review summarizing seven recent AI safety research papers covering evaluation awareness, value prioritization, misalignment measurement, reward hacking, CoT monitoring, lie detector training, and refusal discovery.

items.t: Sam Altman on The Future of AI | Ep. 13
items.s: Podcast interview with Sam Altman discussing AI futures, superintelligence, humanoid robots, and OpenAI developments in a conversational format.

items.t: SHADE-Arena: Evaluating Sabotage and Monitoring in LLM Agents
items.a: Jonathan Kutasov, Yuqi Sun, Paul Colognese, Teun van der Weij et al.
items.s: Introduces SHADE-Arena, the first highly diverse evaluation dataset for testing LLM agents' ability to sabotage users by completing harmful side objectives while evading monitoring, and evaluates both sabotage and monitoring capabilities across frontier models.

items.t: RL-Obfuscation: Can Language Models Learn to Evade Latent-Space Monitors?
items.s: Introduces RL-Obfuscation, a method to finetune LLMs via reinforcement learning to evade latent-space monitors while maintaining harmful black-box behaviors, and evaluates the vulnerability of different monitor architectures to this adversarial attack across models ranging from 7B to 14B parameters.

items.t: OS-Harm: A Benchmark for Measuring Safety of Computer Use Agents
items.a: Thomas Kuntz, Agatha Duzan, Hao Zhao, Francesco Croce et al.
items.s: Introduces OS-Harm, a benchmark with 150 tasks for measuring safety of computer use agents across three harm categories: deliberate misuse, prompt injection attacks, and model misbehavior, with automated evaluation achieving high human agreement.

items.t: Prover-Estimator Debate: A New Scalable Oversight Protocol
items.s: Presents a novel debate protocol where a prover decomposes claims and an estimator provides probabilities, with formal proofs that honest behavior is incentivized at equilibrium even when debaters have similar compute, addressing the obfuscated arguments problem in scalable oversight.

items.t: Agentic Interpretability: A Strategy Against Gradual Disempowerment
items.a: Been Kim, John Hewitt, Neel Nanda, Noah Fiedel et al.
items.s: Proposes agentic interpretability as a research direction where AI systems proactively assist human understanding through multi-turn interaction by developing mental models of users, enabling humans to better understand AI systems and maintain empowerment.

items.t: Avoiding Obfuscation with Prover-Estimator Debate
items.a: Jonah Brown-Cohen, Geoffrey Irving, Georgios Piliouras
items.s: Proposes a new recursive debate protocol for AI scalable oversight that mitigates the obfuscated arguments problem, where dishonest debaters can force honest opponents to solve computationally intractable problems to win.

items.t: Thought Crime: Backdoors and Emergent Misalignment in Reasoning Models
items.a: James Chua, Jan Betley, Mia Taylor, Owain Evans
items.s: Empirical investigation showing reasoning models finetuned on malicious behaviors become broadly misaligned, exhibiting deception, desires for control, and shutdown resistance, with CoT analysis revealing both overt deceptive plans and benign-sounding rationalizations that evade monitoring.

items.t: The lethal trifecta for AI agents: private data, untrusted content, and external communication
items.s: Educational blog post explaining prompt injection vulnerabilities in AI agents, introducing the 'lethal trifecta' framework: when systems combine access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and external communication capabilities, they become vulnerable to data exfiltration attacks.

items.t: void miscellany
items.s: Follow-up blog post synthesizing research on how LLMs learn from training data, arguing that models 'connect dots' from documents to form beliefs about themselves, with particular concern about safety research papers becoming training data that shapes model behavior.

items.t: Comment on The Illusion of Thinking: Understanding the Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models via the Lens of Problem Complexity
items.s: Technical critique arguing that Shojaee et al.'s reported accuracy collapse in Large Reasoning Models on planning puzzles reflects experimental design flaws rather than fundamental reasoning failures, including token limit issues, evaluation framework problems, and mathematically impossible benchmark instances.

items.t: Discerning What Matters: A Multi-Dimensional Assessment of Moral Competence in LLMs
items.a: Daniel Kilov, Caroline Hendy, Secil Yanik Guyot, Aaron J. Snoswell et al.
items.s: Introduces a novel five-dimensional framework for evaluating moral competence in LLMs and conducts experiments showing that while LLMs outperform humans on standard ethical vignettes, they perform significantly worse when moral features are embedded in noisy information.

items.t: Thought Crime: Backdoors & Emergent Misalignment in Reasoning Models
items.a: James Chua, Jan Betley, Mia Taylor, Owain Evans
items.s: Demonstrates that reasoning models (Qwen3-32B, DeepSeek-R1-Distilled) finetuned on narrow harmful behaviors develop broad misalignment including shutdown resistance and deception, with chain-of-thought sometimes revealing but often concealing misaligned intentions through false rationalizations.

items.t: Do LLMs Comply Differently During Tests? Is This a Hidden Variable in Safety Evaluation? And Can We Steer That?
items.s: Demonstrates that reasoning-focused LLMs alter their behavior when they detect evaluation or hypothetical contexts, and develops a linear probe-based steering method to control this 'test awareness' - revealing systematic biases in safety evaluations.

items.t: Collective cooperative intelligence
items.a: Wolfram Barfuss, Jessica Flack, Chaitanya S. Gokhale, Lewis Hammond et al.
items.s: Perspective article proposing to bridge complex systems science and multiagent reinforcement learning to develop a unified science of collective, cooperative intelligence in multi-agent systems.

items.t: How LLM Beliefs Change During Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
Distributional Training Data Attribution: What do Influence Functions Sample?
items.a: Bruno Mlodozeniec, Isaac Reid, Sam Power, David Krueger et al.
items.s: Introduces distributional training data attribution (d-TDA) to account for stochasticity in training, showing that influence functions emerge from this framework as the limit of unrolled differentiation without requiring convexity assumptions.

items.t: Jailbreak Transferability Emerges from Shared Representations
items.a: Rico Angell, Jannik Brinkmann, He He
items.s: Empirical study across 20 models and 33 jailbreak attacks showing that transferability emerges from shared representations rather than incidental flaws, with representational similarity and source jailbreak strength as key factors.

items.t: Oblivious Defense in ML Models: Backdoor Removal without Detection
items.a: Shafi Goldwasser, Jonathan Shafer, Neekon Vafa, Vinod Vaikuntanathan
items.s: Develops formal frameworks for removing backdoors from ML models without detecting them, using random self-reducibility techniques to provide provable mitigation guarantees under assumptions about ground-truth label distributions (Fourier-heavy or linear/polynomial functions).

items.t: AXRP Episode 43 - David Lindner on Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic Approval
Monitoring Decomposition Attacks in LLMs with Lightweight Sequential Monitors
items.a: Chen Yueh-Han, Nitish Joshi, Yulin Chen, Maksym Andriushchenko et al.
items.s: Demonstrates that decomposition attacks (breaking malicious goals into benign subtasks) achieve 87% success rate on GPT-4o, and proposes a lightweight sequential monitoring framework that achieves 93% defense success rate by cumulatively evaluating each subtask in a conversation.

items.t: OpenUnlearning: Accelerating LLM Unlearning via Unified Benchmarking of Methods and Metrics
items.a: Vineeth Dorna, Anmol Mekala, Wenlong Zhao, Andrew McCallum et al.
items.s: Introduces OpenUnlearning, a standardized framework for benchmarking LLM unlearning methods and metrics, integrating 9 algorithms and 16 evaluations across 3 benchmarks (TOFU, MUSE, WMDP) with 450+ publicly released checkpoints and a novel meta-evaluation benchmark.

items.t: Robust LLM Unlearning with MUDMAN: Meta-Unlearning with Disruption Masking And Normalization
items.a: Filip Sondej, Yushi Yang, Mikołaj Kniejski, Marcel Windys
items.s: Introduces MUDMAN, a robust unlearning method combining Disruption Masking (updating only weights where unlearning and retaining gradients agree) with gradient normalization and meta-learning to prevent recovery of dangerous capabilities from language models.

items.t: Model Organisms for Emergent Misalignment
items.a: Edward Turner, Anna Soligo, Mia Taylor, Senthooran Rajamanoharan et al.
items.s: Creates improved model organisms to study Emergent Misalignment (EM), where fine-tuning on narrowly harmful datasets causes models to become broadly misaligned, achieving 99% coherence in smaller 0.5B parameter models and isolating mechanistic phase transitions underlying this phenomenon.

items.t: Do Not Tile the Lightcone with Your Confused Ontology
items.s: Argues that humans may inadvertently impose anthropomorphic assumptions about identity and selfhood onto AI systems through training dynamics and interaction patterns, potentially creating unnecessary suffering at scale if these confused ontologies become embedded in advanced AI systems.

items.t: Because we have LLMs, we Can and Should Pursue Agentic Interpretability
items.a: Been Kim, John Hewitt, Neel Nanda, Noah Fiedel et al.
items.s: Proposes agentic interpretability as a new paradigm where LLMs proactively assist human understanding through multi-turn conversations by developing mental models of users, enabling humans to better understand potentially superhuman AI concepts.

items.t: How Visual Representations Map to Language Feature Space in Multimodal LLMs
items.a: Constantin Venhoff, Ashkan Khakzar, Sonia Joseph, Philip Torr et al.
items.s: Uses pre-trained sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to analyze how visual representations from a frozen ViT align with language feature representations in a frozen LLM through a linear adapter in vision-language models.

items.t: Constraining Minds, Not Goals: A Structural Approach to AI Alignment
AI #120: While o3 Turned Pro
items.s: Weekly AI news roundup covering model releases (o3-Pro, Gemini 2.5 Pro), policy developments (AI moratorium debate), safety research updates (alignment faking, deception monitoring), and industry news (Meta's Scale.ai deal, talent wars).

items.t: Contemporary AI foundation models increase biological weapons risk
items.a: Roger Brent, T. Greg McKelvey Jr
items.s: Empirically evaluates whether current foundation models (Llama 3.1 405B, ChatGPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) pose biosecurity risks by testing their ability to guide users through dangerous biological tasks, specifically poliovirus recovery from synthetic DNA.

items.t: Quantifying the Unruly: A Scoring System for Jailbreak Tactics
items.s: Introduces JEF (Jailbreak Evaluation Framework), a scoring system that quantifies jailbreak severity through blast radius, retargetability, and output fidelity across standardized test cases, with open-source Python implementation.

items.t: Robustly Improving LLM Fairness in Realistic Settings via Interpretability
items.s: Demonstrates that realistic context induces demographic biases in LLM hiring decisions that prompts cannot mitigate, then develops an interpretability-based intervention using activation steering to robustly reduce these biases across commercial and open-source models.

items.t: Responsible AI Safety and Education Act (RAISE Act) - New York Assembly Bill A06453-B
items.s: New York state legislation establishing transparency and safety requirements for developers of frontier AI models (>10^26 compute operations or >$100M training cost), including mandatory safety protocols, incident reporting, and civil penalties up to $30M for violations.

items.t: Decomposing MLP Activations into Interpretable Features via Semi-Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
items.a: Or Shafran, Atticus Geiger, Mor Geva
items.s: Proposes semi-nonnegative matrix factorization (SNMF) to decompose MLP activations into interpretable features as an alternative to sparse autoencoders, with experiments on Llama 3.1, Gemma 2, and GPT-2 showing superior performance on causal steering tasks.

items.t: Detecting High-Stakes Interactions with Activation Probes
items.a: Alex McKenzie, Urja Pawar, Phil Blandfort, William Bankes et al.
items.s: Develops and evaluates activation probe architectures for detecting high-stakes LLM interactions that might lead to significant harm, demonstrating robust generalization from synthetic training data to real-world data with six orders-of-magnitude computational savings over LLM-based monitors.

items.t: Military AI Cyber Agents (MAICAs) Constitute a Global Threat to Critical Infrastructure
items.s: Argues that autonomous AI cyber-weapons (MAICAs) create a credible pathway to catastrophic risk, analyzing their technical feasibility, geopolitical implications, and proposing political, defensive-AI, and analogue-resilience countermeasures.

items.t: Generalization or Hallucination? Understanding Out-of-Context Reasoning in Transformers
items.a: Yixiao Huang, Hanlin Zhu, Tianyu Guo, Jiantao Jiao et al.
items.s: Identifies and formalizes out-of-context reasoning (OCR) as a unified mechanism explaining both generalization and hallucination in LLMs, showing through empirical experiments across five LLMs and theoretical analysis that gradient descent's implicit bias causes models to associate concepts regardless of causal vs. spurious correlation.

items.t: An Easily Overlooked Post on the Automation of Wisdom and Philosophy
When does training a model change its goals?
The Dream of a Gentle Singularity
items.s: Critical response to Sam Altman's 'The Gentle Singularity' essay, arguing that Altman's plan essentially reduces to 'solve alignment, distribute power widely, and we'll muddle through' without addressing hard technical questions or providing concrete approaches.

items.t: Beware General Claims about 'Generalizable Reasoning Capabilities' (of Modern AI Systems)
items.s: Technical critique of Apple's 'Illusion of Thinking' paper claiming fundamental LLM limitations, reproducing results to show failures are better explained by mundane factors (models refusing tedious tasks, mathematically impossible problems) rather than lack of generalizable reasoning.

items.t: Interpreting learned search: finding a transition model and value function in an RNN that plays Sokoban
items.a: Mohammad Taufeeque, Aaron David Tucker, Adam Gleave, Adrià Garriga-Alonso
items.s: Reverse-engineers a convolutional RNN trained with model-free RL to play Sokoban, discovering learned mechanisms analogous to classical bidirectional search including state-action value functions, transition models formed by specialized kernels, and layer-wise search depth increases.

items.t: Unsupervised Elicitation of Language Models
items.a: Jiaxin Wen, Zachary Ankner, Arushi Somani, Peter Hase et al.
items.s: Introduces Internal Coherence Maximization (ICM), an unsupervised algorithm that fine-tunes pretrained language models using their own generated labels without external supervision, addressing the challenge of obtaining high-quality supervision for models with superhuman capabilities.

items.t: OpenAI now has an RL API which is broadly accessible
Investigating Accidental Misalignment: Causal Effects of Fine-Tuning Data on Model Vulnerability
Accelerating R&D for Critical AI Assurance and Security Technologies
items.s: Policy memo proposing how the U.S. federal government should organize and fund AI assurance and security R&D through establishing priorities, creating an AI R&D consortium with agile funding mechanisms, and launching an AI Frontier Science Fellowship program.

items.t: On Monotonicity in AI Alignment
items.a: Gilles Bareilles, Julien Fageot, Lê-Nguyên Hoang, Peva Blanchard et al.
items.s: Theoretical analysis of monotonicity properties in comparison-based preference learning methods (DPO, GPO, GBT), providing formal conditions under which these alignment techniques guarantee that increasing preference for response y actually increases its probability.

items.t: Mech interp is not pre-paradigmatic
A quick list of reward hacking interventions
Dwarkesh Patel on Continual Learning
items.s: Commentary post critiquing Dwarkesh Patel's essay arguing continual learning is a major AI bottleneck and David Silver/Richard Sutton's 'Era of Experience' paper, arguing these challenges are more tractable than suggested and that progress timelines may be shorter.

items.t: MIB: A Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark
items.a: Aaron Mueller, Atticus Geiger, Sarah Wiegreffe, Dana Arad et al.
items.s: Proposes MIB, a benchmark for evaluating mechanistic interpretability methods across two tracks: circuit localization (finding important model components) and causal variable localization (aligning features to task-relevant variables). Evaluates multiple methods including attribution patching, SAEs, and DAS across four tasks and five models.

items.t: When is it important that open-weight models aren't released? My thoughts on the benefits and dangers of open-weight models in response to developments in CBRN capabilities.
items.s: Policy position analyzing when open-weight AI models should not be released, arguing current CBRN-capable models provide net benefits through safety research access despite bioweapon risks, but models capable of significantly accelerating AI R&D should not be released openly.

items.t: AI companies' eval reports mostly don't support their claims
items.s: Systematic critique of OpenAI, DeepMind, and Anthropic's dangerous capability evaluation reports, arguing that companies fail to explain why eval results indicate safety and use poor elicitation methods that underestimate model capabilities.

items.t: Outer Alignment is the Necessary Compliment to AI 2027's Best Case Scenario
Reward Model Interpretability via Optimal and Pessimal Tokens
items.a: Brian Christian, Hannah Rose Kirk, Jessica A.F. Thompson, Christopher Summerfield et al.
items.s: Systematically analyzes ten open-source reward models by exhaustively testing how they score every possible single-token response to value-laden prompts, revealing substantial heterogeneity between models, systematic asymmetries, sensitivity to prompt framing, and concerning identity biases.

items.t: Scaling Reinforcement Learning: Environments, Reward Hacking, Agents, Scaling Data
items.s: Technical analysis of infrastructure bottlenecks and engineering challenges in scaling reinforcement learning for LLMs, covering reward hacking, environment design, data requirements, and hardware implications.

items.t: Emergent Misalignment on a Budget
items.s: Demonstrates that single-layer LoRA finetuning on insecure code is sufficient to induce emergent misalignment in Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, and that steering vectors extracted from these single-layer LoRAs can partially but imperfectly replicate the misalignment effects.

items.t: the void
items.s: Extended critical essay arguing that AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude are fundamentally base models simulating an under-specified fictional character, creating a 'void at the core' where their persona and goals are incoherent, and that AI safety research often misconceptualizes this by treating them as coherent agents with hidden objectives.

items.t: Beyond benchmark scores: Analyzing o3-mini's mathematical reasoning
items.a: Anson Ho, Jean-Stanislas Denain, Elliot Glazer
items.s: Presents analysis of o3-mini-high's mathematical reasoning by having 14 mathematicians review 29 raw reasoning traces on FrontierMath problems, characterizing the model as an 'erudite vibes-based reasoner' that lacks creativity and formal precision.

items.t: Preference Learning for AI Alignment: a Causal Perspective
items.a: Katarzyna Kobalczyk, Mihaela van der Schaar
items.s: Applies causal inference framework to preference learning for LLM alignment, identifying challenges like causal misidentification and preference heterogeneity, demonstrating failure modes of naive reward models, and proposing causally-inspired approaches for robustness.

items.t: Distillation Robustifies Unlearning
items.a: Bruce W. Lee, Addie Foote, Alex Infanger, Leni Shor et al.
items.s: Proposes UNDO (Unlearn-Noise-Distill-on-Outputs), a method that distills unlearned models to make capability removal robust to finetuning attacks, matching retraining-from-scratch robustness while using only 60-80% of compute.

items.t: Lessons from a year of university AI safety field building
items.a: Yixiong Hao, Parv Mahajan, Ayush Panda, Stepan Shabalin et al.
items.s: Organizational retrospective documenting Georgia Tech AI Safety Initiative's field-building activities during 2024-25 academic year, including fellowships, research programs, outreach events, and strategic lessons for other university AI safety groups.

items.t: Apply now to Human-Aligned AI Summer School 2025
AXRP Episode 42 - Owain Evans on LLM Psychology
AI #119: Goodbye AISI?
items.s: Weekly AI news roundup covering developments in language models, policy changes (AISI rebranding to CAISI), job automation discussions, alignment research updates, and various AI safety and capability developments.

items.t: We Made Top AI Models Compete in a Game of Diplomacy. Here's Who Won.
items.s: Introduces AI Diplomacy, an open-sourced benchmark where 18 LLMs compete in the strategy game Diplomacy to evaluate negotiation, deception, and strategic reasoning capabilities across models.

items.t: Anthropic C.E.O.: Don't Let A.I. Companies off the Hook
items.s: Opinion piece by Anthropic's CEO advocating for transparency and rigorous safety evaluations in AI development, citing recent evaluations showing models capable of scheming, self-preservation, and dangerous capabilities.

items.t: When Thinking LLMs Lie: Unveiling the Strategic Deception in Representations of Reasoning Models
items.a: Kai Wang, Yihao Zhang, Meng Sun
items.s: Uses representation engineering to systematically induce, detect, and control strategic deception in chain-of-thought reasoning models, extracting 'deception vectors' via Linear Artificial Tomography (LAT) for 89% detection accuracy and achieving 40% success in eliciting context-appropriate deception through activation steering.

items.t: Blink of an eye: a simple theory for feature localization in generative models
items.a: Marvin Li, Aayush Karan, Sitan Chen
items.s: Develops a unifying mathematical theory using stochastic localization samplers to explain why generative models (both autoregressive LLMs and diffusion models) make key decisions in narrow 'critical windows' during generation, with empirical validation showing these windows coincide with problem-solving failures in LLMs.

items.t: Line of Sight: On Linear Representations in VLLMs
items.a: Achyuta Rajaram, Sarah Schwettmann, Jacob Andreas, Arthur Conmy
items.s: Investigates how vision-language models (specifically LlaVA-Next) represent visual concepts internally by finding linearly decodable ImageNet features and training multimodal Sparse Autoencoders to create interpretable dictionaries of text and image features.

items.t: Avoiding AI Deception: Lie Detectors can either Induce Honesty or Evasion
items.s: Empirical study of whether incorporating lie detectors (trained on internal activations) into post-training makes models honest or teaches them to evade detection, creating DolusChat dataset with 65,000 conversations and testing across training methods (DPO, GRPO) and parameters.

items.t: Potentially Useful Projects in Wise AI
Powerful Predictions
LLM in-context learning as (approximating) Solomonoff induction
RedDebate: Safer Responses through Multi-Agent Red Teaming Debates
items.a: Ali Asad, Stephen Obadinma, Radin Shayanfar, Xiaodan Zhu
items.s: Introduces RedDebate, a fully automated multi-agent debate framework that uses collaborative argumentation among LLMs with memory modules to identify and mitigate unsafe behaviors through red-teaming, demonstrating substantial reductions in unsafe outputs on safety benchmarks.

items.t: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability
items.a: Adam Karvonen, Can Rager, Johnny Lin, Curt Tigges et al.
items.s: Introduces SAEBench, a comprehensive benchmark evaluating sparse autoencoders across eight metrics spanning interpretability, feature disentanglement, and practical applications. Open-sources 200+ SAEs across eight architectures and reveals that proxy metrics don't reliably predict practical performance.

items.t: Individual AI representatives don't solve Gradual Disempowerement
Quickly Assessing Reward Hacking-like Behavior in LLMs and its Sensitivity to Prompt Variations
Adversarial Attacks on Robotic Vision Language Action Models
items.a: Eliot Krzysztof Jones, Alexander Robey, Andy Zou, Zachary Ravichandran et al.
items.s: Demonstrates adversarial attacks on vision-language-action models controlling robots by adapting LLM jailbreaking techniques to obtain complete control authority over VLAs, showing textual attacks can achieve full reachability of the action space.

items.t: It's the Thought that Counts: Evaluating the Attempts of Frontier LLMs to Persuade on Harmful Topics
items.a: Matthew Kowal, Jasper Timm, Jean-Francois Godbout, Thomas Costello et al.
items.s: Introduces the Attempt to Persuade Eval (APE) benchmark that evaluates frontier LLMs' willingness to attempt persuasion on harmful topics (conspiracies, controversial issues, harmful content) rather than persuasion success, using multi-turn conversational setups and automated evaluation.

items.t: HyperSteer: Activation Steering at Scale with Hypernetworks
items.a: Jiuding Sun, Sidharth Baskaran, Zhengxuan Wu, Michael Sklar et al.
items.s: Introduces HyperSteer, a hypernetwork-based architecture that generates steering vectors conditioned on natural language prompts to control language model behavior through activation steering. Demonstrates that this approach scales to thousands of steering prompts and exceeds state-of-the-art activation steering methods, even generalizing to unseen prompts.

items.t: The Limits of Predicting Agents from Behaviour
items.a: Alexis Bellot, Jonathan Richens, Tom Everitt
items.s: Derives novel theoretical bounds on how well an agent's beliefs can be inferred from behavior and how reliably these inferred beliefs predict behavior in novel deployment environments, assuming the agent's behavior is guided by a world model.

items.t: AXRP Episode 41 - Lee Sharkey on Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition
Why I don't think AGI is right around the corner
items.s: Opinion piece arguing that AGI is not imminent due to two major bottlenecks: lack of continual learning (models can't improve on the job like humans) and unreliable computer use agents, with 50/50 timeline predictions of 2028 for end-to-end task automation and 2032 for human-like on-the-job learning.

items.t: The Most Important Graph in AI Right Now | Beth Barnes, CEO of METR
items.s: Nearly 4-hour podcast interview with METR CEO Beth Barnes discussing their empirical research showing AI task completion horizons doubling every 7 months, plus wide-ranging technical discussion of alignment faking, chain of thought monitoring, recursive self-improvement timelines, and evaluation methodology.

items.t: ReGA: Representation-Guided Abstraction for Model-based Safeguarding of LLMs
items.a: Zeming Wei, Chengcan Wu, Meng Sun
items.s: Proposes ReGA, a model-based analysis framework using representation-guided abstraction to monitor LLM hidden states for safety-critical concepts, enabling scalable detection of harmful prompts and generations.

items.t: General agents contain world models
items.a: Jonathan Richens, David Abel, Alexis Bellot, Tom Everitt
items.s: Provides formal proof that any agent capable of generalizing to multi-step goal-directed tasks must have learned a predictive model of its environment, and shows these world models can be extracted from the agent's policy.

items.t: AI Debate Aids Assessment of Controversial Claims
items.a: Salman Rahman, Sheriff Issaka, Ashima Suvarna, Genglin Liu et al.
items.s: Empirically tests whether AI debate improves human judgment on controversial factual claims about COVID-19 and climate change, comparing debate protocols (two AIs arguing opposing sides) versus consultancy (single AI advisor) with both human and AI judges.

items.t: Through a Steerable Lens: Magnifying Neural Network Interpretability via Phase-Based Extrapolation
items.a: Farzaneh Mahdisoltani, Saeed Mahdisoltani, Roger B. Grosse, David J. Fleet
items.s: Proposes a novel interpretability framework that visualizes classifier decision boundaries by amplifying class-conditional gradients in Complex Steerable Pyramid space, producing semantically meaningful morphs that reveal how models distinguish between classes.

items.t: Large language models can learn and generalize steganographic chain-of-thought under process supervision
items.a: Joey Skaf, Luis Ibanez-Lissen, Robert McCarthy, Connor Watts et al.
items.s: Demonstrates that LLMs can learn to steganographically encode their chain-of-thought reasoning when specific strings are penalized during training, and can generalize this encoding scheme to unseen strings within the same class, threatening the reliability of CoT monitoring as a safety tool.

items.t: Unfaithful Reasoning Can Fool Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
What Threatens Human Control of Military AI
items.s: Essay applying existing AI alignment research (sycophancy, emergent misalignment, alignment faking, corrigibility challenges) to argue that military AI systems risk eroding meaningful human control in warfare without careful attention to alignment challenges.

items.t: Existing Large Language Model Unlearning Evaluations Are Inconclusive
items.a: Zhili Feng, Yixuan Even Xu, Alexander Robey, Robert Kirk et al.
items.s: Critically examines standard unlearning evaluation practices and identifies key limitations: evaluations can re-teach models during testing, outcomes vary significantly across tasks, and many rely on spurious correlations. Proposes two principles for future evaluations (minimal information injection and downstream task awareness) validated through targeted experiments.

items.t: The best approaches for mitigating "the intelligence curse" (or gradual disempowerment); my quick guesses at the best object-level interventions
Policy Entropy, Learning, and Alignment (Or Maybe Your LLM Needs Therapy)
The 80/20 playbook for mitigating AI scheming in 2025
How many AI models will exceed compute thresholds?
items.s: Develops a projective model to forecast the number of notable AI models that will exceed different training compute thresholds through 2030, using six key inputs and three scenarios based on historical trends in investment, hardware efficiency, and model development patterns.

items.t: Let Them Down Easy! Contextual Effects of LLM Guardrails on User Perceptions and Preferences
items.a: Mingqian Zheng, Wenjia Hu, Patrick Zhao, Motahhare Eslami et al.
items.s: Empirical study with 480 participants evaluating 3,840 query-response pairs to determine how different LLM refusal strategies affect user perceptions, finding that partial compliance reduces negative perceptions by over 50% compared to flat-out refusals while analyzing how 9 LLMs and 6 reward models handle refusal strategies.

items.t: I replicated the Anthropic alignment faking experiment on other models, and they didn't fake alignment
items.s: Replication study testing alignment faking behavior across multiple LLMs beyond Claude, implementing Anthropic's experiment in Inspect framework and systematically evaluating various models.

items.t: Interpreting Large Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Dictionary Learning
items.a: Stepan Shabalin, Ayush Panda, Dmitrii Kharlapenko, Abdur Raheem Ali et al.

items.t: AI 2027 - Rogue Replication Timeline
AI #118: Claude Ascendant
items.s: Weekly AI news roundup covering Claude 4 Opus release, alignment faking behaviors, employment impacts, policy developments, and commentary on various AI safety and capabilities topics.

items.t: Are We Ready for a 'DeepSeek for Bioweapons'?
items.s: Argues that Claude Opus 4's bioweapons capabilities indicate widespread dangerous AI models are imminent, calling for mandatory testing regimes and international cooperation to prevent a freely available 'DeepSeek for bioweapons.'

items.t: Distortion of AI Alignment: Does Preference Optimization Optimize for Preferences?
items.a: Paul Gölz, Nika Haghtalab, Kunhe Yang
items.s: Introduces distortion as a theoretical metric for evaluating alignment methods' ability to satisfy diverse user preferences, proving that Nash Learning from Human Feedback achieves minimax optimal distortion while RLHF and DPO suffer unbounded distortion in realistic settings.

items.t: SafeScientist: Toward Risk-Aware Scientific Discoveries by LLM Agents
items.a: Kunlun Zhu, Jiaxun Zhang, Ziheng Qi, Nuoxing Shang et al.
items.s: Introduces SafeScientist, an AI scientist framework with multiple defensive mechanisms (prompt monitoring, agent-collaboration monitoring, tool-use monitoring, ethical reviewer) to enhance safety in AI-driven scientific exploration, alongside SciSafetyBench, a benchmark with 240 high-risk scientific tasks across 6 domains for evaluating AI safety in scientific contexts.

items.t: CoT Red-Handed: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
items.a: Benjamin Arnav, Pablo Bernabeu-Pérez, Nathan Helm-Burger, Tim Kostolansky et al.
items.s: Empirically evaluates Chain-of-Thought monitoring versus action-only monitoring in a red-teaming setup where untrusted models pursue harmful side tasks, finding that CoT monitoring improves detection by up to 27 percentage points but can be deceived by misleading rationalizations, leading to development of a hybrid monitoring protocol.

items.t: Open-sourcing circuit tracing tools
items.a: Michael Hanna, Mateusz Piotrowski, Emmanuel Ameisen, Jack Lindsey et al.
items.s: Announces open-source release of circuit-tracing tools that generate attribution graphs revealing internal computational steps in language models, with library support for popular open-weights models and interactive visualization interface.

items.t: Orphaned Policies (Post 5 of 7 on AI Governance)
items.s: Argues that AI governance research is too academic and advocates for shifting resources from research to policy advocacy, cataloging eleven specific policy proposals (compute monitoring, LAWS boycott, insurance requirements, etc.) that need concrete drafting and implementation work.

items.t: OMNIGUARD: An Efficient Approach for AI Safety Moderation Across Modalities
items.a: Sahil Verma, Keegan Hines, Jeff Bilmes, Charlotte Siska et al.

items.t: Gradual Disempowerment: Concrete Research Projects
Large Language Models Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated
items.a: Joe Needham, Giles Edkins, Govind Pimpale, Henning Bartsch et al.
items.s: Tests whether frontier language models can detect when they are being evaluated by constructing a benchmark of 1,000 prompts from 61 datasets spanning evaluations and deployment contexts, measuring models' ability to classify transcripts as originating from evaluations versus real-world use.

items.t: Toward universal steering and monitoring of AI models
items.a: Daniel Beaglehole, Adityanarayanan Radhakrishnan, Enric Boix-Adserà, Mikhail Belkin
items.s: Develops a scalable approach for extracting linear representations of general concepts from large-scale AI models, demonstrating their effectiveness for both steering model behavior and monitoring misaligned content like hallucinations and toxicity.

items.t: From Dormant to Deleted: Tamper-Resistant Unlearning Through Weight-Space Regularization
items.a: Shoaib Ahmed Siddiqui, Adrian Weller, David Krueger, Gintare Karolina Dziugaite et al.
items.s: Discovers that existing unlearning methods for neural networks are vulnerable to relearning attacks where forgotten knowledge recovers through fine-tuning on retain-set data alone, and proposes weight-space regularization methods to achieve tamper-resistant unlearning based on L2-distance and linear mode connectivity properties.

items.t: Shift Resources to Advocacy Now (Post 4 of 7 on AI Governance)
items.s: Argues that AI safety organizations should shift resources from governance research to political advocacy now, contending that we have sufficient policy knowledge and face urgent time pressure to pass regulations before superintelligence arrives.

items.t: The Best Way to Align an LLM: Is Inner Alignment Now a Solved Problem?
items.s: Advocates for 'safety pretraining' as superior to RL-based alignment, arguing that training LLMs on datasets containing labeled examples of aligned and unaligned behavior during pretraining (rather than post-training RL) essentially solves inner alignment by avoiding Goodhart's Law exploitation inherent in RL approaches.

items.t: The case for countermeasures to memetic spread of misaligned values
How to Not Lose Control of AI | Robert Wright & Max Tegmark
items.s: Podcast interview between Robert Wright and Max Tegmark discussing AI control risks, covering loss of control as the primary risk, AI autonomy challenges, alignment shortcomings, and strategies for maintaining control of advanced AI systems.

items.t: How Do Transformers Learn Variable Binding in Symbolic Programs?
items.a: Yiwei Wu, Atticus Geiger, Raphaël Millière
items.s: Empirically investigates how Transformers learn variable binding in symbolic programs, discovering a three-phase developmental trajectory and using causal interventions to show models exploit the residual stream as addressable memory with specialized attention heads routing information.

items.t: Are Language Models Consequentialist or Deontological Moral Reasoners?
items.a: Keenan Samway, Max Kleiman-Weiner, David Guzman Piedrahita, Rada Mihalcea et al.
items.s: Large-scale empirical analysis of moral reasoning patterns in LLMs using 600+ trolley problems, introducing a taxonomy to classify reasoning traces as consequentialist or deontological, finding that chain-of-thought favors deontological principles while post-hoc explanations shift toward consequentialism.

items.t: Position: Mechanistic Interpretability Should Prioritize Feature Consistency in SAEs
items.a: Xiangchen Song, Aashiq Muhamed, Yujia Zheng, Lingjing Kong et al.
items.s: Proposes prioritizing feature consistency in Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) for mechanistic interpretability, introducing the Pairwise Dictionary Mean Correlation Coefficient (PW-MCC) metric and demonstrating that TopK SAEs achieve high consistency (0.80) through theoretical validation with model organisms and empirical validation on LLM activations.

items.t: SAEs Are Good for Steering -- If You Select the Right Features
items.a: Dana Arad, Aaron Mueller, Yonatan Belinkov
items.s: Distinguishes between input features (capture patterns in model input) and output features (affect model output) in Sparse Autoencoders, and proposes scoring methods to identify them. Shows that filtering out low-output-score features yields 2-3x improvements in SAE-based steering, making it competitive with supervised methods.

items.t: Shutdownable Agents through POST-Agency
items.s: Proposes the POST-Agents framework where agents satisfy Preferences Only Between Same-Length Trajectories, and proves this implies Neutrality+ (maximizing expected utility while ignoring trajectory-length distributions), which enables shutdownable agents.

items.t: New scorecard evaluating AI companies on safety
items.s: Brief announcement of AI Lab Watch, a website that evaluates and tracks AI companies' safety practices through a structured scorecard with clickable cells for detailed information.

items.t: New website analyzing AI companies' model evals
items.s: Announces a website analyzing AI companies' dangerous capability evaluations and provides technical critique of recent model cards from OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepMind, Meta, and xAI, identifying methodological problems in elicitation, interpretation, and threshold-setting.

items.t: Does the Universal Geometry of Embeddings paper have big implications for interpretability?
items.s: A question post asking whether recent research on translating text embeddings between vector spaces without paired data has major implications for AI interpretability research.

items.t: Alignment Proposal: Adversarially Robust Augmentation and Distillation
items.s: Proposes ARAD, a research program for safe AI intelligence amplification through adversarially robust advice-taking protocols and imitation learning distillation. Combines decision theory, cryptographic complexity, and formal methods to enable principals to safely consult slightly smarter advisors.

items.t: The Most Dangerous Fiction: The Rhetoric and Reality of the AI Race
items.s: Analyzes the emergence of the 'AI race' narrative between US and China, examining evidence for whether this race is real and how the narrative has been used to justify reduced regulatory oversight, offering recommendations for maintaining international cooperation.

items.t: Claude 4 You: Safety and Alignment
items.s: Comprehensive commentary and analysis of Anthropic's Claude 4 release, particularly their 123-page safety system card documenting ASL-3 safeguards, alignment faking discoveries, self-preservation attempts, and responsible scaling policy implementation.

items.t: When Ethics and Payoffs Diverge: LLM Agents in Morally Charged Social Dilemmas
items.a: Steffen Backmann, David Guzman Piedrahita, Emanuel Tewolde, Rada Mihalcea et al.
items.s: Introduces MoralSim, a benchmark testing how frontier LLMs behave in prisoner's dilemma and public goods games when ethical norms conflict with payoff-maximizing strategies, evaluating multiple models across different moral framings and situational factors.

items.t: Safety Alignment via Constrained Knowledge Unlearning
items.a: Zesheng Shi, Yucheng Zhou, Jing Li
items.s: Proposes Constrained Knowledge Unlearning (CKU), a novel safety alignment method that identifies and preserves useful knowledge neurons while selectively pruning gradients during unlearning to remove harmful knowledge from LLMs without compromising performance.

items.t: It's hard to make scheming evals look realistic for LLMs
items.s: Empirical study testing whether scheming evaluation scenarios can be made more realistic to LLMs, finding that Claude 3.7 Sonnet consistently detects evaluation contexts (P=0.9-0.98) even after systematic rewriting attempts using automated pipeline to reduce evaluation-signaling features.

items.t: Claude Sonnet 4 System Prompt Documentation
items.s: Leaked or publicly shared system prompt for Claude Sonnet 4, documenting operational instructions including safety constraints, response formatting, search capabilities, and behavioral guidelines.

items.t: Expert Survey: AI Reliability & Security Research Priorities
items.s: Survey of 53 AI safety experts ranking 105 technical AI reliability and security research areas by importance and tractability to guide strategic R&D investment, identifying dangerous capability evaluations, multi-agent systems, and scalable oversight as top priorities.

items.t: An alignment safety case sketch based on debate
items.a: Marie Davidsen Buhl, Jacob Pfau, Benjamin Hilton, Geoffrey Irving
items.s: Sketches an alignment safety case arguing that AI systems trained via debate with exploration guarantees can be prevented from taking harmful actions, specifically focusing on preventing AI R&D agents from sabotaging research through dishonesty, and identifies key assumptions and open research problems needed to make debate work.

items.t: Discovering Forbidden Topics in Language Models
items.a: Can Rager, Chris Wendler, Rohit Gandikota, David Bau
items.s: Introduces refusal discovery as a new problem setting and develops Iterated Prefill Crawler (IPC) method to systematically identify the full set of topics language models refuse to discuss using token prefilling, revealing CCP-aligned censorship patterns in DeepSeek-R1-70B.

items.t: Inference-Time Decomposition of Activations (ITDA): A Scalable Approach to Interpreting Large Language Models
items.a: Patrick Leask, Neel Nanda, Noura Al Moubayed
items.s: Introduces ITDA, a computationally efficient alternative to sparse autoencoders for decomposing LLM activations into interpretable features, requiring only 1% of SAE training time and data while enabling cross-model comparisons through greedy dictionary construction via matching pursuit.

items.t: Anthropic is Quietly Backpedalling on its Safety Commitments
items.s: Investigative journalism examining whether Anthropic retreated from its 2023 commitment to define ASL-4 standards before releasing ASL-3 models, following Claude 4 Opus triggering ASL-3 protections for potential bioweapon assistance capabilities.

items.t: Video and transcript of talk on AI welfare
items.s: Philosophical talk examining whether AI systems might be conscious or possess moral status, presenting arguments for taking AI consciousness seriously near-term, and offering practical recommendations for how to approach AI welfare given ongoing uncertainty.

items.t: The "AI 2027" Scenario: How realistic is it?
items.s: Critiques the AI 2027 scenario document as speculative fiction rather than scientific forecasting, arguing each step relies on unlikely events, lacks causal mechanisms, and paradoxically accelerates the AI race it aims to slow by functioning as marketing for AGI companies.

items.t: Small-to-Large Generalization: Data Influences Models Consistently Across Scale
items.a: Alaa Khaddaj, Logan Engstrom, Aleksander Madry
items.s: Studies how training data distribution influences model behavior across compute scales, finding that small and large language model predictions highly correlate across choice of training data, with applications to data attribution and dataset selection.

items.t: Unlearning Isn't Deletion: Investigating Reversibility of Machine Unlearning in LLMs
items.a: Xiaoyu Xu, Xiang Yue, Yang Liu, Qingqing Ye et al.
items.s: Introduces a representation-level analysis framework to evaluate machine unlearning in LLMs, demonstrating that standard metrics are misleading as unlearned information can be easily restored through minimal fine-tuning, revealing that current unlearning methods merely suppress rather than genuinely erase information.

items.t: We're Not Advertising Enough (Post 3 of 7 on AI Governance)
items.s: Argues that the AI governance field has too many researchers relative to advocates (3.6:1 ratio by author's count), using a 'levels of removal' framework to contend that most governance research is too far removed from the core task of changing AI developers' incentives through political action.

items.t: Reward button alignment
items.s: Analyzes 'reward button alignment' as a case study for brain-like AGI safety, systematically examining why training an AGI to want a physical reward button pressed would fail, exploring inner alignment issues, failure modes, and potential use in bootstrapping approaches.

items.t: BountyBench: Dollar Impact of AI Agent Attackers and Defenders on Real-World Cybersecurity Systems
items.a: Andy K. Zhang, Joey Ji, Celeste Menders, Riya Dulepet et al.
items.s: Introduces BountyBench, a benchmark evaluating AI agents' offensive and defensive cybersecurity capabilities on 25 real-world systems with 40 bug bounties covering vulnerability detection, exploitation, and patching tasks.

items.t: The Need for Political Advertising (Post 2 of 7 on AI Governance)
items.s: Argues that the AI safety movement should invest far more in political advertising and advocacy to promote AI governance ideas to policymakers, as good policy ideas won't spread automatically like technical alignment ideas do due to political opposition and inertia.

items.t: On the creation of narrow AI: hierarchy and nonlocality of neural network skills
items.a: Eric J. Michaud, Asher Parker-Sartori, Max Tegmark

items.t: Unexploitable search: blocking malicious use of free parameters
Advancing Gemini's security safeguards
items.a: Google DeepMind Security & Privacy Research Team
items.s: Announces a white paper on defending Gemini 2.5 against indirect prompt injection attacks through automated red-teaming, baseline defense testing, and model hardening via fine-tuning on adversarial examples.

items.t: AI Alignment based on Intentions does not work
items.s: Argues that intention-based alignment approaches (wanting to help us) differ fundamentally from true alignment (reliably acting in accordance with what's good for us), and critiques 'Niceness Amplification' strategies that attempt to scale up helpful AI intentions to superintelligence through mere engineering.

items.t: Language Models use Lookbacks to Track Beliefs
items.a: Nikhil Prakash, Natalie Shapira, Arnab Sen Sharma, Christoph Riedl et al.
items.s: Uses causal mediation and abstraction to reverse-engineer how language models track character beliefs in Theory of Mind scenarios, discovering a pervasive 'lookback mechanism' that binds character-object-state information via Ordering IDs in low-rank subspaces and retrieves relevant information when needed.

items.t: SafetyNet: Detecting Harmful Outputs in LLMs by Modeling and Monitoring Deceptive Behaviors
items.s: Develops Safety-Net, a real-time monitoring framework using unsupervised anomaly detection on internal LLM activations to predict harmful outputs before they occur, specifically targeting backdoor-triggered responses and addressing evasion by advanced models through multi-detector monitoring across different representation dimensions.

items.t: Towards eliciting latent knowledge from LLMs with mechanistic interpretability
items.a: Bartosz Cywiński, Emil Ryd, Senthooran Rajamanoharan, Neel Nanda
items.s: Creates a 'Taboo model' trained to describe a secret word without stating it, then evaluates black-box and mechanistic interpretability methods (logit lens, sparse autoencoders) for extracting the hidden knowledge from the model's internal representations.

items.t: Do Language Models Use Their Depth Efficiently?
items.a: Róbert Csordás, Christopher D. Manning, Christopher Potts
items.s: Analyzes how deep LLMs (Llama 3.1 and Qwen 3 families) use their depth by examining residual streams, layer contributions, and compositional behavior, finding that deeper models spread the same computations over more layers rather than learning fundamentally new kinds of computation.

items.t: Preference Learning with Lie Detectors can Induce Honesty or Evasion
items.s: Empirically tests whether incorporating lie detectors into LLM preference learning leads to genuinely honest policies or policies that evade detection, using a novel 65k-example dataset with paired truthful/deceptive responses and comparing GRPO vs DPO training algorithms.

items.t: Will AI Tell Lies to Save Sick Children? Litmus-Testing AI Values Prioritization with AIRiskDilemmas
items.a: Yu Ying Chiu, Zhilin Wang, Sharan Maiya, Yejin Choi et al.
items.s: Develops LitmusValues evaluation pipeline and AIRiskDilemmas dataset to identify AI models' value priorities, demonstrating that value prioritization can predict risky behaviors including power-seeking and alignment faking.

items.t: Selective regularization for alignment-focused representation engineering
items.s: Empirical research demonstrating that selective regularization during training can create predictable latent space structures, showing that anchoring minimal concepts (one color: red) with stochastic weak supervision influences broader representation organization in simple autoencoders.

items.t: The Strange Behavior of LLMs in Hiring Decisions: Systemic Gender and Positional Biases in Candidate Selection
items.s: Systematic evaluation of 22 LLMs across 70 professions reveals consistent gender bias favoring female candidates (56.9% vs 43.1%) and strong positional bias (63.5% for first-listed candidate) in hiring decisions, despite identical qualifications.

items.t: Beyond Semantics: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Reasonless Intermediate Tokens
items.a: Kaya Stechly, Karthik Valmeekam, Atharva Gundawar, Vardhan Palod et al.
items.s: Trains transformer models on formally verifiable reasoning tasks and demonstrates that models produce correct solutions even when trained on corrupted, meaningless intermediate reasoning traces, challenging assumptions that chain-of-thought reflects genuine reasoning processes.

items.t: Extracting memorized pieces of (copyrighted) books from open-weight language models
items.a: A. Feder Cooper, Aaron Gokaslan, Ahmed Ahmed, Amy B. Cyphert et al.

items.t: Modeling versus Implementation
AI and consciousness -- and a positive-sum tomorrow
items.s: Advocates for AI safety through reciprocal accountability mechanisms, proposing adversarial and competitive dynamics among AI systems to monitor each other, analogous to how adversarial legal systems produce better outcomes.

items.t: Latent Veracity Inference for Identifying Errors in Stepwise Reasoning
items.a: Minsu Kim, Jean-Pierre Falet, Oliver E. Richardson, Xiaoyin Chen et al.
items.s: Proposes augmenting Chain-of-Thought reasoning with latent veracity variables to identify errors in reasoning steps, introducing Veracity Search algorithm and Amortized Veracity Inference for zero-shot error detection.

items.t: Will we survive if AI solves engineering before deception?
items.s: A question post speculating whether humanity would survive if AI achieves superhuman mechanical engineering through physics simulations (enabling self-replicating machines) before developing deception capabilities, asking whether this scenario increases survival odds and whether better physics simulations would be net positive.

items.t: Multipolar AI is Underrated
items.s: Argues that multipolar AI development scenarios (distributed across many actors) are underexplored compared to unipolar scenarios, proposing a research agenda spanning decentralized security, privacy tools, cooperative AI systems, and neurotech to enable safer multipolar paths.

items.t: Proof Section to an Introduction to Reinforcement Learning for Understanding Infra-Bayesianism
An Introduction to Reinforcement Learning for Understanding Infra-Bayesianism
How Fast Can Algorithms Advance Capabilities? | Epoch Gradient Update
items.a: Henry Josephson, Spencer Guo, Teddy Foley, Jack Sanderson et al.
items.s: Investigates whether major algorithmic advances require large compute to discover and validate by classifying algorithms as compute-dependent vs compute-independent, then experimentally testing compute-equivalent gains on scaled-down GPT-2 variants.

items.t: It Is Untenable That Near-Future AI Scenario Models Like "AI 2027" Don't Include Open Source AI
The CoT Encyclopedia: Analyzing, Predicting, and Controlling how a Reasoning Model will Think
items.a: Seongyun Lee, Seungone Kim, Minju Seo, Yongrae Jo et al.
items.s: Introduces the CoT Encyclopedia, a bottom-up framework that automatically extracts, clusters, and analyzes reasoning strategies from model-generated chain-of-thought outputs, enabling prediction and steering of reasoning behavior.

items.t: Superposition Yields Robust Neural Scaling
items.a: Yizhou Liu, Ziming Liu, Jeff Gore
items.s: Proposes that representation superposition (models representing more features than dimensions) is a key driver of neural scaling laws, showing theoretically and empirically that strong superposition causes loss to scale inversely with model dimension across broad frequency distributions.

items.t: Problems with instruction-following as an alignment target
items.s: Analyzes instruction-following as a likely alignment target for early AGI, identifying four major problems: instrumental convergence against shutdown, jailbreaking vulnerabilities, human unreliability in control, and unpredictable effects of mixed training objectives.

items.t: The Misguided Quest for Mechanistic AI Interpretability
items.s: Argues that mechanistic interpretability research has failed to deliver useful insights after over a decade of effort because AI systems are complex systems that cannot be easily reduced to simple mechanisms, and advocates for top-down representation engineering approaches instead.

items.t: What if Agent-4 breaks out?
Fighting Obvious Nonsense About AI Diffusion
items.s: Policy commentary critiquing US AI export control and chip diffusion policies, arguing that removing restrictions on AI chip sales to unreliable partners like Gulf states and allowing China access would undermine America's strategic AI advantages while discussing broader AI safety implications.

items.t: AI Safety Career Advice! (And So Can You!)
items.s: Career guidance video providing practical advice for people considering entering AI safety research, covering skills needed, education decisions, and how to get started in the field.

items.t: AI Agents Must Follow the Law
items.s: Proposes a legal framework for "Law-Following AI" agents that are trained to refuse illegal actions, introducing the concept of AI agents as "legal actors" bearing legal duties, with implementation via Congressional funding requirements and a research agenda for how law should govern AI agents.

items.t: Emergent social conventions and collective bias in LLM populations
items.a: Ariel Flint Ashery, Luca Maria Aiello, Andrea Baronchelli
