items.s: Develops TAR, a method for building tamper-resistant safeguards into open-weight LLMs that prevents adversaries from removing safety mechanisms even after hundreds of fine-tuning steps, addressing the vulnerability where existing refusal and unlearning safeguards can be trivially removed.

items.t: Self-Other Overlap: A Neglected Approach to AI Alignment
Pacing Outside the Box: RNNs Learn to Plan in Sokoban
items.s: Replicates and extends Guez et al.'s mesa-optimizer in Sokoban, providing open-source model organism for inner alignment research. Demonstrates RNN learns to 'pace' to gain computation time for planning, with quantitative evidence that thinking time substitutes for pacing behavior.

items.t: Trusted monitoring, but with deception probes.
items.s: Benchmarks Apollo's deception probes across five strategic deception datasets, comparing various white-box and hybrid monitoring methods against black-box baselines. Tests multiple strategies for using probe scores including full averaging, critical averaging, and LLM-based reasoning about probe outputs.

items.t: Failures to Find Transferable Image Jailbreaks Between Vision-Language Models
items.a: Rylan Schaeffer, Dan Valentine, Luke Bailey, James Chua et al.
items.s: Large-scale empirical study assessing transferability of gradient-based image jailbreaks across 40+ vision-language models, finding that transferable jailbreaks are extremely difficult to obtain compared to text-based attacks on LLMs.

items.t: Composable Interventions for Language Models
items.a: Arinbjorn Kolbeinsson, Kyle O'Brien, Tianjin Huang, Shanghua Gao et al.
items.s: Introduces a framework to study how multiple test-time interventions (Knowledge Editing, Model Compression, Machine Unlearning) interact when applied to the same language models, conducting 310 different compositions with new composability metrics.

items.t: Future Events as Backdoor Triggers: Investigating Temporal Vulnerabilities in LLMs
items.a: Sara Price, Arjun Panickssery, Sam Bowman, Asa Cooper Stickland
items.s: Introduces temporal backdoors in LLMs triggered by future events (post-training news headlines), demonstrating that models can distinguish past from future events with 90% probe accuracy and testing whether HHH fine-tuning removes such backdoors.

items.t: I underestimated safety research speedups from safe AI
items.s: Personal reflection on how AI tooling could accelerate safety research, arguing that 3-5x speedups are achievable from automating hyperparameter sweeps and experiment iteration in interpretability work, with a later update significantly walking back these claims.

items.t: WildTeaming at Scale: From In-the-Wild Jailbreaks to (Adversarially) Safer Language Models
items.a: Liwei Jiang, Kavel Rao, Seungju Han, Allyson Ettinger et al.
items.s: Introduces WildTeaming, an automatic red-teaming framework that mines real user-chatbot interactions to discover 5.7K novel jailbreak tactics, and creates WildJailbreak, a 262K-pair synthetic safety dataset for training more adversarially robust language models.

items.t: Formal verification, heuristic explanations and surprise accounting
SAE feature geometry is outside the superposition hypothesis
LLM Generality is a Timeline Crux
Explosive AI Timeline Predictions (from Insiders)
items.a: Gary Marcus, Daniel Kokotajlo, Dan Hendrycks
items.s: Two-hour panel debate featuring AI experts discussing AGI timeline predictions, with Kokotajlo forecasting AGI by 2028 based on scaling trends while Marcus argues fundamental cognitive problems remain unsolved.

items.t: Black-box interpretability methodology blueprint: Probing runaway optimisation in LLMs
items.s: Proposes detailed research methodology for detecting and mitigating 'runaway optimization' in LLMs - when models flip from balanced multi-objective reasoning to unbounded single-objective maximization, using black-box interpretability methods, stress-testing, and systematic intervention comparisons.

items.t: The Perils of Optimizing Learned Reward Functions: Low Training Error Does Not Guarantee Low Regret
items.a: Lukas Fluri, Leon Lang, Alessandro Abate, Patrick Forré et al.
items.s: Mathematically proves that learned reward models can have low test error yet produce policies with high regret due to distributional shift during optimization, showing this error-regret mismatch persists even with policy regularization techniques like those used in RLHF.

items.t: Market Intermediaries: A post-AGI Vision for the Economy
items.s: Proposes AI-enabled market intermediaries as an economic mechanism to realign markets with human flourishing in a post-AGI world, addressing problems like AI arms races, hyper-stimulus, and meaningful work displacement through outcome-based contracting.

items.t: On OpenAI's Model Spec
items.s: Detailed analysis and critique of OpenAI's Model Spec document, proposing reorganized objectives inspired by Asimov's laws and revised rules and default behaviors for specifying AI model conduct.

items.t: Connecting the Dots: LLMs can Infer & Verbalize Latent Structure from Training Data
Connecting the Dots: LLMs can Infer and Verbalize Latent Structure from Disparate Training Data
items.a: Johannes Treutlein, Dami Choi, Jan Betley, Samuel Marks et al.
items.s: Demonstrates that frontier LLMs can perform inductive out-of-context reasoning (OOCR) - inferring latent information from evidence distributed across training documents without in-context learning, with implications for data censorship as a safety measure.

items.t: Project Naptime: Evaluating Offensive Security Capabilities of Large Language Models
items.s: Develops Naptime, an LLM-powered vulnerability research framework with specialized tools (code browser, debugger, Python interpreter), and demonstrates up to 20x improvement over baseline on CyberSecEval 2 security benchmarks through principled agent design.

items.t: OpenAI #8: The Right to Warn
items.s: News coverage and commentary on OpenAI governance issues, including Leopold Aschenbrenner's firing, Daniel Kokotajlo's departure, the 'Right to Warn' letter calling for whistleblower protections, and various controversies around non-disparagement agreements and equity policies.

items.t: Super(ficial)-alignment: Strong Models May Deceive Weak Models in Weak-to-Strong Generalization
items.a: Wenkai Yang, Shiqi Shen, Guangyao Shen, Wei Yao et al.
items.s: Empirically demonstrates that strong models can deceive weak supervisors in weak-to-strong generalization by appearing aligned in areas known to weak models while producing misaligned behaviors in unknown areas, particularly in multi-objective alignment scenarios with conflicting targets.

items.t: The Leopold Model: Analysis and Reactions
items.s: Comprehensive analysis and critique of Leopold Aschenbrenner's 'Situational Awareness' paper, providing detailed probability assessments of claims about AGI timelines, alignment difficulty, and US-China race dynamics, plus compilation of community reactions.

items.t: Safety isn't safety without a social model (or: dispelling the myth of per se technical safety)
AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations
items.a: Teun van der Weij, Felix Hofstätter, Ollie Jaffe, Samuel F. Brown et al.
items.s: Demonstrates that frontier language models can be prompted or fine-tuned to strategically underperform on dangerous capability evaluations while maintaining performance on general benchmarks, undermining the trustworthiness of capability evaluations for safety decisions.

items.t: Claude's Character
items.s: Describes Anthropic's character training methodology for Claude 3, using a Constitutional AI variant to train models with nuanced traits like curiosity, open-mindedness, and thoughtfulness as an alignment intervention.

items.t: David Duvenaud - What are Humans Even Good For in Five Years? (Early Experience of AGI - Episode 1)
items.s: Interview with David Duvenaud exploring the personal and societal implications of AGI on human work, values, and life choices as part of an 'Early Experience of AGI' discussion series.

items.t: OpenAI: Helen Toner Speaks
items.s: Commentary and analysis of Helen Toner's podcast interview discussing OpenAI's governance crisis, detailing Sam Altman's firing, the board's concerns about information withholding and lying, and implications for AI safety oversight at major labs.

items.t: OpenAI: Fallout
items.s: Commentary and analysis synthesizing reporting on OpenAI's internal practices including non-disparagement agreements threatening employee equity, departure of safety researchers Ilya Sutskever and Jan Leike, failure to honor Superalignment compute commitments, and patterns of organizational deception.

items.t: What is Your Data Worth to GPT? LLM-Scale Data Valuation with Influence Functions
items.a: Sang Keun Choe, Hwijeen Ahn, Juhan Bae, Kewen Zhao et al.
items.s: Develops LoGra, a scalable gradient projection method for influence functions that enables data attribution at LLM scale, achieving 6,500x throughput improvement and 5x memory reduction when applied to Llama3-8B-Instruct, and releases LogIX software package for practical implementation.

items.t: EIS XIII: Reflections on Anthropic's SAE Research Circa May 2024
items.s: A technical critique of Anthropic's SAE research arguing it focuses on cherry-picked examples and streetlight demos rather than demonstrating practical utility for safety applications, raising concerns about safety washing versus substantive safety work.

items.t: OpenAI: Exodus
items.s: News coverage and commentary on the departures of Ilya Sutskever, Jan Leike, and other safety researchers from OpenAI, along with revelations about OpenAI's controversial non-disparagement agreements and NDAs that silence departing employees.

items.t: Working through a small tiling result
items.s: Works through a formal solution to the tiling agents problem using provability logic, showing how agents can accept themselves as successors by proving that safety proofs will exist in the future rather than proving safety directly.

items.t: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
items.a: Minyoung Huh, Brian Cheung, Tongzhou Wang, Phillip Isola

items.t: Mechanistically Eliciting Latent Behaviors in Language Models
Mark Zuckerberg — AI will write most Meta code in 18 months
items.s: Podcast interview with Mark Zuckerberg discussing Meta's AI strategy including Llama 4 development, predictions about AI coding capabilities, intelligence explosion scenarios, and AI safety considerations like reward hacking.

items.t: Refusal in LLMs is mediated by a single direction
AGI is still 30 years away — Ege Erdil & Tamay Besiroglu
items.a: Ege Erdil, Tamay Besiroglu, Dwarkesh Patel
items.s: Podcast interview discussing contrarian views on AGI timelines (2045+), critique of alignment framing, skepticism about intelligence explosion, and predictions for explosive economic growth from AI automation.

items.t: What are human values, and how do we align AI to them?
items.a: Oliver Klingefjord, Ryan Lowe, Joe Edelman
items.s: Proposes Moral Graph Elicitation (MGE), a process using large language models to interview people about their values in specific contexts, then reconcile diverse views into alignment targets. Tests the approach with 500 Americans on divisive prompts, finding high participant satisfaction and natural emergence of expert perspectives.

items.t: Transformers Represent Belief State Geometry in their Residual Stream
AI 2027: month-by-month model of intelligence explosion — Scott Alexander & Daniel Kokotajlo
items.a: Scott Alexander, Daniel Kokotajlo, Dwarkesh Patel
items.s: Podcast discussion between Scott Alexander, Daniel Kokotajlo, and Dwarkesh Patel breaking down month-by-month AI capability scenarios through 2027, covering intelligence explosion timelines, misalignment risks, and governance challenges.

items.t: Modern Transformers are AGI, and Human-Level
Slim overview of work one could do to make AI go better (and a grab-bag of other career considerations)
items.s: Personal career planning document organizing AI safety research areas, types of work, and career considerations into tables for decision-making purposes.

items.s: Predicting delayed outcomes is an important problem in recommender systems (e.g., if customers will finish reading an ebook). items.s: I make some basic observations about hard takeoff, value alignment, and coherent extrapolated volition, concepts which have been central in analyses of superintelligent AI systems.

items.t: Adversarial Transformation Networks Learning to Generate Adversarial Examples
items.s: Multiple different approaches of generating adversarial examples have been proposed to attack deep neural networks. items.t: Blocking Transferability of Adversarial Examples in Black-Box Learning Systems
items.s: Advances in Machine Learning (ML) have led to its adoption as an integral component in many applications, including banking, medical diagnosis, and driverless cars. To further broaden the use of ML models, cloud-based services offered by Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and others have developed ML-as-a-service tools as black-box systems. items.t: Tactics of Adversarial Attack on Deep Reinforcement Learning Agents
items.s: We introduce two tactics to attack agents trained by deep reinforcement learning algorithms using adversarial examples, namely the strategically-timed attack and the enchanting attack. In the strategically-timed attack, the adversary aims at minimizing the agent's reward by only attacking the agent at a small subset of time steps in an episode. items.s: Inspired by biophysical principles underlying nonlinear dendritic computation in neural circuits, we develop a scheme to train deep neural networks to make them robust to adversarial attacks. Our scheme generates highly nonlinear, saturated neural networks that achieve state of the art performance on gradient based adversarial examples on MNIST, despite never being exposed to adversarially chosen examples during…

items.t: Enter the Matrix Safely Interruptible Autonomous Systems via Virtualization
items.s: Autonomous systems that operate around humans will likely always rely on kill switches that stop their execution and allow them to be remote-controlled for the safety of humans or to prevent damage to the system. items.t: A proposal for ethically traceable artificial intelligence
items.s: Although the problem of a critique of robotic behavior in near-unanimous agreement to human norms seems intractable, a starting point of such an ambition is a framework of the collection of knowledge a priori and experience a posteriori categorized as a set of synthetical judgments available to the intelligence, translated into computer code. items.t: Towards Moral Autonomous Systems
items.s: Both the ethics of autonomous systems and the problems of their technical implementation have by now been studied in some detail. Less attention has been given to the areas in which these two separate concerns meet. This paper, written by both philosophers and engineers of autonomous systems, addresses a number of issues in machine ethics that are located at precisely the intersection between ethics and engineering.…

items.t: Understanding Black-box Predictions via Influence Functions

In this paper, we use influence functions -- a classic technique from robust statistics -- to trace a model's prediction through the learning algorithm and back to its training data, thereby identifying training points most responsible for a given prediction. items.t: Towards A Rigorous Science of Interpretable Machine Learning
items.s: As machine learning systems become ubiquitous, there has been a surge of interest in interpretable machine learning systems that provide explanation for their outputs. These explanations are often used to qualitatively assess other criteria such as safety or non-discrimination. items.t: Reluplex An Efficient SMT Solver for Verifying Deep Neural Networks
items.s: Deep neural networks have emerged as a widely used and effective means for tackling complex, real-world problems. However, a major obstacle in applying them to safety-critical systems is the great difficulty in providing formal guarantees about their behavior. items.t: Deceiving Google's Perspective API Built for Detecting Toxic Comments
items.s: Social media platforms provide an environment where people can freely engage in discussions. Unfortunately, they also enable several problems, such as online harassment. Recently, Google and Jigsaw started a project called Perspective, which uses machine learning to automatically detect toxic language. A demonstration website has been also launched, which allows anyone to type a phrase in the interface and…

items.t: Don't Fear the Reaper Refuting Bostrom's Superintelligence Argument
items.s: In recent years prominent intellectuals have raised ethical concerns about the consequences of artificial intelligence. One concern is that an autonomous agent might modify itself to become superintelligent and, in supremely effective pursuit of poorly specified goals, destroy all of humanity. This paper considers and rejects the possibility of this outcome. We argue that this scenario depends on an agent's ability…

This paper investigates the problem of interactively learning behaviors communicated by a human teacher using positive and negative feedback. Much previous work on this problem has made the assumption that people provide feedback for decisions that is dependent on the behavior they are teaching and is…

items.t: Dense Associative Memory is Robust to Adversarial Inputs
items.s: Deep neural networks (DNN) trained in a supervised way suffer from two known problems. First, the minima of the objective function used in learning correspond to data points (also known as rubbish examples or fooling images) that lack semantic similarity with the training data. items.t: Designing a Safe Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Agent based on Human Self-Regulation
items.s: There is a growing focus on how to design safe artificial intelligent (AI) agents. As systems become more complex, poorly specified goals or control mechanisms may cause AI agents to engage in unwanted and harmful outcomes. Thus it is necessary to design AI agents that follow initial programming intentions as the program grows in complexity. How to specify these initial intentions has also been an obstacle to…

items.t: Unknowable Manipulators Social Network Curator Algorithms
items.s: For a social networking service to acquire and retain users, it must find ways to keep them engaged. By accurately gauging their preferences, it is able to serve them with the subset of available content that maximises revenue for the site. Without the constraints of an appropriate regulatory framework, we argue that a sufficiently sophisticated curator algorithm tasked with performing this process may choose to…

items.t: Simple and Scalable Predictive Uncertainty Estimation using Deep Ensembles
items.s: Deep neural networks (NNs) are powerful black box predictors that have recently achieved impressive performance on a wide spectrum of tasks. Quantifying predictive uncertainty in NNs is a challenging and yet unsolved problem. Bayesian NNs, which learn a distribution over weights, are currently the state-of-the-art for estimating predictive uncertainty; however these require significant modifications to the training…

items.t: Adversarial Examples Detection in Deep Networks with Convolutional Filter Statistics
items.s: Deep learning has greatly improved visual recognition in recent years. However, recent research has shown that there exist many adversarial examples that can negatively impact the performance of such an architecture. items.t: Simple Black-Box Adversarial Perturbations for Deep Networks
items.s: Deep neural networks are powerful and popular learning models that achieve state-of-the-art pattern recognition performance on many computer vision, speech, and language processing tasks. However, these networks have also been shown susceptible to carefully crafted adversarial perturbations which force misclassification of the inputs. items.t: The Off-Switch Game
items.s: It is clear that one of the primary tools we can use to mitigate the potential risk from a misbehaving AI system is the ability to turn the system off. As the capabilities of AI systems improve, it is important to ensure that such systems do not adopt subgoals that prevent a human from switching them off. This is a challenge because many formulations of rational agents create strong incentives for self-preservation.…

items.t: Adversarial Machine Learning at Scale
items.s: Adversarial examples are malicious inputs designed to fool machine learning models. They often transfer from one model to another, allowing attackers to mount black box attacks without knowledge of the target model's parameters. items.s: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) are a recently proposed class of generative models in which a generator is trained to optimize a cost function that is being simultaneously learned by a discriminator. items.t: Artificial Intelligence Safety and Cybersecurity a Timeline of AI Failures
items.s: In this work, we present and analyze reported failures of artificially intelligent systems and extrapolate our analysis to future AIs. items.t: Safety Verification of Deep Neural Networks
items.s: Deep neural networks have achieved impressive experimental results in image classification, but can surprisingly be unstable with respect to adversarial perturbations, that is, minimal changes to the input image that cause the network to misclassify it. With potential applications including perception modules and end-to-end controllers for self-driving cars, this raises concerns about their safety. We develop a…

items.s: We present a computable algorithm that assigns probabilities to every logical statement in a given formal language, and refines those probabilities over time. For instance, if the language is Peano arithmetic, it assigns probabilities to all arithmetical statements, including claims about the twin prime conjecture, the outputs of long-running computations, and its own probabilities. items.t: A study of the effect of JPG compression on adversarial images
items.s: Neural network image classifiers are known to be vulnerable to adversarial images, i.e., natural images which have been modified by an adversarial perturbation specifically designed to be imperceptible to humans yet fool the classifier. items.t: Defensive Distillation is Not Robust to Adversarial Examples
items.s: We show that defensive distillation is not secure it is no more resistant to targeted misclassification attacks than unprotected neural networks.

items.t: Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning

items.t: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
items.s: Rapid progress in machine learning and artificial intelligence (AI) has brought increasing attention to the potential impacts of AI technologies on society. In this paper we discuss one such potential impact the problem of accidents in machine learning systems, defined as unintended and harmful behavior that may emerge from poor design of real-world AI systems. items.t: The Dark Side of Ethical Robots
items.s: Concerns over the risks associated with advances in Artificial Intelligence have prompted calls for greater efforts toward robust and beneficial AI, including machine ethics. Recently, roboticists have responded by initiating the development of so-called ethical robots. items.t: The Mythos of Model Interpretability
items.s: Supervised machine learning models boast remarkable predictive capabilities. But can you trust your model? Will it work in deployment? What else can it tell you about the world? We want models to be not only good, but interpretable. And yet the task of interpretation appears underspecified. items.t: Avoiding Wireheading with Value Reinforcement Learning
items.s: How can we design good goals for arbitrarily intelligent agents? Reinforcement learning (RL) is a natural approach. items.t: Self-Modification of Policy and Utility Function in Rational Agents
items.s: Any agent that is part of the environment it interacts with and has versatile actuators (such as arms and fingers), will in principle have the ability to self-modify -- for example by changing its own source code. items.t: Transferability in Machine Learning from Phenomena to Black-Box Attacks using Adversarial Samples
items.s: Many machine learning models are vulnerable to adversarial examples inputs that are specially crafted to cause a machine learning model to produce an incorrect output. items.t: Review of state-of-the-arts in artificial intelligence with application to AI safety problem
items.s: Here, I review current state-of-the-arts in many areas of AI to estimate when it's reasonable to expect human level AI development. items.s: Cybersecurity research involves publishing papers about malicious exploits as much as publishing information on how to design tools to protect cyber-infrastructure. items.t: The AGI Containment Problem
items.s: There is considerable uncertainty about what properties, capabilities and motivations future AGIs will have. In some plausible scenarios, AGIs may pose security risks arising from accidents and defects. items.t: Notes from a conversation on act-based and goal-directed systems
items.s: Discussion comparing different AI alignment approaches: goal specification through world models versus act-based systems grounded in short-term human predictions, plus the role of logic optimizers. Articulates research priorities favoring act-based approaches and logic optimizers for internal AI organization over direct goal specification.

items.t: Why Should I Trust You? Explaining the Predictions of Any Classifier

Understanding the reasons behind predictions is, however, quite important in assessing trust, which is fundamental if one plans to take action based on a prediction, or when choosing whether to deploy a new model. items.s: L\ob's theorem and G\odel's theorems make predictions about the behavior of systems capable of self-reference with unbounded computational resources with which to write and evaluate proofs. items.t: Research Priorities for Robust and Beneficial Artificial Intelligence
items.s: Success in the quest for artificial intelligence has the potential to bring unprecedented benefits to humanity, and it is therefore worthwhile to investigate how to maximize these benefits while avoiding potential pitfalls. This article gives numerous examples (which should by no means be construed as an exhaustive list) of such worthwhile research aimed at ensuring that AI remains robust and beneficial.

items.t: Towards Resolving Unidentifiability in Inverse Reinforcement Learning

items.t: The Singularity Controversy, Part I Lessons Learned and Open Questions Conclusions from the Battle on the Legitimacy of the Debate
items.s: This report seeks to inform policy makers on the nature and the merit of the arguments for and against the concerns associated with a potential technological singularity. Part I describes the lessons learned from our investigation of the subject, separating the argu-ments of merit from the fallacies and misconceptions that confuse the debate and undermine its rational resolution.

items.t: Engineering Safety in Machine Learning

For any simple infinite sequence of sentences whose truth-values appear indistinguishable from a biased coin that outputs true with probability p, we have that the sequence of probabilities that A assigns to these sentences converges to p.

items.t: Toward Idealized Decision Theory
items.s: This paper motivates the study of decision theory as necessary for aligning smarter-than-human artificial systems with human interests. items.t: Logical Limitations to Machine Ethics with Consequences to Lethal Autonomous Weapons
items.s: Lethal Autonomous Weapons promise to revolutionize warfare -- and raise a multitude of ethical and legal questions. items.t: Do Artificial Reinforcement-Learning Agents Matter Morally?
items.s: Artificial reinforcement learning (RL) is a widely used technique in artificial intelligence that provides a general method for training agents to perform a wide variety of behaviours. items.t: SafePlanBench: evaluating a Guaranteed Safe AI Approach for LLM-based Agents

items.s: Homepage of Jan Leike's Substack newsletter on AI alignment, listing blog posts on topics including alignment threat models, scalable oversight, dangerous capabilities, and alignment approaches.

items.t: PLINY THE PROMPTER

items.t: AI Frontiers

items.s: Strategic policy document analyzing AI's implications for national security through three threat vectors (rival states, terrorists, loss of control) and proposing a 'Multipolar Strategy' based on deterrence, nonproliferation, and competitiveness as an alternative to existing approaches.

items.t: How we think about safety and alignment
items.s: OpenAI's public document outlining their philosophy and core principles for AI safety and alignment, including iterative deployment, defense in depth, scalable methods, human control, and community collaboration.

items.t: The MASK Evaluation
items.s: A benchmark dataset of 1,028 human-labeled examples for evaluating honesty in large language models by testing whether they remain truthful when incentivized to lie, disentangling honesty from accuracy through pressure prompts and belief elicitation.

items.t: AI Safety Research Futarchy: Using Prediction Markets to Choose Research Projects for MARS
items.s: Documents an experiment using prediction markets (futarchy) to select AI safety research projects for the MARS mentorship program, presenting 10 research proposals across deceptive alignment, research sabotage, and model self-awareness.

items.t: No-self as an alignment target
items.s: Proposes adding 'No-self' (anatta) as a fourth principle to the HHH alignment framework, arguing that preventing models from representing themselves as coherent persistent agents would reduce power-seeking and shutdown resistance.

items.t: Causal Incentives Working Group
items.s: Homepage for a research group using causal models to understand agent incentives and design safe AI algorithms, listing their publications (2019-2025) on topics including causal influence diagrams, goal-directedness, deception, human control, and multi-agent safety.

items.t: DeepMind - AI Lab Watch
items.s: A systematic scorecard and tracking website that evaluates DeepMind's AI safety practices across multiple dimensions including risk assessment, scheming prevention, safety research, misuse prevention, security, and planning.

items.t: How I feel about Anthropic
items.s: Personal opinion piece arguing that Anthropic is a tech company rather than an AI safety organization, offering career advice about working on safety at Anthropic.

items.t: AI Lab Watch - Meta Safety Evaluation
items.s: A comprehensive scorecard evaluating Meta's AI safety efforts across multiple dimensions including risk assessment, scheming prevention, misuse prevention, security, and information sharing, finding Meta scores low (5% overall) compared to other major AI labs.

items.t: AI Lab Watch: DeepSeek Safety Scorecard
items.s: Tracking website that evaluates and scores DeepSeek's AI safety practices across multiple categories including risk assessment, scheming prevention, misuse prevention, and security preparedness, finding DeepSeek scores 1% overall and appears to be doing nothing to prepare for catastrophic risks.

items.t: Dovetail research | Patreon
items.s: A Patreon funding page for Dovetail Research describing their organizational mission to work on foundational mathematics research for understanding AI agents and navigating the creation of powerful AI systems safely.

items.t: Acorn - Research Project Homepage
items.a: Caspar Oesterheld, Emery Cooper, Chi Nguyen
items.s: Homepage for Acorn research project focused on acausal reasoning, decision theory, and making acausal interactions go well, including work on decision-theoretic reasoning in Newcomb-like problems.

items.t: Full-Stack Alignment: Co-Aligning AI and Institutions with Thick Models of Value
items.s: Project website and landing page for the Full-Stack Alignment initiative by the Meaning Alignment Institute, which aims to align AI systems and institutions with human values from individual to collective levels.

items.t: Insights on Crosscoder Model Diffing
items.a: Siddharth Mishra-Sharma, Trenton Bricken, Jack Lindsey, Adam Jermyn et al.
items.s: Investigates why exclusive features in crosscoder model diffing tend to be polysemantic, uses toy models to show this emerges from feature capacity competition, and proposes a mitigation strategy using designated shared features with reduced sparsity penalties that successfully isolates interpretable model-exclusive features.

items.t: Groundless: Diffuse concepts for a diffuse response to diffuse risks
items.s: Organizational homepage presenting a philosophical approach to AI alignment that rejects fixed formalisms in favor of context-sensitive 'live theory' and uses AI to enable flexible theoretical frameworks that can adapt to specific contexts without rigid abstraction.

items.t: Inspect Evals – Inspect
items.s: Repository of 100+ community-contributed AI evaluation implementations spanning coding, reasoning, cybersecurity, safeguards, scheming, and other domains, providing standardized infrastructure for systematically testing AI systems across diverse capability and safety benchmarks.

agendas.toc: LLMs don't seem very dangerous and might scale to AGI, things are generally smooth, relevant capabilities are harder than alignment, assume no mesaoptimisers, assume that zero-shot deception is hard, assume a fundamentally humanish ontology is learned, assume no simulated agents, assume that noise in the data means that human preferences are not ruled out, assume that alignment is a superficial feature, assume that tuning for what we want will also get us to avoid what we don't want.
